We're tied with Mike Rogers in the newest polling. Trump's handpicked
candidate, a 30-year career politician with over a year of spending and

Tied. With a few weeks left, in one of the seats that decides control of
the United States Senate.

I'm not going to dress that up. I have never taken a dime of corporate PAC
money, and I never will. I won the primary without a single dollar from
AIPAC, and that hasn't changed and won't change in the general. I'm not

Money out of politics. Money in your pocket. Medicare for All. That
platform just won the most expensive Democratic Senate primary in the
country's history. Now it has to win in November, and it wins the same way
it won in August: one dollar, one door, one person at a time.

In solidarity,

Abdul

---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

**CONCORD, N.H. —** New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie released the following statement following John E. Sununu’s Republican primary victory for U.S. Senate:“I would like to congratulate John E. Sununu on his primary victory for the U.S. Senate. John is exactly the candidate we need to take on Chris Pappas and fight for Granite Staters in the United States Senate,” **said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie.** “Chris Pappas is a do-nothing politician looking for a six-year promotion after spending the last seven years in Congress with little to show for it. Granite Staters deserve a Senator who will put New Hampshire first, deliver results, and bring the New Hampshire Advantage to Washington. John E. Sununu has the experience and determination to get the job done, and I look forward to working with him to defeat Chris Pappas and send him packing in November.”

subject: I’m officially the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate here in New Hampshire
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
We need to start this general election on the right foot.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8796%2E582294%2EZ-7Dqb)
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260908_4.Rv6I5a&refcode=em20260908-4&t=2&akid=8796%2E582294%2EZ-7Dqb)
Hi, it’s Chris Pappas.
**It’s official: I am the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate here in New Hampshire.**
I’m grateful to every Granite Stater who put their trust in me and helped build this campaign together.
Growing up in Manchester and working alongside my family at our restaurant, I learned that you don’t get ahead just by making promises. You have to be accountable. You listen to people, work hard, and deliver.
That’s the same approach I’ve brought to Congress, and it’s why I’m running for the Senate.
I’m running to make New Hampshire more affordable for working families; protect Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid; safeguard reproductive freedom; and stand up for the small businesses that are the backbone of our communities.
**And now our general election fight against John Sununu officially begins.**
Political experts just changed this race to a Toss-up. The fact is: New Hampshire is a fiercely independent state, and this election could go either way. The country is watching, and the outcome here in New Hampshire will determine control of the U.S. Senate and what the next two years look like for millions of families across the country.
**[We are running a grassroots-powered campaign fueled by people like you. We need all hands on deck in order to keep New Hampshire blue and flip the Senate. Will you step up with $5 or whatever you can spare to boost our campaign as we enter the general election?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260908_4.Rv6I5a&refcode=em20260908-4&t=3&akid=8796%2E582294%2EZ-7Dqb)**
**[CHIP IN TO KEEP NH BLUE »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260908_4.Rv6I5a&refcode=em20260908-4&t=4&akid=8796%2E582294%2EZ-7Dqb)**
John Sununu has spent his career putting Washington and corporate special interests ahead of Granite Staters. While he was in Congress, he voted to give tax breaks to Big Pharma and Big Oil, and now he’s profiting off of investments in those same industries.
As we speak, national Republicans and dark-money groups are spending millions to put him back in the Senate because they know he’ll do the bidding of Trump and corporate interests, not look out for the people of New Hampshire.
**This race is a Toss-up, so we need to join together right now and stay focused over the next eight weeks.**
**[Will you chip in a $5 contribution right now to help us hit the ground running to keep this seat blue?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260908_4.Rv6I5a&refcode=em20260908-4&t=5&akid=8796%2E582294%2EZ-7Dqb)**

When you love New Hampshire, you don’t just talk about what makes this state special. You stand up and fight for the people who call it home.
Thank you for everything,
Chris Pappas

_**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### On Sunday, the president of the United States posted an image of himself on a black throne surrounded by fire, announced that the Moon belongs to us, and suggested we rename New Mexico. I know. You have seen the screenshots, you have made the joke, and you have moved on, because that is what we all do now.
##### Here is why you should not move on. David Shuster spent this week on the part nobody screenshotted: earlier this year, during a mission to rescue a downed American pilot in Iran, Trump's own Cabinet and his own generals decided the commander in chief could not be in the Situation Room. Not would not. Could not. They ran the operation around him because they believed his presence would get Americans killed.
##### That is not a meme. That is the 25th Amendment's exact premise, already acted on in secret by the people who took an oath alongside him. David lays out what Section 4 actually requires, why it has never been used this way, and what Congress owes the country before the midterms.
##### This is the reporting we can do because you pay for it--no advertisers to spook, no network lawyers, no anchor telling us to be careful. [If you are reading Blue Amp free, this is the week to fix that. * * *
_**by David Shuster**_
There have been countless moments over the past ten years when Donald Trump's bizarre social media posts indicated something with him is very wrong. Sunday now stands at the top of the list.
The President of the United States, who has at his disposal the Army, the Navy, the Air Force, the nuclear arsenal, and endless stationery bearing the presidential seal, spent much of the day engaged in an unhinged digital freak show. The performance included AI fantasies, geopolitical doodling, self-coronation and, for good measure, a declaration that the Moon belongs to the United States.
Trump unleashed dozens of posts, including images of himself surrounded by giant robots with glowing eyes and ominous captions.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1c8cda55-bc9e-49eb-aa7b-8af3b8a6c545?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In one, he appeared amid a dystopian landscape beneath the words "THEY WILL NEVER SLEEP AGAIN." In another, he sat upon a black throne amid fire, ruins and mechanical giants.
Then came the cartography.
New Mexico, which survived centuries of Spanish rule, Mexican sovereignty, American conquest and statehood, was invited to undergo another administrative reincarnation. Trump suggested that it be renamed "New America," a proposal accompanied by an AI-crafted image.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.ZTytFWJGJCmBs9caZPGzqfPk6Zj3T3ez1PxT5cC3U28?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214595161)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1c8cda55-bc9e-49eb-aa7b-8af3b8a6c545?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The President has no authority simply to rename a state, but constitutional limitations have never been of any concern to Trump.
Then came the Moon.
Trump posted an image of it floating serenely above the Earth, decorated with an American flag and the majestic announcement: "THE MOON IS OURS." The post was archived at 1:56 p.m. Sunday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1c8cda55-bc9e-49eb-aa7b-8af3b8a6c545?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
One might conclude that the Presidency now belongs to an exceptionally excitable 12 year old with access to an image generator. However, there were more serious items in the President's bizarre and demeaning performance.
Trump shared an image depicting Iran's territory reshaped in the outline of his own face, and another suggesting the destruction of Kharg Island.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1c8cda55-bc9e-49eb-aa7b-8af3b8a6c545?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
He also boasted that he had made "Hundreds of Billions of Dollars" from stocks and other holdings while asserting that he did it for the country rather than himself.
Most Americans, confronted with this lunatic spectacle, might ask a very old-fashioned question: Is the President capable of doing the job?
This is where the Twenty-Fifth Amendment enters the equation. The amendment does not provide a constitutional trapdoor to remove presidents who take actions that are offensive, foolish, vulgar, or ridiculous. Section 4 establishes a procedure under which the vice president and a majority of the Cabinet can declare that the President is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office. If the President contests this declaration, the issue goes to Congress where two thirds vote in both houses would be necessary to keep the President from resuming his powers.
This is an exceptionally challenging threshold, and perhaps deservedly so.
A U.S. President does not become constitutionally incapacitated because he or she posts a silly picture, or two, or twenty.

On Sunday he posted that the Moon is ours. | | and | Sep 8| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Cliff 's Note: On Sunday, the president of the United States posted an image of himself on a black throne surrounded by fire, announced that the Moon belongs to us, and suggested we rename New Mexico. I know. You have seen the screenshots, you have made the joke, and you have moved on, because that is what we all do now. Here is why you should not move on. David Shuster spent this week on the part nobody screenshotted: earlier this year, during a mission to rescue a downed American pilot in Iran, Trump's own Cabinet and his own generals decided the commander in chief could not be in the Situation Room. Not would not. Could not. They ran the operation around him because they believed his presence would get Americans killed. That is not a meme. That is the 25th Amendment's exact premise, already acted on in secret by the people who took an oath alongside him. David lays out what Section 4 actually requires, why it has never been used this way, and what Congress owes the country before the midterms. This is the reporting we can do because you pay for it--no advertisers to spook, no network lawyers, no anchor telling us to be careful. -- Cliff by David Shuster** There have been countless moments over the past ten years when Donald Trump's bizarre social media posts indicated something with him is very wrong. Sunday now stands at the top of the list. The President of the United States, who has at his disposal the Army, the Navy, the Air Force, the nuclear arsenal, and endless stationery bearing the presidential seal, spent much of the day engaged in an unhinged digital freak show. The performance included AI fantasies, geopolitical doodling, self-coronation and, for good measure, a declaration that the Moon belongs to the United States. Trump unleashed dozens of posts, including images of himself surrounded by giant robots with glowing eyes and ominous captions. | | ---|---|--- In one, he appeared amid a dystopian landscape beneath the words "THEY WILL NEVER SLEEP AGAIN." In another, he sat upon a black throne amid fire, ruins and mechanical giants. Then came the cartography. New Mexico, which survived centuries of Spanish rule, Mexican sovereignty, American conquest and statehood, was invited to undergo another administrative reincarnation. Trump suggested that it be renamed "New America," a proposal accompanied by an AI-crafted image. | | ---|---|--- The President has no authority simply to rename a state, but constitutional limitations have never been of any concern to Trump. Then came the Moon. Trump posted an image of it floating serenely above the Earth, decorated with an American flag and the majestic announcement: "THE MOON IS OURS." The post was archived at 1:56 p.m. Sunday. | | ---|---|--- One might conclude that the Presidency now belongs to an exceptionally excitable 12 year old with access to an image generator. However, there were more serious items in the President's bizarre and demeaning performance. Trump shared an image depicting Iran's territory reshaped in the outline of his own face, and another suggesting the destruction of Kharg Island. | | ---|---|--- He also boasted that he had made "Hundreds of Billions of Dollars" from stocks and other holdings while asserting that he did it for the country rather than himself. Most Americans, confronted with this lunatic spectacle, might ask a very old-fashioned question: Is the President capable of doing the job? This is where the Twenty-Fifth Amendment enters the equation. The amendment does not provide a constitutional trapdoor to remove presidents who take actions that are offensive, foolish, vulgar, or ridiculous. Section 4 establishes a procedure under which the vice president and a majority of the Cabinet can declare that the President is unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office. If the President contests this declaration, the issue goes to Congress where two thirds vote in both houses would be necessary to keep the President from resuming his powers. This is an exceptionally challenging threshold, and perhaps deservedly so. A U.S. President does not become constitutionally incapacitated because he or she posts a silly picture, or two, or twenty. **CONCORD, N.H. —** New Hampshire Republican State Committee Chairman Scott Maltzie released the following statement following Lily Tang Williams’ Republican primary victory for the Congressional District 2 seat:“I want to congratulate Lily Tang Williams on her primary victory. Lily is a fearless fighter who will proudly represent New Hampshire in Washington. She campaigns the true Granite State way, showing up, talking to voters, listening to Granite Staters, and holding town halls,” **said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie.** “Unlike Maggie Goodlander, who only seems to show up in New Hampshire when it is time to campaign, Lily is out there every day fighting for the people of this state. If there is an event, Lily is there. She is a true example of the American Dream, and her firsthand experience of living without the freedoms we too often take for granted gives her a unique perspective on why we must protect them. I look forward to working with Lily to send her to Congress and keep fighting for Granite Staters in November.”

Dear Peter, There are moments in a campaign when you can feel something beginning to change. Rick’s recent interview with News Center Maine is one of those moments. In the middle of a crowded Governor’s race, **Rick is offering Maine something different** : an independent voice who is willing to listen, tell the truth about what is making life harder, and focus on results instead of political theater. He speaks with the steadiness and honesty that have always defined him about the cost of living, housing, energy, health care, and the need to restore trust in government. These are not abstract issues. They are the pressures that families, workers, older, and young Mainers are feeling every day. **Rick believes Maine can do better.** We can make homeownership possible again. We can lower costs by demanding accountability and value from government. We can build an economy where young people can stay, families can put down roots, and older Mainers can remain secure. And we can do it by putting people ahead of parties and insiders. # PRESS RELEASE

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
September 8, 2026

**CONTACT**
Todd Cheewing
Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com

**LILY TANG WILLIAMS WINS NH-02 PRIMARY, TURNS FIGHT TO MAGGIE GOODLANDER**

MANCHESTER, N.H. — Lily Tang Williams won the Republican nomination for New Hampshire’s 2nd Congressional District Tuesday night, with the race called shortly after polls closed.

“This victory belongs to Granite Staters who believe the American Dream is worth fighting for,” said Williams. “Now we take that fight straight to Maggie Goodlander.”

Williams pledged to campaign as an independent voice focused on affordability, opportunity, and representing all Granite Staters.

“I’ll work for every Granite Stater as an independent voice—not the extremists driving today’s Democrat Party,” Williams said. “Maggie Goodlander has had two years in Congress. Now she has to answer for what she has—and hasn’t—accomplished. I’m ready to fight to make New Hampshire affordable again and preserve the American Dream.”
**About Lily Tang Williams**
Born in China just before Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in more than a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.

Peter, deciding to run for this U.S. Senate seat wasn’t easy.
I had planned on serving North Carolina from here at home. That’s why I was so humbled when North Carolinians twice elected me to be their Governor.
**But this Senate race is too consequential to sit out. The stakes are simply too high.**
I entered this race to fight for people like you, who’ve put your trust in me – and I have full faith that together, we can win. But this week, we’re facing a crucial test of our grassroots movement’s strength.
After far-right super PACs started flooding the airwaves with tens of millions in GOP dark money, my narrow lead in the polls began to shrink. Now, a recent poll shows me statistically tied with my MAGA opponent.
**Peter, the hard truth is that if we don’t respond immediately, we risk falling behind for good.[_So with less than nine weeks left until Election Day and time running out to fight back, I’m personally asking you to help out by making your first $5 donation, right now._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1303&amount=5&t=8&akid=3247%2E124072%2EBEVpj2)

I’m running because our nation cannot afford two more years of unchecked Republican power in Washington. The attacks on health care, on democratic values and even on Americans – **they have to stop.**
Our leaders should be focusing on strengthening our communities by investing in public schools, securing health care access and prioritizing hardworking folks over the wealthiest few. That’s what I strove to do in North Carolina – and by the end of my time in office, we added thousands of jobs by expanding the clean energy economy, gave public school teachers statewide a much-needed raise, expanded Medicaid and more.
**This is the work I’m ready to continue as the next Senator from North Carolina. That means we have to flip this seat from red to blue for the first time in a generation and take back the Senate for the people who elect us, which is easier said than done.**
I’ve never lost a race, but this one will be the most competitive of my career. It’s the best pick-up opportunity for Democrats this cycle, and our ability to flip the Senate hinges on us succeeding. That’s why far-right groups are already spending nearly $100 million so far to attack me – and experts expect this to be the most expensive Senate race ever, so they will spare no expense to help President Trump’s handpicked candidate buy his way to victory.
So if they see us missing our fundraising goals, they _will_ use this as an opportunity to strike. They _will_ flood the airwaves with millions more in attack ads to smear me, knowing that their investments are working as intended, because we _will not_ have enough funds to fight back.
[**_Chipping in $5, $25 or whatever amount is right for you before the end of the day won’t just help us close the gap in time; it’ll prove to everyone that momentum is on our side. body:
But we have so much to be proud of.

| |

| | Dear David, Before anything else, **I need to say thank you.** Thank you for every door you knocked, every call you made, every postcard you wrote, every dollar you gave, and every ounce of hope you put into this campaign. **We came up short tonight, but coming up short doesn’t mean we failed._Not even close._** When we started this campaign, we had one idea: that more of the same won’t fix this, and that if we truly want to change things, we have to do things differently. We didn’t have establishment backing, or a Rolodex of fancy donors. We just had each other. **By every traditional measure, we shouldn’t have been able to compete. But we did.** We proved we were a real force in this race because we had something more powerful than establishment support or corporate money. We had people. We had people like you who gave your time, your energy, and your resources to a movement fighting for a different kind of politics that puts people first, listens before it speaks, and answers to our neighbors instead of big donors. Thank you so much for being a part of this. Thank you for believing things can be different, and for putting in the work to make it so. I am so, so proud to have been on this journey with you, David, and I can’t wait for the next step in our journey together. Hi, it's Chris Pappas.

**It's official: I am the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate here in New Hampshire.**

I'm so grateful to every Granite Stater who put their trust in me and helped build this campaign together.

Growing up in Manchester and working alongside my family at our restaurant, I learned that you don't get ahead just by making promises. You have to be accountable. You listen to people, work hard, and deliver.

That's the same approach I've brought to Congress, and it's why I'm running for the Senate.

I'm running to make New Hampshire more affordable for working families; protect Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid; safeguard reproductive freedom; and stand up for the small businesses that are the backbone of our communities.

**And now our general election fight against John Sununu officially begins.**

Political experts just changed this race to a Toss‐up. The fact is: New Hampshire is a fiercely independent state, and this election could go either way. The country is watching, and the outcome here in New Hampshire will help determine control of the U.S. Senate and what the next two years look like for millions of families across the country.

No images? [Click here](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-e-ftidto-hhlljjcji-h/) **For Immediate Release:** September 8, 2026**Contact:** Kylie Glatfelter, Communications Director, [kglatfelter@indiana.gop](mailto:kglatfelter@indiana.gop)**Strong Fiscal Leadership Keeps Gas Tax Relief Going for Hoosiers ****Indianapolis, IN **- Hoosiers will see another month of savings at the pump after Governor Mike Braun extended the suspension of Indiana's Gasoline Usage Tax and Gasoline Excise Tax through October 5. The continued relief is the latest example of what responsible fiscal leadership delivers. Indiana has built a strong financial foundation by balancing budgets, maintaining healthy reserves and responsibly managing taxpayer dollars - giving state leaders the flexibility to provide relief to Hoosier families when they need it the most. "Governor Braun continues to make affordability a priority and deliver real relief for Hoosier families," said Indiana Republican Party Chairwoman Lana Keesling. "Years of responsible Republican leadership have put Indiana in a position to keep more money in Hoosiers' pockets while still meeting the needs of our communities and investing in our state's future." Indiana's reserves are currently projected to surpass $5 billion. That fiscal strength gives the state additional flexibility to offset revenue lost during the gas tax suspension without slowing down road, bridge and infrastructure work across the state. "Indiana's strong financial position reflects a commitment to living within our means," said State Comptroller Elise Nieshalla. "Years of disciplined budgeting and careful stewardship of taxpayer dollars have prepared our state to weather changing economic conditions while protecting the long-term financial stability Hoosiers expect." "Keeping Indiana financially prepared means being ready to act when Hoosiers need relief," said State Treasurer Daniel Elliott. "We can help families facing higher prices today without losing sight of the investments our communities depend on tomorrow." Governor Braun first suspended the Gasoline Usage Tax in April and later expanded the relief to include the Gasoline Excise Tax. The latest extension keeps both suspensions in place statewide through October 5.### [](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftidto-hhlljjcji-r/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftidto-hhlljjcji-y/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftidto-hhlljjcji-j/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftidto-hhlljjcji-t/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftidto-hhlljjcji-i/)[](https://indianarepublicancentralcommittee.cmail19.com/t/y-l-ftidto-hhlljjcji-d/) ** PAID FOR BY THE INDIANA REPUBLICAN STATE COMMITTEE. ****NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE OR CANDIDATE'S COMMITTEE. ****WWW.INDIANA.GOP.** | Indiana Republican State Committee 101 W. Experts at Inside Elections just shifted this race to a Toss-up, meaning the GOP’s millions in spending are working, and **we have a coin-flip chance of losing this Senate race.**
And now that John Sununu is officially our opponent – he will have the entire Republican war chest united behind him, so this race will only get more competitive.

Every dollar we raise right now goes directly into reaching voters, expanding our field programs, and countering the attack ads flooding the airwaves. subject: From Caribou, Maine, to the U.S. Senate

body:
It all started in a small town in Aroostook County.

It all started in a small town in Aroostook County.
| Hi, it's Susan.I don't get to slow down and share this very often, so today I wanted to take a moment to tell you a bit about how I got here.I grew up in Caribou, Maine - one of six kids raised by my parents, Pat and Don. Both of them served as mayor of Caribou at one point, and my dad, a World War II veteran, went on to serve in the Maine Legislature. Public service just runs in the family - I'm actually the fourth generation of Collins' in public service.Our family also ran a small retail lumber business that's been passed down for six generations, dating back to 1844. Growing up around that kind of hard work taught me a lot about what it means to show up for your community, day after day.My path to Washington wasn't a straight line. I got my start working for a Maine congressman, followed him to the Senate, and eventually found myself championing small businesses - first at the state level, then with the Small Business Administration, and later running a center dedicated to family businesses.Eventually, I ran for the Senate myself, and I've been honored to serve Maine ever since - always trying to work across the aisle and get real results for the people back home.That's my story. name: Ted Cruz
subject: What I said on Meet the Press this weekend and what I didn't say
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate
body:
I was asked about my future this weekend. I told them I'm focused on yours.

| | | | Hey Fellow Conservative, I was just on Meet the Press.... Kristen Welker asked me about 2028. About whether I'm going to run for president again. But here's the truth I told her on national television this weekend, and the truth I want to tell you directly right now: **This is not the season right now.** In the last decade, there has not been another Republican who has campaigned for more Senate candidates, more House candidates, more gubernatorial candidates than I have. I have been on the road. I have been in the arena. I have shown up in states where it was hard and uncomfortable and politically complicated, because that's what this fight demands. __I am doing it again right now_._ I need you to understand what we're actually fighting because this isn't just about seats and majorities and who controls which chamber. This is about something far bigger. **_The Democrat Party I came up watching is gone_.** What replaced it is something my father would have recognized immediately, because he lived it. He was tortured in a Cuban prison. He watched his country get strangled by a communist regime that promised the people everything, free healthcare, free education, power to the people, and delivered misery, silence, and chains. **That ideology, socialism, Marxism, the DSA agenda, is winning Democratic primaries across this country right now.** They elected a Democratic Socialist as mayor of New York City. Their endorsed candidates swept primaries in Michigan and Florida. And now that same machine is flooding money into Senate races that were never supposed to be competitive. **Texas. Iowa. Alaska. Michigan. Georgia.** James Talarico alone has $21.5 million in the bank to try to flip the Texas Senate seat. Democrats are outraising Republicans in nearly every battleground state. The Cook Political Report recently called both Texas and Iowa toss-ups. **_The map is shifting, and money is the reason_.** Chuck Schumer only needs a few of these seats to take back the majority. And the moment he does and the tax cuts get reversed, the border gets opened, conservative judges get blocked, and everything we have fought for gets dismantled piece by piece by people who openly admire the ideology that destroyed my father's country. _I will not let that happen._ I told Kristen Welker this weekend that this is the season of the midterms. I meant it. I am going to spend every day between now and November 3rd on the road, on the trail, fighting for every conservative candidate who needs someone to show up for them. **But I need to know you're fighting with me.** Not in October when it's almost too late. Right now, while there's still time to close the fundraising gap, get ads on the air, and build the ground game that shows up on Election Day. **Will you chip in today? Even $5 sends a message that conservatives are awake, organized, and ready.[[LINK]](https://trk.email.tedcruz.-xN0t5BhXyn7E2rg)** [**[****PROTECT AMERICA - CHIP IN $6 TODAY ->]**](https://trk.email.tedcruz.) There will be a season for other conversations. President Trump said it himself -- he thinks I'm talented, and he thinks I might just run again someday. _Someday._ **Today, I'm fighting for the Senate majority, for the Texas race, and for the country my father chose when he had nothing left to lose.** I hope you're fighting with me. For liberty, Ted CruzU.S. Senator - Texas

## Canada's Tariffs on US Goods Kick In
Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20 billion in U.S. goods [took effect](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2uozAQBeCngc7IsQk_hYtt6LLtlmiAGZjF4IgZwu7bXyW6b3D7o6PznT-P_gEceZ9_w4ZBKfU7XhJRFY9-hB0mhl3hYCJZWE_ZKa7cO-sqY1tj2x5G5Rf2JeRTIESHPsdwq5umLZvStvkSPA6OrAfvB_L-TiWRaytEaLAiaCjn8O6zrW1v1lZlXdyd92TtdHM1-GG4Z6XFiTUdxd_Euy5I8X964VGMactjWFSfkvlfmesy113XVVD6N5zCO4q8M5nrnimy8iiZ6z4sEOOs-ZaZU8yc0iQm8opm47gaUcRo5hTJjPEcxCisaJAIR82PMD0vjpGlqrPSzhtw_IzRH374Cu4rAAD__xO-ib0) just after midnight Tuesday morning, hitting American milk, cheese, steel, golf clubs, appliances, and clothing with duties of 15% to 50%. Ottawa vowed to match Washington's 50% duties "dollar for dollar" after trade talks collapsed last month. Economists say Midwest manufacturers and dairy producers in Wisconsin and Vermont could [take the biggest hit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0M2OrCAQBeCnwR0GEX9YsLgbd323szQlFlrTKAawTb_9xM68wewqqeTkfOfrMT6APO3Lf9jQZBfGHa_kMWeMo4UdZoI9QyTn0kr5TLvzTxqlkC0Xmgs9gs30wlFBMRuHKLEu0FRd32vVK6GL1TSTtda2SjoHna00VBKbvlaoK-G6XhVk7jyhha6EaFVXNrKunRBzJTuop6lhSuBMOcTyO9CeV3T-HV4YSxu2wps15yOx-h-TA5PDdV2lndLtuP9MDvfJ5PDhAI-YwRPkEN_8V8bPxJcQ5sQ38k9-YHTnhnwJ3nHrzynxHM_tYHIoopmPi7yn1HZMiWUD8p8a-Y_rvYz8CQAA__9nlYcx). Hours before they kicked in, President Trump threatened to [ban sales](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0Dtu6zAQheHVSJ2N4UMSWbC4wIU6pwqQUhhLQ2sSShTIsY3sPnC2kPYc4Cv-j8t0QU68395woyAxTzs9ayIRKtOMOy6Mu2DhGOvKcq97TF88adD9CfwJ_ISz8IMmi-0SIpEm01JQg3PeOgu-XYOjbu6MXazvfI_g9NV5p-3cWYzaKdNyeHngwSuA3g7nThsTARalBzTXa9dYoIUll_Nn5l1Wiuk7P6ic57y1KawiR23Mv0aPjR6l3GWteWZMr_81WiiE6X_eMS3v5b4djR6PXKU2elRq0Ab84Iyy0CvwXVvCcjw5Ja790Fi4bci_VCt_LPQI-icAAP__gcF4BQ) of Canadian plane maker Bombardier's jets in the U.S., writing, _"If they want our Market, they must build here."_ The tit-for-tat covers about 6% of American exports to Canada, with 50% U.S. tariffs on Canadian cars and steel still set for January. See [the full list](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGS3CAQRU-DslYxSCuhgMAJ2Tp1qELQrHqNQAWtUfn2rpnyDXyB__57vz7XT0eJ8tdPd6DhWNaMd0vIjHX1LrtALrOrFGPbia-WY_pNq5JqArmAXFbnmZ64jq4LJiIqHDo0j1nrZdSjXLrdzD7oeRumYdr0Nk0zerkEPeKo58cyTLIj89qTi1weUk7j3H-oYYhShoea3bBtH2KUGIhL7b8LZd4xpj_libX35eiS2ZnPJoYfQlmh7H3f_fu5670TymIWygY8XeUDM0Ok7LJHoexLVSj7ggtlpRbKJmoMJcJZS7g8N4i1HMA7wpWJMUBjx9igXds3egYu4MuVGSv8qwQYI76bQMOT8diwgoYXpN_5SF014bwpJWrTLEb5dThKbxH-z_5Po_4GAAD__4RQnAM) of tariffed products here.
## Mamdani Faces Push to Skip 9/11 Event
A petition from 9/11 [victims' relatives urging](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLvOnDAQRp8GOqNhzHIpXKSh-9OmRLP2eJnEF4QdyL59tHmF1J_06Zzz42v7IgmSXt8psqk-b4nvErhWPjdLiZxQqnSK92WX-rskH37JhoCjgkXBspGtcvE2UOuMZ0bWLZt-mudlmAdY2t1otF7j5GnEWTvEST8Y6NmTBRgs9a2Yzx8ssPQA4zB1D9TaA7geJ9LP56MZgJ3UfHY_s6S6sw_vfPHZ2RzbYPZaj9Lobw2uDa73fXc-__l4fPYG1yMHqWJLg6unKEG4qKXv1SW2Siwqcin0YhUpOkqijsBUWLmsUq7K5sgqcsynUFCWT445vdvTuOOWEKSMUzPAK5KEfzz1PzNeBv8GAAD__71oijE) New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's exclusion from Friday's 25th anniversary ceremony at ground zero topped 100,000 signatures Tuesday. Mamdani says he will attend, and has at least eight commemorations planned this week, including a speech at the NYPD's official ceremony. [The petition](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLsOnDAQAL8GukXGvAsXaa67tCmRwWu8ifEie-_Q_X10-YUU045G8-u5Pi1FSsdPe6IRz2vCu0QUwbzuNllHNonN5H0JJK-SfPxDq1Z6BLWAWla7C71x7W3tjEfU2NVo2mmel37u1VIH42a_DbMed-dm3c6d3dTe74P3Q7v4YVA1ma9PLWpplRr7qRl013mlXKsn223bUPUKHQnn5jdTkoA-fviNudn5rKMJIlepuh-VflT6cd93swebDmw4H5V-XF8i2oJQ6EggDOV1XZwFAifOlA6QgHDiyfkD7EECF4TIRYATFLwEzw0ztK0EuEkCODoSyafOxl03xUhlnKpeHael-K9K_nPm2-i_AQAA__90GozI) lists eight grievances, including his pick of a chief counsel who represented a man charged in a 2002 tanker bombing plot, and his ties to a Brooklyn imam who hosted the 1993 World Trade Center bombing mastermind. Former New York Gov. George Pataki, a Republican, says Mamdani [should skip](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuypCAQhp8GM6YA8UJAsInZ2XRDq0eaY-8gWNIzlm-_5b7CSf_6b_X9-Zq_gBLl79-woedY5oxnTciMx7xAhkCQGQ6Ksa7E75pjetFslOmlclK5GRamD84WmuAjosG2Qa-HcXR2tMo1q-8taGP6NriotTbqGdGhdnocl9hB7Bvyd59yymmlejs8OtO2UamgzQDt89kJqzAQl-Pxt1DmFWO6ygePx1K2JvmVea-i_SXMJMx0nudjIb4gh8rAmK_bJsy0l0RMSxVmuveEmZS7ZWB4kaxwVbnBFiCTrGt5pyDri3bptJYbbuUgSMJMVnejvnPN4cN-UkpU-0FY9b0Bpf-P-IcgP978CwAA___yBIbp) the event unless he distances himself from streamer Hasan Piker, who said America deserved 9/11, remarks Mamdani has called "objectionable and reprehensible."
## NFL Launches Global 2026 Season
The NFL's 107th season [kicks off today](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO6yAABNDTmA4LAzamoPiNu_x2S4vAELPBEBkSa2-_Sq6w9UhPM_N1WS82pphv_-0O00JZM86a0BqO1dlsfbS52SOGULfYnjWHdI8rZ3yiTFOmV-tafGGVlngTAA5BYAY1z1rOkmmyGXhg9C6oUQzzNLlRX5WCF5MXcnTck2jeHtNMD4xNUvUjFyIw5geurLhex04y-NjK0X-XmNuGkH7KC0fvyk6S2Vp71E786_jS8eU8zz6H9M46vrzndHz5FM4h0eo2-GcCPZBgK6gr-yOhgdZkG2gJ9ATudKA3u6OSw_jHGVOKdVKdZLfdxg9N2h_fehn-GwAA__9sPn_z) with a Super Bowl LX rematch, as the defending champion Seattle Seahawks host the New England Patriots. Tomorrow, the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams meet in Melbourne for the league's first regular-season game ever played in Australia. The schedule is the league's most global ever: a [record nine international games](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OpDAQhJ_GZKDG5s-Bg0vI5tILUYPbQ88ZG9le0L79ajbbeJNKSqr69P17LA9kz-H5Fw8yxcUl0J09lUJp2TCgZQwFEzuXdy4fOTj_nxcJcqhB16AX3ApftHRYWeOIJKmKTDtOk-6mDnS1m0mRQgeqH7fWDtO2Ao3r4FAN0Evb6YrNew806BZg6Maml0o5ANvKEdW69qIDslxial6RQ9nJ-c94UWq2eFTe7KWcWag_Qs5Czvd9Ny88MRQ-KDdbbF6nkHM-YypZyPn9JeQM-h2TkPMRE9U_6jo4X2fCHEN9JrqYbiHnKhl73uw952EUHTwPZP-NUH5p7jLyKwAA___Nh4FI) across seven countries and four continents, including first-time visits to Rio de Janeiro and Paris. The season wraps up on Valentine's Day 2027 with Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The Rams open as [Super Bowl favorites](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAURb8Gd4zwgxmbgiIN3aZNaWHzGL-EAQvejjN_H80qf7Ddla50dO_59bF8BMpU7j_DAx2nuhQ8e0ZmbMsWSogUCodGKfWd-LOXlP_QAgpuUlmp7BI2picuJgzRJURAPaAbp3m2ZjbKDrszekrXVadpG0fQEBLO02wNWL0lrfU6kHvzlFV2VOpmpssVtE5KxRGmoNf1KozCSFzb5Xelwjum_KpPbJetPobsduajC_1DgBfgz_O8YD_KuxTg31GAX5GZyl2A71zbS4BfBHiKAryZZmVnCwL816_-eWCTaz2zzH9J1hi7LCnLftTGXf4nyY6h1yJPKpIrh9zlkcOrptSH5uJxUs7Ub5Mw6v4IlL-28jcVPx38CwAA___Ov5Dv) after acquiring Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett, with the Buffalo Bills, Baltimore Ravens, Seahawks, and Kansas City Chiefs close behind in the betting odds. body:
Lindsey promised me things would be okay. I've watched him keep that promise to South Carolina ever since. Now, it’s my turn. |
---

Fellow Patriot,

There's a moment I've never forgotten.

I was 11 when we lost our mom. A little over a year later, we lost our dad, too. Our family business - a pool hall and bar right on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - still needed to be run. And I was wondering what came next.

[](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=ad1a63aa17714e63ab7ec4f5e3fc5738&_e=Z75zLIkytg08S4qw54FGByGJwPPnUWvSyiFJwzbhWALoRBRSUmF5xxv-Z-Ltb1GE-cwfR2o-hTLyqVunfMHW_giojCOlcrT5YbtSmpnwELNUmcNqM1arnT8ab8zlvJDEFe84RfiHdy5C4ycwvkjx22fc791o-xcCrnzLxh3yKlrI11_JiO7ahxGbzDgr8k9qxbks-N8yFZlLP4GyK4evUWw4MkGelPzEfMlFwYsEp7-euGFkFvI_GvXZlWAZEFVVfdWD6IQoNavn-F4fovvV5I7fWrAO5t8ilSZrYneWDHRB-bkURj1f6QOAW0hmwCrYDxuN8CAxR-Tot3B81vXT1MlhHhDpS63UB2Mhh2fn7ETDkEdAd4hMoW6Dmw-J0cXMgnQR0R_uu748-yeiD40oGULcNfVhja0gyguPoHkbTc6ahZkfaQXGqpm4CVGctPM-EeUe2uD3kxO3L92bj1febfAHR1APwdcO7BqE3NmYYAFX4HUJeeqLFLmlpeAZzyFdA9ElC-orS3QQ0HAJ-maerRxmZ3I3VeHgVoxFwJJ29ekCg3HQVkJCtnNNKbqp8Uh7YjWlmT94VoSpUoU7ZbRO8OF7sgu9Y_wJl-WxdBOwrH2gcyn1OPgEp8YKO7NvintTwCYXSrFZtXKa_EjaDRxSLkuD20q10nMJ711Be6iCcvCtMW3O6NUws0U2884g5ZZ6G_gPNkZe1SfVczWpjf_ceA%3D%3D)
My brother Lindsey figured it out.

He was in college, and he came home on weekends to take care of me and keep the doors open. It wasn't easy for him, but he made sure I had what I needed. That's just what he always did.

Our folks never finished high school. They ran the Sanitary Cafe - part bar, part restaurant, part pool hall - and we lived in the back of it, right there on Main Street. Lindsey swept those floors right alongside me. We both heard those conversations of working people from the textile mills, stopping in after their shift, talking about what they needed, what they hoped for, and what kept them up at night.

Those people shaped him a lot more than much else ever did.

After college and law school, he joined the Air Force. There he served as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after South Carolina sent him to the Statehouse, Congress and finally, the Senate, he kept his commission. His service included short deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq where he stood shoulder to shoulder with 19-year-olds from little towns just like ours who were willing to give everything.

You want to know why he fought so hard in Washington? _Because he knew who was counting on him._

It's the family in Greenville stretching a paycheck that doesn't quite reach. The veteran in Spartanburg that earned every benefit he gets. The business owner in Florence who built something from nothing and doesn't need the government to make it harder.

These are his people. And right now, they need someone in their corner.

**The radical left in this country today:** they want open borders, higher taxes, and more government in your life. They'll smile and tell you it's for your own good.

I'm here to tell you it isn't.

clean_body: Lindsey promised me things would be okay. I've watched him keep that promise to South Carolina ever since. Now, it’s my turn. | Fellow Patriot, There's a moment I've never forgotten. I was 11 when we lost our mom. A little over a year later, we lost our dad, too. Our family business - a pool hall and bar right on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - still needed to be run. And I was wondering what came next. My brother Lindsey figured it out. He was in college, and he came home on weekends to take care of me and keep the doors open. It wasn't easy for him, but he made sure I had what I needed. That's just what he always did. Our folks never finished high school. They ran the Sanitary Cafe - part bar, part restaurant, part pool hall - and we lived in the back of it, right there on Main Street. Lindsey swept those floors right alongside me. We both heard those conversations of working people from the textile mills, stopping in after their shift, talking about what they needed, what they hoped for, and what kept them up at night. Those people shaped him a lot more than much else ever did. After college and law school, he joined the Air Force. There he served as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after South Carolina sent him to the Statehouse, Congress and finally, the Senate, he kept his commission. His service included short deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq where he stood shoulder to shoulder with 19-year-olds from little towns just like ours who were willing to give everything. You want to know why he fought so hard in Washington? Because he knew who was counting on him. It's the family in Greenville stretching a paycheck that doesn't quite reach. The veteran in Spartanburg that earned every benefit he gets. The business owner in Florence who built something from nothing and doesn't need the government to make it harder. These are his people. And right now, they need someone in their corner. The radical left in this country today: they want open borders, higher taxes, and more government in your life. They'll smile and tell you it's for your own good. I'm here to tell you it isn't. The legacy my brother built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did every single day for the great people of South Carolina. I am starting this General Election behind financially. All those years ago, he promised me things would be okay. Now, it's my turn to pick up where he left off and make sure the people he loved, South Carolinians from the Grand Strand to the Golden Corner, are okay. I can't let him down. That's why, when President Trump asked me to run, I answered the call. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart. Our vision is simple: **_A world where every child is safe and free._** We work with partners to prevent exploitation before it begins, support rescue operations, and equip investigators. Our partners walk with survivors as they heal and rebuild their lives. Because rescue is only the beginning. And right now, there is an urgent need. We are launching **_Operation Search and Rescue, _**a _ _ mission to connect investigators and agents, identify traffickers, and build criminal evidence.

We will support real rescue operations using tools like **digital tracking and face recognition**. This is how children are found and how traffickers are stopped.

## Texas Approves New Social Studies Standards
The Texas State Board of Education gave [final approval](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE8DmUe28Z_BgYNNyP6mG6LGbqC1xkZ2A_Nvv2KusFlJpSpVvT_f4zdQpLT8hg0dv-c8JrxqRGYsY8m1zlSwMsU4HSVRWmJOyzpqqZ9CWiHtCJ7pxNFAG9wkg1UtOvXqe_ulXi_Zrs70GEwfjAkKZeh1b_SEszSdVPapVdeSu-uklVYpqY19WKWVmabOSvh66m5ujMRAnMuDV2R8Q53jTz6xPHze2uhW5r023a9GD40erut6zPl9_7j9Rg9HbfTwyQkMhwemnMSUoQQB-17yiVX4nPhWpRJE4Y9SyB_x2IRfIS1YBf9QWkSBQB6ioBphE1YoJYAZ_N_aFhf2i2Kk-nw1Ri4bUPwM5P8Fezr9LwAA__-TA5HC) Friday to new high school social studies standards covering U.S. history, government, and world geography. Dozens of speakers testified across hours of meetings, most opposing the final version. The standards attribute the Sept. 11 attacks to "radical Islam" rather than to the specific terrorist groups involved. Students will also study early Islam through Muhammad's "brutal military campaigns against Jewish and Christian tribes" and the "normalization of slavery." Board member Brandon Hall said [dropping](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuuozAQhp8GOkdj4zi4oNiG7my7JRpfgJEcG3lMcs7br8grnO6TZv6L_n9fyxdSorz9xWec2vdalhzfnGJrsS61MK9UIzdKyZ01U95Sydu-KFBGgBVgF_SNXnHR2IfJQbCyj5N8jKO9y8cD-n0CZfR9UAaGIKVxdoRBj4NGeTdoVq16mi47sGClBKXtzUoltXODBbwbNaydhhiolXpre2zxG3lNP-UV682XZ5-mvbWDu-FPp-ZOzQadvw6dmrmV-tOp-aMRMZweG5UsXMEaBB5HLa_IwpfcLqpMmESOb8HFX8jtDHQ9nLWSP9P5FMfpEnmx07YL9nspiQWGUCMz5U0QJ7ySpR3BWJCdmvs6heNNKRGbR6dheyKlT_P228Vfk_ofAAD__5X-mMQ) "brutal" would be "whitewashing and watering down a part of history." Board member Will Hickman countered that "military battles and wars are all brutal, but we have not described any others that way." The Republican-majority board approved the language over objections from Democratic members, Muslim groups, and three board-appointed curriculum experts. Districts set their own lesson specifics but must follow the standards, which phase in starting in the 2030-31 school year.
## Ross Fire Still Burning, 57% Contained
The Ross Fire is [57% contained](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOgzAQRU9jOqLxAAEXLrZxl223RAYPYMlgZA9J9vYr5wrbTDNfX--_n8f4sD74Y_22O2l-L3E86JUDMVMaU8x58Yky-xCmKx3-WEM81m1EwHsNqgY12pn9k8bWVk5P4JSsSMt-GFQn-x6qTasWW8SucU3XNx1IcIMd0Lp-Uc4BdJXXpQ4UKCkBW3VTEmU7TY0C292xWUQL5DzHdOONmN42L-E3Pind5rhXQW_MZxbNl0Aj0OSTZk7XHuJsQ1lTUgINv8szXrzVn46aQn3aHAWakhJoCoZAA6qcQaApAupioL5OZ5mqpN358iH4fO9FC-tuffhA8H_lPTX-BQAA__8NzYOM) after burning more than 90,400 acres in Palo Pinto and Jack counties since Aug. 24, making it the largest summertime wildfire in Texas since statewide records began in 2005. The Texas A&M Forest Service says the fire has [destroyed 167 structures](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyhCAQhp8GOxxYUY6CIo3dpU3pgK66Ew4cIOfl7TPeK6Tdb_b_5_u_7tPdUaC4fboH2vpa0xTxLAFrxTzlVMpKGUulEPxPjhS3kOK2TyBg4MJwYSY3V3ripFyzWC8WIxu0Ut9uppdai2a3yncGhZaD7uXamZsSoL02al5A90vvG7JXnDDCSClAmdZIkMr7zgjXD9CtTAlcqKbc1h0rvlxZw296Ym7n9GiC3Ws9Cus-GIwMxvM829mXy-PiDMb3C4PxOjEYLy1-efGILvPDhcQPijXxnbadnxSWN81UvhmMTbbLcVIIVAbNlNgejsK7uf53saeFvwAAAP__dJ6B2w), including 18 occupied homes, and damaged 95 more. Buildings at Worth Ranch, a Scouting America camp, sustained catastrophic damage. No campers were present. Hundreds of firefighters, engines, and aircraft have worked the blaze. Jack County lifted mandatory evacuations a day after ordering them, and school districts resumed normal operations by Aug. 31. Drought keeps statewide wildfire potential high after more than 1,000 fires burned 300,000 acres this year. "_The dry grass and vegetation provide a lot of fuel_ ," said UT Arlington assistant professor Yunyao Li.
## Free Eggs Coming to Food Banks
The [South Plains Food Bank in Lubbock](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAUhJ8Gd1hA8A8FxW3c5bZbWmCOMQqGCE7s5O1XXu0bbDuaGX0zX_f5bkIMyf83O2h8r3lOcNYIiFDmkmtdQ4GKIUb7KikkH3Py2yyY6ClTlKnZLBgOmKVpnLbMKd6A5sM4qo4PA2s2zTq7LOCcc_3YDWoZViGgs6ZTo-3kKpugrzqmmOKcCalaxQWX1t4UM10vbiuRDFzAXFrcAOFt6ho_-YDSLnlvot4Qn5Xc_hExETGd59nCAeWD28X7sjYvj8tJxHSNI2L6FekZYqQFFggHUC7Zg4L3la4l79Qg5pLgQz0kKCbSByT6NG_MiYipKdo9r3io_UAk87sJ8QcH_3rjocV3AAAA__9nIYti) and the High Plains Food Bank in Amarillo will each receive 140,400 free eggs, part of a statewide handout of more than 7 million eggs, Attorney General Ken Paxton announced Tuesday. subject: Some things you never forget
body:
Lindsey promised me things would be okay. I've watched him keep that promise to South Carolina ever since. Now, it’s my turn. |

Fellow Patriot,

There's a moment I've never forgotten.

I was 11 when we lost our mom. A little over a year later, we lost our dad, too. Our family business - a pool hall and bar right on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - still needed to be run. And I was wondering what came next.

[](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=9f5214908c5e45cfade6715b3643cd8b&_e=Xu2s0FTN8mcUQPHg1mfHEEWaheXJvGRRLFFQxDX3i4Yj2gFzR29kYNegF-tQYmVlPD2u7xQXG2cQ9DubxLqhk6BrD3mEoCwQMnGYczmB_fwIKGxkPHjcMCpzuoEfgGf8v3qfsiQKZwyekAJeHk5G9O7c7C42ZxueM9jGvxmoqOo3IZp19jxouFVhHusrkaCBxsPca1lhiFWHct3LuxSU_GqcPYxEowcjB6KUZvQirKH_q9XA2CqGtqBHdyKRqcBLztUDKeE17LkIhd0aa-sy2X8ITjS0Gk0AZwxL8i4xnEaA5ypMxAxgTm9LMx7iPfrkMq5dkbn-CHxVXiPpsoIzJa6hFUpt5Fr4FDE850XDKrh7_x60ksz-NyX3fPrjZiL8Yhe6-dcQ7xu2to5C90gP-tNEDe63aJp43Vmh-x2Ukelb8tUj_U2niWxRCVGRrKkdDBTfuumL5ZLDvmtcK_6dc7Ilb0f_J7tJ4iJycCjmPHXvC0GTQ6D2G4ZTWRJr1C6u4xOGjHwh_VmBMjhsS9mQdIaCSVZeRrEKETLivC-kLv4mDznbuYsFmCwfNqdaYp_NDGlUDU1AOuExGLsJgRNWuG7YgCvg0VE9jz61kmhf5gYXzFtguN0MMU5CcgpvF5hBR5PFbAr6rhbOtl9p2p9UkFEWw_RtcFOXt-KeMwUtZgw9MQjg6A_YytsNhxey4qQ-LkmGY1QRf0jHFEZIl7uP6bITiH5D8BoLMt-klG7942Y%3D)
My brother Lindsey figured it out.

He was in college, and he came home on weekends to take care of me and keep the doors open. It wasn't easy for him, but he made sure I had what I needed. That's just what he always did.

Our folks never finished high school. They ran the Sanitary Cafe - part bar, part restaurant, part pool hall - and we lived in the back of it, right there on Main Street. Lindsey swept those floors right alongside me. We both heard those conversations of working people from the textile mills, stopping in after their shift, talking about what they needed, what they hoped for, and what kept them up at night.

Those people shaped him a lot more than much else ever did.

After college and law school, he joined the Air Force. There he served as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after South Carolina sent him to the Statehouse, Congress and finally, the Senate, he kept his commission. His service included short deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq where he stood shoulder to shoulder with 19-year-olds from little towns just like ours who were willing to give everything.

You want to know why he fought so hard in Washington? _Because he knew who was counting on him._

It's the family in Greenville stretching a paycheck that doesn't quite reach. The veteran in Spartanburg that earned every benefit he gets. The business owner in Florence who built something from nothing and doesn't need the government to make it harder.

These are his people. And right now, they need someone in their corner.

**The radical left in this country today:** they want open borders, higher taxes, and more government in your life. They'll smile and tell you it's for your own good.

I'm here to tell you it isn't.

clean_body: Lindsey promised me things would be okay. I've watched him keep that promise to South Carolina ever since. Now, it’s my turn. | Fellow Patriot, There's a moment I've never forgotten. I was 11 when we lost our mom. A little over a year later, we lost our dad, too. Our family business - a pool hall and bar right on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - still needed to be run. And I was wondering what came next. My brother Lindsey figured it out. He was in college, and he came home on weekends to take care of me and keep the doors open. It wasn't easy for him, but he made sure I had what I needed. That's just what he always did. Our folks never finished high school. They ran the Sanitary Cafe - part bar, part restaurant, part pool hall - and we lived in the back of it, right there on Main Street. Lindsey swept those floors right alongside me. We both heard those conversations of working people from the textile mills, stopping in after their shift, talking about what they needed, what they hoped for, and what kept them up at night. Those people shaped him a lot more than much else ever did. After college and law school, he joined the Air Force. There he served as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after South Carolina sent him to the Statehouse, Congress and finally, the Senate, he kept his commission. His service included short deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq where he stood shoulder to shoulder with 19-year-olds from little towns just like ours who were willing to give everything. You want to know why he fought so hard in Washington? Because he knew who was counting on him. It's the family in Greenville stretching a paycheck that doesn't quite reach. The veteran in Spartanburg that earned every benefit he gets. The business owner in Florence who built something from nothing and doesn't need the government to make it harder. These are his people. And right now, they need someone in their corner. The radical left in this country today: they want open borders, higher taxes, and more government in your life. They'll smile and tell you it's for your own good. I'm here to tell you it isn't. The legacy my brother built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did every single day for the great people of South Carolina. I am starting this General Election behind financially. All those years ago, he promised me things would be okay. Now, it's my turn to pick up where he left off and make sure the people he loved, South Carolinians from the Grand Strand to the Golden Corner, are okay. I can't let him down. That's why, when President Trump asked me to run, I answered the call. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart. That is how consequential this moment is.

But here is the part the pundits won't tell you. None of that happens automatically.

__The Democrats are at war with the American people -- open borders, defunding ICE, eliminating voter ID, putting men in women's sports.__

You name it, they are on the wrong side of it.

DHS took a system called the SAVE database. That stands for Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements. It was built to verify immigration benefits. That's it. That's all it was supposed to do.
They repurposed it to flag American voters as suspected non-citizens. Over 24,000 names. Referred to ICE.
Standing Our Ground is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..h_Sl2HmVoE7Tc9zb_Q2H3-sKcIB21ouKXhMArOJ6clA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=214813965)
Here's the part that should make your blood pressure go up. The database is full of errors. We're not talking about a few edge cases. We are talking about naturalized citizens, people who went through the whole process, who became Americans, who have every legal right to vote, getting flagged. Being treated like they don't belong here.
The Georgia Secretary of State got a subpoena from immigration enforcement requesting voter records, including citizenship documents, for 13 individuals. Thirteen. Individual. People. Who are American citizens.
I want to be clear about something. Andrea Flores worked immigration policy at DHS under Obama and Biden. She knows what that database was built for. She knows what it is not for. And she said flat out, this is wrong. And she said the small number of subpoenas they've issued tells you this is not the widespread phenomenon they wanted people to believe it was. That's why they're having such a hard time finding it. Because it doesn't exist.
Mark Elias and the team at Democracy Docket are filing lawsuits. An appeals court has already blocked DHS from using SAVE to scrub voter rolls.
Sit with what this is. They built a system to help immigrants access benefits. They turned it into a tool to strip Americans of their right to vote. And they're doing it sixty days before an election.
That's not a mistake. That's a plan.

body:
This proud mom thanks you for all you’ve done for my Gabby and for this movement.
#

Hello friend,
My name is Gloria Giffords. I’m Gabby Giffords’s mom. I stand in awe of my daughter.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260909-1-b&t=1&akid=11789%2E3935704%2EO6oHiN)
I know every mom will tell you her child is perfect, but Gabby is just about as close as it comes. Growing up, she was always a good kid. She was a loyal friend. And to know Gabby Giffords is to know one thing: _Don’t ever — not for one moment — underestimate her._
Gabby’s one tough cookie. If she thought she could do something, she put her mind to it until it was done. And to anyone who thought she wasn’t capable of something..._well, she quickly proved them wrong._
Our nation has seen what Gabby is capable of since that awful morning in January 2011. It’s been a long road to recovery, but she continues fighting — not only for herself, but for families all across our country.
She inspires me every day, and I know I’m not alone.
**[Today, I am asking for you to join me in supporting Gabby’s work. GIFFORDS PAC is on the front lines to end the gun violence crisis in America, and they need more grassroots support ahead of the upcoming election. name: Team Gina
subject: Recent news has created massive confusion across Texas. We’re clearing up that confusion.
body:
Greg Abbott is counting on Texas voters to sit this election out.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Recent news has created massive confusion across Texas because 1.2 million registered Texas voters have been placed on the voter “suspense” list.
When voters see headlines like this, many people assume that their registration has been cancelled or that they can no longer cast a ballot. This confusion is extremely dangerous, and it plays in Greg Abbott’s favor.
**We want to be clear about what this news means. Being on the voter suspense list does _not_ mean your voter registration has been purged. It simply means that local officials need an updated address before October 5th – the voter registration deadline here in Texas.**
Abbott and Republicans know that confusion can discourage people from the polls. And they do these deliberate tactics so that people are discouraged from showing up, because they know that the stakes of this race couldn’t be higher.
**And Abbott also knows that when Texans turn out, his time in office is up. That’s why we can’t allow a single eligible voter to be sidelined by confusion or bureaucratic red tape.**
Our campaign is organizing on the ground every single day between now and November to clear up the confusion, reach voters directly, and make sure our community is ready to make their voices heard at the ballot box.

We just won two elections in two weeks. The special, then the runoff.

Peter,
The Department of Justice has been busy under its new leader, Todd Blanche, Trump's former personal lawyer. But they haven't been fighting crime. On the contrary, the DOJ seems to be gearing up to commit crimes of its own.
Last month, Donald Trump gave a national address on elections where he floated completely made up data and reheated debunked conspiracies to lay the groundwork to use unconstitutional and highly illegal actions to challenge the results of the upcoming midterms.
Now, Todd Blanche is putting Trump's plan into motion. It was just announced the DOJ will be sending a record breaking one thousand election monitors to polling locations for the midterm elections.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001RthZj8iJsZqPmYP9EABmsP1Wq_qOzMxS-0Erq88Im9CSakDQBVbzUl77UN9tT_xopyPhRmuDK0x8bgOPITbOPFjwt4rXIlp8MErkbusdeGnZhNd7hLij-rlyUTzTjxFwQe9dURcRrtwkD-B0sSLPVBKm6SQ2w3d1T1TGuur4Bv2dYFYIlUqFpVlZdaxR3I4yYNOf4hWnIEk0-4sF7bYUUK52qczGw4tTzJOFVCWevDrEWXFpo3y26Q==&c=BG4oEwl4DR9_9c1dWYvgLNkjSPN5OhYDsKDH_1jcgDpVmeTRAwFvLg==&ch=d4KgXnvh4M5YXqP0Y4CuQKh-GzCxhlxXWE2_Nr13u6Pvn30Ol2O_sw==)
---
There is no doubt what the Trump admin is intending with this move. The DOJ isn't sending a historic number of election monitors because voter fraud exists, it's because it doesn't. What they're hoping to catch isn't fraud, but any slip-up or honest mistake by a poll worker--any excuse, however small, to challenge an election's results.
And don't take it just from us. One state election official laid out to NPR earlier this month what this could look like in practice: a DOJ monitor finds a pretext to challenge a result, a friendly judge issues subpoenas the day after Election Day, agents show up at a county office in a close race, and walk out with the ballots "so we can count them."
This is exactly why Defend Our Courts exists. We're building a firewall of state Supreme Courts, the courts with ultimate say over election law in their states, and the last line of defense when Trump tries to steal an election in broad daylight.
There are only 55 days left until the midterm elections. We have to be prepared for the worst, and make this election too big to rig. But for us to fight at the scale this moment demands, we have to dramatically build our war chest, right now. And that means we need the help of Democrats everywhere today.

However , you can do so at the link at the bottom of this email. | == | Peter, The Department of Justice has been busy under its new leader, Todd Blanche, Trump's former personal lawyer. But they haven't been fighting crime. On the contrary, the DOJ seems to be gearing up to commit crimes of its own. Last month, Donald Trump gave a national address on elections where he floated completely made up data and reheated debunked conspiracies to lay the groundwork to use unconstitutional and highly illegal actions to challenge the results of the upcoming midterms. Now, Todd Blanche is putting Trump's plan into motion. It was just announced the DOJ will be sending a record breaking one thousand election monitors to polling locations for the midterm elections. | == There is no doubt what the Trump admin is intending with this move. The DOJ isn't sending a historic number of election monitors because voter fraud exists, it's because it doesn't. What they're hoping to catch isn't fraud, but any slip-up or honest mistake by a poll worker--any excuse, however small, to challenge an election's results. And don't take it just from us. One state election official laid out to NPR earlier this month what this could look like in practice: a DOJ monitor finds a pretext to challenge a result, a friendly judge issues subpoenas the day after Election Day, agents show up at a county office in a close race, and walk out with the ballots "so we can count them." This is exactly why Defend Our Courts exists. We're building a firewall of state Supreme Courts, the courts with ultimate say over election law in their states, and the last line of defense when Trump tries to steal an election in broad daylight. There are only 55 days left until the midterm elections. We have to be prepared for the worst, and make this election too big to rig. name: Enoch for Congress
subject: We’re at a Critical Point, What We Raise Now Could Make the Difference...
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Committee to Elect Enoch
body:
Our new signs arrive today, and they’re already spoken for. We urgently need more signs and resources to launch our digital ads.

| | | | | |
---
| | | | | | Hello Peter,

We have reached a **critical point in this campaign.**
Our newest order of campaign signs is **due to arrive today—and every one of those signs has already been spoken for.** That is exciting because it shows that people across the district want to publicly show their support. But it also means **we urgently need to order more signs.**
At the same time, we need to **get our digital advertising up and running** so we can reach thousands more voters across Ohio’s 8th Congressional District.**What we are able to raise right now could make or break this election.** We are entering the period when voters are paying closer attention, making decisions, and preparing to vote. We cannot afford to lose momentum because we don't have the resources to communicate with them.

### **Can you help us meet this moment?**
###
A [contribution of **$5, $10, $25, $50, $100, $250, $500](https://us.list-manage.com/tudfRuhUvvE?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)—or whatever you can afford, **will help us put more signs throughout the district, reach voters through digital advertising, print additional campaign materials, and expand our grassroots voter outreach.

---
| [Contribute $1, $5, $10, $25 today!](https://us.list-manage.com/15xdUREs6JL?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
---
| |
And there are ways to help that don't require making a contribution. **Come out and join us this week!**
**TONIGHT — Wednesday, September 9 | LULAC Candidates Forum**
**5:30–7:30 PM**
Fueled Collective
3825 Edwards Rd., Suite 103
Cincinnati, OH 45209
I will be participating in a Candidates Forum with the **League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC)**. LULAC Cincinnati lists the Fueled Collective at this address as its contact location.
[](https://us.list-manage.com/ueW0yjuQhX2?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)**THURSDAY, September 10 | Walk With Us in the Harvest Home Parade**
**Team Enoch gathers at 5:00 PM**
We need volunteers to **walk with us, carry signs, distribute literature, and show voters the strength of this grassroots campaign.** The official parade information confirms that participants form at 5:00 PM and the parade begins at 6:00 PM.
**Sign up to volunteer through CampaignHQ:**
[Join Team Enoch on CampaignHQ](https://us.list-manage.com/uM5iYfgT8vk?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
[****](https://us.list-manage.com/7O7qIgNXYGS?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)**SATURDAY, September 12 | Hair. Housing. & Healthcare. — It All Hits Home.**
**2:00–4:00 PM**
The Pike Bar & Grill
10010 Springfield Pike
Cincinnati, OH 45215
Join us for a **fundraising event, panel discussion, and community meet & greet** focused on issues that African Americans face, and that touch our families every day: **Hair. Housing. Healthcare. It All Hits Home.**
We'll bring together community voices to talk about the issues affecting our families, our neighborhoods, and our future.**Food and drinks will be served while they last!**

### **This Campaign Needs You Now**

There are many ways to be part of this movement. **Donate. Walk with us. Volunteer. Put up a sign. Attend an event. Share our campaign with your friends and family.** Our grassroots campaign is built one person at a time. Every contribution helps us reach another voter. Every volunteer helps us reach another neighborhood. Every sign gives our campaign greater visibility.**Our signs arriving today are already spoken for. Let's raise enough to order the next batch immediately, and get our digital ads running.**
---
| [DONATE](https://us.list-manage.com/szSzNk58W00?e=c6e7dff14c&c2id=d95570268fc9105c688a303b4f3b91b8)
---
| |
We have worked too hard and come too far to slow down now.**Let's finish strong.**
With gratitude,
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch, Ph.D., MBA**
Democratic Candidate for Congress
Ohio's 8th Congressional District
**Enoch for Congress**

body:
Senate Republicans recently announced that they have no plans to spend party money to help conservative Ken Paxton

| | | |
#
---
---
|
---
Senate Republicans recently announced that they have no plans to spend party money to help conservative Ken Paxton win the U.S. Senate race in Texas. "We in the Senate don't have the money budgeted for Texas. We need help from the president," said Senator John Kennedy (R-LA). Republican Leader John Thune (R-SD) later confirmed the plan to abandon Paxton financially and deflected responsibility to the president. "I'm hoping the White House will become engaged; Texas is an incredibly expensive state," Thune said. What makes this so infuriating is that the Senate GOP spent over $100 million attacking Ken Paxton in the Republican primary. **They had plenty of money to spend on Texas when they were trying to defeat a conservative, but when it comes to defeating a Marxist like James Talarico, they’ve got nothing.** You would think that since they spent so much against the party's eventual nominee, they would feel some obligation to help him now. **This race is competitive because they hurt Paxton in the primary. It should be on them, not President Trump, to clean up their mess. You break it, you own it.** Sadly, that's not going to happen. Now we know why Trump: \- Invaded Venezuela
\- Removed the dictator Maduro but kept his VP in power \- While blocking opposition leader and Nobel laureate Maria Corina - \- - Machado from returning home
\- And delaying all talk of elections...

...so the U.S. could control Venezuelan oil in violation of its constitution!

Will gas prices come down for Americans? I hope so, though they’re not likely to come down nearly as much as Trump has forced them up through his idiotic and illegal Iran War.

But here’s a guarantee — this will surely pad the pockets of the Trump family and of Big Oil companies, and it will delay a transition to cleaner energy.

Bottom line: using our troops for a private oil grab is corruption at an epic scale.

This President just can’t hold back from abusing his power to enrich himself, his family, and his donors. From selling off presidential pardons to the highest bidder to raking in billions from a shady crypto sale, we see it every day.

It’s hard not to grow numb to it — nobody even bats an eye at his shameless promotion of his golf and hotel properties, urging foreign leaders and special interests to spend, spend, spend.

But when faced with a President who’s all about me, myself, and I, it’s more important than ever to get back to _we, the people_.

**We have a chance with the upcoming midterm elections to put a check on Trump’s power by retaking Democratic majorities in both the House and the Senate, and to deliver a resounding rebuke of this corrupt White House with a big, blue wave across the country.**
