---|---|---
Rep. Ashley Hinson and Sen. Joni Ernst are trying to add their China-backed "Save Our Bacon Act" (SOB) or some version of it, to the 2026 Farm Bill to nullify existing voter-approved U.S. state laws preventing the most extreme confinement and abuse of pigs and other farm animals and to prohibit states from passing new similar laws.
Guess who really loves their idea of undermining U.S. voters, the U.S. Supreme Court (which upheld the laws), and negating state laws in order to allow the most extreme confinement and abuse of farm animals to continue? China, which owns the largest pork processor operating on U.S. soil.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0b97e034-3b32-4888-a90c-900ab1d0938d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
China-owned Smithfield and its U.S. lobbying group, the National Pork Producers Council, have been aggressively pushing for Hinson and Ernst's SOB Act, and Federal Election Commission [records](https://substack.com/redirect/9a67afc7-1cdb-4d3c-94ac-d508d22e3e49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) show that both Ernst and Hinson, along with many other House and Senate Republicans and Democrats, have taken thousands of dollars in campaign donations from these organizations. In 2022, Rep. Dan Newhouse [returned campaign funding](https://substack.com/redirect/c54031b4-e813-4d91-bc47-ed9e3a020e47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Smithfield due to its Chinese ownership. Hinson and Ernst, as of now, have refused to do the same.
Ashley Hinson recently said that concerns about her bill is ["Chinese propaganda."](https://substack.com/redirect/fa3f53e2-4551-4ffc-8ddd-bc0a0a3c3aaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But the receipts tell a different story.
Smithfield has been [controlled by China's 万洲国际 (WH Group)](https://substack.com/redirect/201d8990-13a9-4d4d-97a8-530ccb54de24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (formerly Shuanghui Group) since 2013, when they bought the company with a loan from a CCP state bank. WH Group's leadership is literally stacked with [members of the CCP](https://substack.com/redirect/201d8990-13a9-4d4d-97a8-530ccb54de24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Its chairman, Wan Long, was also a [soldier](https://substack.com/redirect/a4f52d22-ea4d-4bbb-b99f-fd594c9ca0d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the People's Liberation Army. The Smithfield purchase handed the Chinese company control of valuable American agricultural infrastructure, technology and approximately 146,000 acres of American farmland at the time.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..zxj6sJU97xBaY8l2AfU6z-UiQq4C4P8vOKfcubmXVz0?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214901990)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/94cc739e-f00a-416f-9c0d-7a3a2ff67b4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Disclosures [filed in August 2026](https://substack.com/redirect/4cc92264-bc70-4049-b30c-2cee7534e85e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reveal that China's CCP-tied pork company Smithfield paid lobbying firm Greenberg Traurig, LLP, $120,000 to spend April through June of 2026 lobbying on "animal welfare standards; Farm Bill reauthorization; issues related to foreign ownership of agricultural land."
It was recently revealed that Smithfield's lobbyist initially failed to disclose that his Farm Bill and SOB Act lobbying benefits China, as required by US law.[ As Loomered.com first reported](https://substack.com/redirect/1732b45e-40e8-497e-a2bc-09f48805eef7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the lobbyist was forced to amend the report to add WH Group (万洲国际) as a "foreign entity" after a federal complaint was filed.
Communist China understands the stakes perfectly. In 2023, the [CCP-controlled propaganda outlet China Weekly](https://substack.com/redirect/9cc3911e-4806-449b-be07-c8dffca7dcc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) celebrated Hinson's bill as a measure that "would significantly increase China's share of the U.S. pork market if it is successfully passed."
The translated article titled "The International Outlook Is Positive for China's Pork Industry" said Hinson's bill was important to China because: "many US states have different laws regarding pork production, posing multiple challenges to Chinese investors and making it difficult for them to compete with domestic companies. Furthermore, these state laws often favor smaller US farms, disadvantaging multinational corporations and weakening the operational efficiency of Chinese pork companies."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c49c54a0-d99d-40e5-a77c-5086add24814?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Republicans cannot claim to put America First while helping a Chinese-controlled conglomerate undermine American voters and farmers.
Last year, when asked about the SOB Act, I told the [New York Sun](https://substack.com/redirect/b6eb7b2f-1f4c-4126-b5e8-8cf5f6ed7880?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "Like most people, I eat meat and also support humane animal treatment...I support states' rights."
Fortunately, some real America First Republicans have refused to play into Xi Jinping's hands. In September 2025, [14 House Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/8fc4eb36-a144-421f-8406-b9bdb1b8143d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including Reps. Anna Paulina Luna and Byron Donalds urged congressional agriculture leaders to reject the SOB Act and related proposals.
They called the measures "sweeping federal overreach" that would trample states' rights, overturn voters' decisions, punish farmers who invested in meeting higher standards and expand foreign influence over American food production.
Luna and Donalds also [led a similar push](https://substack.com/redirect/6b1e50ba-cbe3-42c6-8cf3-bc750ae0d997?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against Hinson's bill in 2024.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/240c8006-cabb-4027-b46f-1f48f28321d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Senator Tom Cotton](https://substack.com/redirect/4a2b2a95-5d93-4155-b8a9-a721b9fa9714?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is one of the many members of Congress who have also warned about Smithfield and China's control over the U.S. food supply, stating: _" From purchasing fields and pastures to gobbling up companies like Smithfield, Chinese influence in American agriculture means that China's needs, not America's, come first."_
Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman John Boozman has also [said](https://substack.com/redirect/37633f6f-8741-4039-9a32-be9cdfc90d5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "The Chinese Communist Party clearly wants to supplant our country's influence and leadership in every area, including agriculture."
"We must not fall asleep at the switch and give China an opening to exploit," Boozman said.
Now, he must prove he means it.
Boozman's Farm Bill is set to be voted on again in the Senate Agriculture Committee on September 15. It failed last month in a 10-11 vote. Hinson and Ernst's CCP-friendly SOB Act was not included in the bill, but could still be added if American voters don't call their representatives and demand that it not be included in the Farm Bill.

A claim by Dr. Kimberly Biss, a St. Petersburg, Florida OB-GYN who has practiced since 1998, is recirculating after Sens. Rand Paul and Ron Johnson released a trove of Dr. Anthony Fauci's 2021 text messages. Biss first described her experience publicly in October 2023, at a Florida roundtable and in interviews; her figures spread widely again in August 2026.
Biss says her practice averaged a 4% monthly miscarriage rate in 2020 -- a year with no COVID vaccination and record pregnancies and deliveries. In November 2021, her biller flagged eight miscarriages in a month with 20 newly registered pregnant patients. She says the rate doubled to 8% in 2021, doubled again to 15-16% in 2022, and reached 30% by early 2023 -- numbers she had "never seen." Roughly 65% of her pregnant patients were vaccinated, about 80% with Pfizer, she says, and hypertensive disorders such as preeclampsia and postpartum hemorrhage -- requiring transfusions -- also rose after 2021.
The Fauci texts, released August 10, 2026, came from more than 34,000 messages recovered from his government phone. On January 25, 2021, Fauci told Surgeon General Vivek Murthy and CDC Director Rochelle Walensky that post-injection fevers "theoretically could be associated with miscarriage in the 1st trimester"; both called it a "good point." The next day, he texted that 10,000-plus vaccinated pregnant women had shown "no issues" and animal studies had raised no red flags -- language fact-checkers note matched his public statements at the time, though he did not publicly mention the fever caveat.
Federal agencies and large peer-reviewed studies, including CDC v-safe data covering tens of thousands of pregnancies, have found no elevated miscarriage risk from COVID vaccination; losses among completed pregnancies ran around 13%, within the 10-20% background range. Fact-checkers at FactCheck.org, PolitiFact, and AFP note Biss's figures are unreviewed, single-practice tallies, and that counting miscarriages against a month's new patients is a flawed denominator -- her 4% baseline is itself far below typical background rates.

| | | | Peter, Billion-dollar tech companies have a massive problem on their hands. Their new artificial intelligence data centers guzzle an ungodly amount of power and water. Unsurprisingly, when they try to build these massive, noisy, polluting server farms in regular neighborhoods, local communities revolt. In just the first quarter of this year alone, at least 75 of these mega-projects were blocked by residents who refuse to watch their electricity bills spike and their resources drain. So, the administration found a loophole for their billionaire donors: **stop asking local communities and just hand over federal public lands instead.** On Wednesday, the Department of Energy announced a massive $100 billion project to allow private corporations to build a sprawling AI server campus and a 2-gigawatt natural gas power plant directly on federal land in Kentucky. That is enough gas to power 750,000 homes, dedicated entirely to a corporate server farm. [**This is a five-alarm fire for our public lands, and we need to fight back immediately. So, the administration found a loophole for their billionaire donors: stop asking local communities and just hand over federal public lands instead. On Wednesday, the Department of Energy announced a massive $100 billion project to allow private corporations to build a sprawling AI server campus and a 2-gigawatt natural gas power plant directly on federal land in Kentucky. That is enough gas to power 750,000 homes, dedicated entirely to a corporate server farm. This is not an isolated incident. They are pushing the exact same playbook in Ohio, South Carolina, and the Nevada desert. They want to build on federal lands because building on land owned by the Department of Energy or the Interior Department allows them to bypass local regulators, cut the public out of the process entirely, and skip time-consuming environmental reviews. It turns out the only real "innovation" happening here is the tech and fossil fuel lobbies figuring out how to get the government to give them our real estate to build their infrastructure. But here is where we go on the offensive. The administration is moving quickly and quietly because they know this strategy is politically toxic. They know that if the public realizes they are handing over our deserts and federal lands to build giant, gas-powered server farms, there will be hell to pay at the ballot box. We are building the rapid-response infrastructure to expose these backroom deals and turn this corporate land grab into a political death sentence for the politicians cheering it on. We just need the volume to get our message directly into their home districts. They think they can quietly turn our public lands into their own private, taxpayer-subsidized power grid. Let's make sure the people rubber-stamping this are out of a job. You take our land—we take your seat. Instead, the judge set bail at $5,000. He posted it and walked right back onto our streets. Now just weeks later, that same man is accused of shooting a 24-year-old near the West Indian Day Parade route on Monday. The victim had no prior arrests. He was just a New Yorker in the wrong place. This is not a one-off. A Post review of this judge's cases found more than half of the defendants she arraigned walked out without bail, including two charged with attempted murder.

clean_body: Friends, Here's what soft-on-crime looks like in real life. A 19-year-old was charged with attempted murder for allegedly firing a gun at a 15-year-old boy in front of a Brooklyn playground in July. Prosecutors begged the judge to keep him locked up. | Friends, Here's what soft-on-crime looks like in real life. | A 19-year-old was charged with attempted murder for allegedly firing a gun at a 15-year-old boy in front of a Brooklyn playground in July. Prosecutors begged the judge to keep him locked up. Instead, the judge set bail at $5,000. He posted it and walked right back onto our streets. Now just weeks later, that same man is accused of shooting a 24-year-old near the West Indian Day Parade route on Monday. The victim had no prior arrests. He was just a New Yorker in the wrong place. This is not a one-off. A Post review of this judge's cases found more than half of the defendants she arraigned walked out without bail, including two charged with attempted murder. I am the only member of Congress from New York City fighting to end the revolving door that puts criminals back on our streets. | Friend, we deserve courts that protect victims, not repeat criminals. | | | | | | Thank you, Nicole | Nicole for New York, PO Box 60487, Staten Island, NY 10306

Friend,

It’s here! My new book, End Property Tax Now, has officially been released.

But this is about much more than a book.

It’s about a simple question: If you have to keep paying the government every year for the right to keep your home, do you ever truly own it?

In 2025 I stood at the Capitol and proposed legislation on this very topic! And the debate took off.

In End Property Tax Now, I lay out the moral, economic, and constitutional case for eliminating and replacing property taxes — and, most importantly, a practical path for Floridians to take this issue directly to the voters.

Our mission is to get End Property Tax Now on the ballot and let the people decide.

That means we need more than readers. We need people willing to become part of the movement.

You can purchase an individual copy of the book on Amazon here:

GET THE BOOK ON AMAZON https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=hyQT3t.K_M5liyD&b=p2tah9H_mzbRJ1qX6vf9hw

https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=hyQT3t.K_M5liyD&b=uaTVebGSv4RZld7IWD53VQ

But if you believe in this mission, I’m asking you to consider doing something bigger.

We've created special sponsorship packages where you can purchase 10, 100, 250, 500 or even 1,000 books at substantial discounts, with FREE shipping and special bonuses. Put them in the hands of friends, neighbors, business owners, civic leaders, churches, organizations and anyone who believes true home ownership matters.

Even better, 100% of the profits from these book sales help fund outreach, education and signature collection as we work toward getting this initiative on the ballot.

BECOME A SPONSOR + GET BOOKS IN BULK https://clicks.aweber.com/y/ct/?l=1fqto&m=hyQT3t.K_M5liyD&b=X_TXVXAOJj9dP2PlmiVsEg

• One book can start a conversation.
• Ten books can influence a group.
• A hundred can impact a community.
• Thousands can help create a movement.

Please get the book, share the message, sign the petition, and help us give Floridians the opportunity to vote on the future of property taxes.

It’s time to turn property taxpayers into property owners.

Let’s do this!

custom_fields.mailing_source_code %}&amounts=amounts) Peter — in almost 250 years, there’s never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate. **It’s time to change that.**

I’m Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota.

I am Ojibwe and a proud member of the White Earth Nation. My family is the Wolf Clan. The mission of my clan is to never leave anyone behind — and that’s been my guiding principle.

I am the descendant of people who were forced off their land onto the White Earth reservation. I am the relative of residential boarding school survivors. I am the daughter of a man who always spoke truth to power for the good of the Anishinaabe people.

I’m thinking of my daughter — who just got her first jingle dress — and whether or not she will see Indigenous women in all parts of our government.

**Right now, there are _no_ Native voices in the US Senate. _If I win this race, we can change that._** [**It's high time that all our communities have a seat at the table. If you agree, will you pitch in $10 or whatever you can to power my campaign and Blue Amp Action and help me make history?**](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/15531?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.09_Flanagan-Native_B2_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=4&akid=3064%2E259176%2EzUct-Z) | [SPLIT $20 >>](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/15532?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.09.09_Flanagan-Native_B2_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON_RS&t=5&akid=3064%2E259176%2EzUct-Z)

My Ojibwe name means 'Speaks in a Loud and Clear Voice woman.' So I’m using that voice to call out MAGA extremism — loudly and clearly.
But I can’t do it alone. Hey folks,
The Tate brothers are getting desperate--and it's getting weird.
Their lawyer is publicly begging the Trump administration for special treatment, Andrew Tate is floating the idea of running for president, and the whole thing is starting to look like an attempt to turn serious criminal allegations into a political persecution narrative. We need to talk about what's actually happening here.
* [**00:01:50**] Why the Tate brothers' complaints about their detention don't add up--and what their lawyer appears to be asking the Trump administration to do for them.
* [**00:04:58**] Andrew Tate starts talking about becoming president. It sounds absurd until you remember we've already watched someone use politics as a shield against legal accountability.
* [**00:07:18**] Why a 2028 presidential campaign could give Tate exactly what he wants: attention, political relevance, and a ready-made story that "the system" is coming after him.
* [**00:10:07**] Tate lawyer Joe McBride's extradition argument falls apart, and we get into the misinformation and procedural games surrounding this case.
* [**00:13:19**] This is what accountability actually looks like. The process is slow and frustrating, but that doesn't mean the Tate brothers are being persecuted or denied a fair process.

This episode is about more than Andrew and Tristan Tate. It's about what happens when wealthy, influential people try to turn accountability into persecution--and when political relationships create questions about who gets protected, who gets special treatment, and who our government really works for. That's exactly why Endless Urgency keeps following these stories, even after everyone else moves on.

name: Michael Baumgartner
subject: Fresh from the Trail: This week's campaign update!
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Vote Baumgartner for Congress | www
body:
Painting it Red all across Eastern Washington!

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/juHN0XdyrWj?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
|
---
| |
# Painting it Red in Eastern Washington!
---
|
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/JLCdmZFGddw?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| |

**Paint It Red** was a great success! The room was packed, the energy was electric, and Republicans from across Eastern Washington came together ready to get to work.
I was proud to welcome Congressmen Randy Fine and Abe Hamadeh as our guest speakers. Both brought an incredible message and reminded us why the stakes are so high, and why we have every reason to be optimistic about what’s ahead.
But the best part was seeing so many friends, supporters, and volunteers in one room, fired up and ready for November. The red wave is building, and you can feel it. We have an incredible team, inspiring momentum, and a lot of work ahead of us.
Let’s keep the pedal down and paint Washington **RED!**
---
|
---
| |
# Stevens County:
# Small Town, Big Spirit
# Northeast WA Fair and Parade
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ivnwZ8yvQVu?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| |

Team Baumgartner was out in force at the Northeast Washington Fair Parade in Colville and what a great day it was! We had a fantastic group of volunteers filling the streets with Team Baumgartner signs, smiles, and of course, lots and lots of candy. I’m incredibly grateful to everyone who showed up, waved signs, handed out candy, and helped make sure our campaign was well represented.
---
|
---
| |
# Walla Walla County:
# Walla Walla Fair and Frontier Days Parade
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/KcJyEmvauRl?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
| |
It was great to join Walla Walla County Sheriff Mark Crider for a fantastic evening at one of America’s best rodeos! The annual Friday feature is “Tough Enough to Wear Pink Night” in support of breast cancer awareness and early detection - in case you were wondering!
Walla Walla knows how to put on a parade—and Team Baumgartner was ready for it! We joined forces with the local Republican Party, passed out plenty of signs and enough candy to keep the kids happy. I spent a good part of the parade route high-fiving as many people as I could. The smiles, cheers, and friendly faces along the route were fantastic, and our volunteers did a great job.
It was one of those days that reminds me why I love campaigning across Eastern Washington: meeting people face-to-face, and enjoying the communities I’m working to represent in Congress.
Walla Walla brought the energy, and Team Baumgartner brought the candy.
Thank you for all the support, Walla Walla!
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/8ztDfjJ6ywr?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
|
---
|
---
| |
# Adams County:
# Wheatland Community Fair and Parade
---
|
---
| |
Team Baumgartner had a great crew out in Ritzville for the day, and our volunteers brought plenty of enthusiasm to the streets. We waved, greeted neighbors, passed out signs and candy, and enjoyed every minute of being part of the community. I’m always grateful for the people who take time out of their day to come out, support the campaign, and help us bring the message of Eastern Washington to every corner of the district. Ritzville showed us once again that small towns have big spirit!
---
|
---
|
---
| |
# Asotin County:
# Gathering with Supporters
---
|
---
| |
My team and I had a great time meeting with supporters in Clarkston bright and early last week. I’m grateful to everyone who joined us to offer encouragement and share their ideas for our wonderful Eastern Washington! Your support is so much appreciated.
---
|
---
| |
# Garfield County:
# Meeting with Rural Voters
---
|
---
| |
I really enjoyed being back in Garfield County at the Pataha Flour Mills near Pomeroy for some great conversations with local folks, along with State Representative Mary Dye. Thank you for the warm welcome!
---
|
---
| |
# Letter to the Editor
---
| |

Thank you to Spokane resident Jan Grayhek for her letter in the August 25th _Spokesman Review_ :

**Support Baumgartner** In response to a letter published on Aug. 18 regarding “Baumgartner’s fiscal Insanity,” there’s another side that most people are unaware of because they don’t know all the facts. The “One Big Beautiful Bill” is an amazing piece of legislation that, to this day, is unrealized for all the good it contains. If everyone would take the time to research what’s in this bill, they would know otherwise.Congressman Baumgartner wants fiscal responsibility for our country, but he alone cannot pass legislation to make the necessary cuts in our budget. Spending is the problem and until both sides of Congress can agree on spending cuts, nothing will change.
[_Read the full letter_](https://us.list-manage.com/iS1vs22SPce?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)
If you want to write a letter and would like more information about how to do that, please [get in touch](mailto:stephanie@votebaumgartner.com?subject=Letter%20to%20the%20Editor&body=)!
---
|
---

If you have a couple of hours to spare, please reach out to us! Visit our [**website**](https://us.list-manage.com/O_SqFPS37yz?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)**** to sign up now for opportunities, from attending parades or knocking on doors, to making phone calls or writing letters.**Upcoming Events** Team Baumgartner is on the move across Eastern Washington, connecting with neighbors and celebrating traditions that make our communities strong. Here is where you can find us next:
**Saturday September 12:** Sprague Days Parade 11 am: Flags up, high-fives ready, and smiles on full blast as we parade through Sprague. Come join us!
**Saturday September 12: **Columbia County Fair: Come by the Republican table at the fair! We’d love some company and you can grab a sign too.
**Saturday September 12: **Spokane County Interstate Fair: Come by the Republican table at the fair! We’d love some company and you can grab a sign too.**Saturday September 19:** Odessa Deutschesfest Parade: Break out the lederhosen and meet us in Odessa for brats, bier, and a whole lot of gemütlichkeitas as we roll through town. Come wave and grab a sign![T](https://us.list-manage.com/tUaCCISDR8V?e=5a45b9550e&c2id=b2f1dd870633a757190c0f1edbcab238)hank you for all your encouragement and support! -Michael

I've been given the opportunity to attend the **United Nations Climate Change Study Programme in Geneva, Switzerland,** an intensive, in-person program bringing together just **30 participants** for direct engagement with UN agencies, international organizations and the people shaping global climate policy on the even of this year's [COP31 conference in Turkiye.](https://substack.com/redirect/d5e5537a-78d6-40b8-a2ec-36b10112378a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And I need to raise the first **$3,000 as soon as possible** to secure my place and get the visa process moving.
[Click now to donate!](https://substack.com/redirect/00252e76-7072-472c-b09e-58cb23b5cf67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Long before most people knew my name because of COVID, I was a climate and disaster scientist.
I studied hurricanes and climate extremes at LSU, contributed to the National Climate Assessment, modeled sea-level rise and future hurricane scenarios for Louisiana's coastal planning, worked with Indigenous communities confronting climate change and land loss, and built my career around the place where **science, disasters, policy and people collide**.
Moments from my work in climate research, community partnerships, and advocacy.
Since then, that work has expanded into public health, government accountability, journalism, science communication and international climate work.
Now I have a chance to bring all of those threads together in Geneva.
The UNITAR program includes direct engagement with experts from across the UN and International Geneva; workshops on climate mitigation, adaptation, resilience, sustainable finance and the just transition; institutional visits; and, critically, opportunities to build relationships with people working throughout the international climate system.
**Only 30 people are chosen to go.**
That's why I'm asking for help now.
**The total goal: $8,000**
The **first $3,000 is urgent** : that's the program fee, which I need to pay so I can secure my place and move forward with the Swiss visa process.
[Click now to donate!](https://substack.com/redirect/00252e76-7072-472c-b09e-58cb23b5cf67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The remaining funds will cover airfare to Geneva, lodging, local transportation, meals, travel insurance, visa-related expenses and the other costs of spending a week working in one of the world's most important centers of climate science and diplomacy.
If enough people give $5, $10 or $25, we can get there.
But I'm also looking for **larger donors and organizational sponsors** who believe that independent scientists and science communicators should have a seat in the rooms where global climate policy is being shaped. Sponsorship support can help cover the program itself, travel, lodging or the entire trip.
This is more than five days in Geneva. It's access to institutions, experts and relationships that could shape what I do next -- and knowledge, interviews, reporting and connections that I can bring back and share with all of you.
I've spent my career trying to make science accessible to the people most affected by it, whether that meant hurricane risk on the Gulf Coast, public-health data during a pandemic, or climate reporting today.
**Help me take that work to the United Nations.**
**We need $3,000 immediately to secure the program and visa, and $8,000 to get me all the way to Geneva.**
Every donation gets us closer. Every share helps. And if you or your organization is interested in sponsoring this trip, please reach out directly.
[Click now to donate!](https://substack.com/redirect/00252e76-7072-472c-b09e-58cb23b5cf67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

name: Forward Party
subject: All Eyes on Senator Buss and Utah SD11
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Emily Buss is now the Republican candidate's only opponent.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
Emily Buss first set out to serve her local community, figuring she would start small, running as an underdog for city council — and nearly won. So when the Utah Forward Party held a first-of-its-kind, ranked choice special election to fill a vacancy in Utah Senate District 11, Emily decided to step up. Her community-first focus made her a perfect fit, and she won — and did so under the Forward Party banner. Once again, we have [endorsed](https://www.forwardparty.com/media/press_release/forward-party-announces-21-candidates-across-utah-as-two-party-system-buckles/?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_117a&n=1) Senator Buss (along with other Forwardist candidates in the state last week). **Fight Night in Utah** The stakes for Senator Buss’ reelection bid got even higher when her Democratic counterpart [withdrew](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=-gb2ihFF5WJvyzjmUm1LHooym3c4vAqN7JTx97dnnerpYct_tZU2G8Yf3Y6EZDS3ephlkEjl0ur0iEqI3YLlnM2C9q1jC9aJEHr6y-eJeys&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_117a&n=2) from the SD11 race, leaving Buss in a head-to-head matchup against Republican challenger Brooks Benson. This raises the stakes and introduces a new moment and opportunity for an independent candidate, running for reelection as an incumbent. Winning would allow Senator Buss to continue to serve as the highest ranking Forwardist in all of the United States. **Straight Down the Middle** Senator Buss’ story gets even more interesting. As recounted by a series of [posts](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=2X1n4M6G0-hjmnAFsRUnQ8vkeX-Me9Shhv5qHoUL3CDD1aZLYERLOtWdCPqH58X_KZUHcVEv7WcP7qpg2UMYH1ZyTBuzb5nCKeMLQi5mkR0&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_117a&n=3) on X, Senator Buss is also delivering on the promise of independent governance, with a voting record reflective of an ideology score landing smack dab in the middle of her Utahn state legislative colleagues. Plainly stated, Senator Buss isn’t voting a party line or playing a character on the stage of partisan politics. She’s voting for the needs and desires of her constituents — serving them the way representative government has always been intended to work.
* * *
November 3rd is 55 days away. The Forward Party has endorsed candidates on the ballot in South Carolina, California, Ohio, Montana, New York, Idaho, South Dakota, Colorado, Minnesota, Utah, and others across the country. Every one of them is evidence of the same thing: good representation does not require a party. It requires the right person.
---
---
---

This first week, we will have an impressive group of Forward candidates running in different states at different levels of office, on Forward ballot lines. Check out the line-up below:
* [Celeste Landry](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=WO2HVQgNb817Jo2zwbQSnz5X8LXbc4ZO5WLXitwFvZo&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_117a&n=5) — Secretary of State, Colorado
* [Jay Reeves](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=HzrZM8hVAwoS6IFX1cuAe-R_MR4hunJmMXu-YXYl7nQ&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_117a&n=6) — State Auditor, Minnesota
* [Monique Doward](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=Vovs6xFfL7F-2WrgnPuWHhm7IRlyOzqpMf206p_Hb1Ny3mRYgKnqF8qD-R0WSuh_&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_117a&n=7) — State Senator, Minnesota
* [Mike Sell](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=_DqHPfihgiZgD_cLB6k0tk4aD7MtO8tl5Mp-Ig98_VQ&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_117a&n=8) — U.S. House of Representatives, Florida 4th District
* [Bob Chew](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=l0lUlBvb1yNqwnNgcncp0959pHb0qz6qqT4Q2dS-kXY&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_117a&n=9) — U.S. Senate, Colorado
* [Senator Emily Buss](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=KHrrw4pAKaPQu3IIodAf0l8kHehDkLhVr5gxse-rdBHqvb3Y-bGumHHDE1-iqUG-&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_117a&n=10) — Utah State Senate, District 11 (Incumbent)

clean_body: Let's set the record straight before the Republican midterm convention starts. | = Let's set the record straight before the Republican midterm convention starts, Peter. The RNC chairman called it "Trump-a-palooza," and he's not wrong. Over the next two days, Trump and Republican leaders will descend on Dallas with one goal: hide from the mess they've made. They'll deflect, deny, and lie because they don't want to answer for an agenda that's making life harder and more expensive for everyday Americans — all while putting Trump and his billionaire allies ahead of working families. But with hundreds of megadonors in attendance, make no mistake, Republicans are going to raise a lot of money over the next two days. = | = Here's what we can expect from the Republican midterm convention: 🎯 Republicans will spotlight their target districts, many of which are also EMILYs List Mission Majority races. Expect them to paint EMILYs List women like Christina Hines (MI-10) and Cait Conley (NY-17) as "extreme." The truth? Our women live in these districts and are facing the same challenges as their neighbors. They see firsthand what Republican policies are doing to their communities, and they have real plans to fix the damage. 🚨 Republicans will continue pushing to end vote by mail. They'll sow doubt in our democracy, laying the groundwork to suppress votes and reject election results the moment they don't like them. We've seen this playbook before, Peter — the lies, the spin, the same tired agenda repackaged as something new. Every hour Republicans spend on that stage is another hour they're building their war chest. Peter, **FIRST:** Trump signed an unconstitutional executive order attempting to unconstitutionally influence our elections and restrict who can receive a mail-in ballot. **THEN:** The Supreme Court allowed his administration to move forward, greenlighting interference in the upcoming midterm elections. **NOW:** A Postal Service whistleblower says the USPS has been secretly rushing to build a “risky and haphazard” system to implement Trump’s plan, even as its legality remains unresolved. The consequences, they add, could be “catastrophic.” According to the whistleblower, one barcode that fails to scan could jeopardize a batch containing tens of thousands of ballots. Millions of Americans could potentially receive their ballots late—or not at all. Mail-in voting reduces barriers for older adults, military members, rural and tribal communities, voters of color, and voters with disabilities. Trump’s plan threatens to disenfranchise millions of Americans who depend on it. clean_body: Before the Republican Midterm Convention in Dallas, I'm finalizing the national roster of verified conservatives. Your name is missing. | Fellow Conservative, Before the Republican Party's first-ever Midterm Convention opens in Dallas, I am doing something I have never done before. I am taking the roll. As Senate majority leader, it is my job to know exactly where this majority stands before we walk into that arena. Every verified conservative. Every confirmed Republican. Every patriot who wants their name on the record before the most important midterm election of our lifetimes. I want to be direct with you. This isn't a fundraising pitch. It's a roll call. And in 30 years of public service, I have learned that the senators who walk into a fight knowing exactly who is behind them are the ones who win it. The Democrats have their list. They have been building it since the night of the 2024 elections. They know which precincts they need, which voters they have to move, and which seats they have to flip to take the majority from Republicans. I am in this fight every single day. We’re excited to announce that we’ve endorsed Governor Tina Kotek for re-election in the upcoming general election! As the Trump Administration rolls back environmental protections and attacks our public lands, it’s more important than ever to elect state leaders who will protect Oregon’s climate and environment. Governor Kotek is one of many leaders who have already been pushing back to protect Oregonians, and OLCV is excited to endorse all of them! Due to Trump’s recent attacks on vote-by-mail, I’m sure some of you are worried about voting this election. I want to assure you that despite Trump’s Executive Order, **nothing changes for voters in this election.** States, not the federal government or USPS, run elections according to the U.S. Constitution. States and local election officials will continue administering elections, and the Postal Service remains a safe and reliable way to cast your ballot. Operational changes at the Postal Service may cause mail delays, so please vote as early as possible if you vote by mail. **If you plan to return your ballot by mail, it’s best to do so as early as possible.** To vote in this year’s election, be sure that you’re registered to vote by the voter registration deadline on Tuesday, October 13th – which you can do by [clicking here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138870705/645472082/-336827175?lang=en&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMxYjdkMDFiLTZlYWMtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOTMzYiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=5pwpf7dnw_XaeVljTFuzyrnPETkmjS_hMbTp9sMgfu4=&emci=e88fac2c-a6ab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=c1b7d01b-6eac-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=2107230). If you’ve got any questions about voting this year, please check out our [2026 voter resources](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138870706/645472083/639686694?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9BVi9BVkxDVi8xLzcwODc3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImMxYjdkMDFiLTZlYWMtZjExMS05YjMzLTAwMjI0ODJhOTMzYiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=5pwpf7dnw_XaeVljTFuzyrnPETkmjS_hMbTp9sMgfu4=&emci=e88fac2c-a6ab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=c1b7d01b-6eac-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=2107230), or simply reply to this email with any questions.

| Last week, I made my first trip to Washington since June, just in time to see Congress do what the American people elected them to do: Vote to condemn socialists.
I'm joking, obviously, but apparently some of my soon-to-be colleagues are not.
They seem to think voters didn't send them to Congress to lower rents, fight for universal child care, or raise wages.
No - what voters *actually* want are strongly worded press releases with a performative vote attached. And, unsurprisingly but still disappointingly, several members of our own Democratic Party crossed over to help Republicans pass it.
Peter, I didn't run for Congress to win Mike Johnson's approval, and I'm not going to spend my time there bending the knee to his messaging votes.
While the House was busy with that, my neighbors in Queens and Brooklyn were cutting back on groceries to make rent. Those are the people I answer to. Health care, housing, a paycheck that covers the month - that's the work, and I'm looking forward to doing it alongside colleagues who feel the same way.
So here's where I could use your help: our FEC fundraising deadline is September 30th, and what we raise before then is a public record of who funds this campaign. No corporate PACs, no billionaires, just working people who want a government willing to fight alongside them.
[If you can, contribute before the deadline to help us show up in Washington exactly as fearless as we've been all along.](https://irrem7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001uz9AwTv9NR8kN8VLNgAn5MqyVwQYEjJVAtfCz1_pCfdKax0z8xJ6nIu9m50qu4WeV-zCYVYf8sjy7c8xjRgkXbTBD-oudyS5-KQSHrTnYc8j1cDwg7TwqATgeNuqP3tWV5VFOVeSx5F5E-3oEHY7gaXD6nACbepf5JZ851FHwH0kHCTT3SnvhoeXbdpa2EsQO0ryvshl0nbL84p-9WrnhHz70aCcU97F7nCDOLtXNSlmsx7UU9U_qA==&c=u9tm5huU7r00lhywyzORL39DtuKjTN61fmSF1-Eiior4gtuEwwW4uw==&ch=1qVJOgdrZh7YQXCXOaAh8Fnr4rbSrmeCQiiR9TYj4mdky1IfJw10bA==)

A few years ago, if you said an avowed socialist could be leading the Senate race in Texas, I'd have called you crazy. It's happening. In the coming weeks, we’ll have more volunteers out knocking on doors and giving out yard signs. We’ll be sending more mailers to voters and getting more information out online. And you’ll see even more of Team Kelly out on the ground across the district.

**This is the sprint we’ve been building toward all year, and we are ready to run it. **

body:
Amy just gave me a number I can't ignore

New endorsements, September events, Membership Drive, and a look ahead to November. | | | Hi Peter, September is officially underway, and we’ve got a packed month ahead at the PA WFP. We have four new endorsements to share, events happening in Philadelphia and Harrisburg, our September Membership Drive running all month long, and Election Day getting closer by the day. So, let’s get into it.
* * *
🗳️ **Meet the Newest Additions to Our WFP Slate** Our 2026 slate is growing! This month, we’re adding four more candidates to the list of PA WFP endorsements:
* **Rep. Jen Mazzocco** | PA House District 42 Jen is a longtime Pittsburgh public school teacher and union leader who was elected to the State House earlier this year after serving on Dormont Borough Council. She’s now running for a full term representing communities in Pittsburgh’s South Hills.

* **Rob Gurtcheff** | PA House District 170 Rob is a Northeast Philly native, Army veteran, and certified fraud examiner running to represent the 170th District. He served as a counterintelligence special agent in Afghanistan, Kuwait, and Iraq before returning home to Northeast Philadelphia.

* **Chris Thomas** | PA Senate District 24 Chris is a former middle school math and science teacher, community organizer, and volunteer firefighter from Perkiomenville. He’s running for State Senate in the 24th District, which includes parts of Montgomery and Berks counties.

* **Rep. Chris Deluzio** | U.S. House District 17 Chris represents Pennsylvania’s 17th Congressional District in Western PA. A Navy and Iraq War veteran and former voting rights attorney, he was first elected to Congress in 2022 and is running for another term this November.

**And we’re not done yet. More PA WFP endorsements are on the way, so keep an eye out as our 2026 slate continues to grow!** [**View the full list of PA WFP endorsements here.**](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYd6eLP33O2GRZpvuK-wGuT_Dhu582hzcqGTrbPxc1kDAshXv7arJBgop4hzANHQtSQT86XaqIlsC7IgEptTlCc6s-9V3E545N-UMCbORIC4cScqCnmJBbb3Xl36c8zIWw9EKmr3aQk0x1nkb99fO4R6tgkN4_27aM5POnTnjLg-MOo_Dj11g3vSkazWgSd6C_ufoE1ipoJ9dQkfQcBaUvu05BtjWf3-tglob9fVvj-x0cpqfD5FQON2MAL_La93mpOHvYgccdoJAZ677LE2iBA/4tw/fncpWp10TzOZWPi-UQ1fPg/h0/h001.RldERnVRbN7PHmJh7aWjXulJ7pJBYD2h69JDKUNCPNg)

_Tuesday, September 29th_ Later this month, we’re heading to Harrisburg for a Lobby Day focused on our Tax Billionaires, Fund PA campaign. 💛 **Membership Drive Month!** All September long, we’re holding our annual PA WFP Membership Drive, which means you have the whole month to become a dues-paying member of the party by signing up as a monthly sustainer. Here’s how it works: **sustaining members give $10 or more to the PA WFP each month. By making your support recurring, you’re helping power the party not just during election season, but all year long.** That steady, month-after-month support gives us the ability to plan ahead, organize members across Pennsylvania, recruit and support candidates, invest earlier in important races, and keep our work going in Harrisburg, Philadelphia, and communities across the state. **Usually, we pack our Membership Drive into just one week. clean_body: New endorsements, September events, Membership Drive, and a look ahead to November. | | | Hi Peter, September is officially underway, and we’ve got a packed month ahead at the PA WFP. We have four new endorsements to share, events happening in Philadelphia and Harrisburg, our September Membership Drive running all month long, and Election Day getting closer by the day. So, let’s get into it. 🗳️ Meet the Newest Additions to Our WFP Slate Our 2026 slate is growing! This month, we’re adding four more candidates to the list of PA WFP endorsements: Rep. Jen Mazzocco | PA House District 42 Jen is a longtime Pittsburgh public school teacher and union leader who was elected to the State House earlier this year after serving on Dormont Borough Council. She’s now running for a full term representing communities in Pittsburgh’s South Hills. Rob Gurtcheff | PA House District 170 Rob is a Northeast Philly native, Army veteran, and certified fraud examiner running to represent the 170th District. He served as a counterintelligence special agent in Afghanistan, Kuwait, and Iraq before returning home to Northeast Philadelphia. Chris Thomas | PA Senate District 24 Chris is a former middle school math and science teacher, community organizer, and volunteer firefighter from Perkiomenville. He’s running for State Senate in the 24th District, which includes parts of Montgomery and Berks counties. Rep. Chris Deluzio | U.S. House District 17 Chris represents Pennsylvania’s 17th Congressional District in Western PA. A Navy and Iraq War veteran and former voting rights attorney, he was first elected to Congress in 2022 and is running for another term this November. And we’re not done yet. More PA WFP endorsements are on the way, so keep an eye out as our 2026 slate continues to grow! Upcoming events: ☕ Coffee and Council Thursday, September 17th | 7:30-9:30 AM Philadelphia City Council is heading back into session, and we’re kicking things off with coffee and a conversation about what to expect at City Hall. 🏛️ Harrisburg Lobby Day Tuesday, September 29th Later this month, we’re heading to Harrisburg for a Lobby Day focused on our Tax Billionaires, Fund PA campaign. On Tuesday, September 29th, PA WFP members and supporters will meet directly with state lawmakers to talk about the campaign and the push to make it part of the conversation around Pennsylvania’s 2027–2028 state budget. Lobby Day runs from 7:30 am to 5:00 pm. Participants will also be required to attend a virtual training beforehand, with sessions available on September 22nd or September 28th from 6:00 to 7:30 pm. 💛 Membership Drive Month! All September long, we’re holding our annual PA WFP Membership Drive, which means you have the whole month to become a dues-paying member of the party by signing up as a monthly sustainer. Here’s how it works: sustaining members give $10 or more to the PA WFP each month. By making your support recurring, you’re helping power the party not just during election season, but all year long. That steady, month-after-month support gives us the ability to plan ahead, organize members across Pennsylvania, recruit and support candidates, invest earlier in important races, and keep our work going in Harrisburg, Philadelphia, and communities across the state. Usually, we pack our Membership Drive into just one week. This year, we’re making it all month long, so you have plenty of time to sign up. And as a little thank-you: 🌟 Become a sustaining member with a recurring gift of $10 or more per month, and we’ll send you an exclusive PA WFP magnet. 🌟 Prefer to make a one-time contribution? Give any amount during the Membership Drive, and we’ll send you a PA WFP sticker. The drive runs through September 30th, so you’ve got all month to become a sustaining member and get a little PA WFP swag in the process. 💛 👀 And then comes November Pennsylvania’s General Election is Tuesday, November 3rd, which means we’re heading into the final stretch of the 2026 election. In the weeks ahead, we’ll have more endorsements to announce, more ways to volunteer, more events, and plenty more to share as Election Day gets closer. Today is Primary Election Day in my home state of Rhode Island. There's one race in particular that I think progressives across the country should have on their radar--David Morales's campaign for mayor of Providence. For _[The Nation](https://substack.com/redirect/829bb304-bb1a-4d15-b2e1-dd019d67a250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ ,__ I wrote about some lessons that leftist organizers and candidates in other small cities could learn from this race.
Thanks--and if you're in Rhode Island, don't forget to get out and vote!
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2c364909-607a-4fd0-bc28-5b9e63183d98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
When David Morales shared with me that he was planning to run for mayor of Providence, I told him I wasn't so sure it was a good idea.
It was February 2025, and we were getting beers at the Wild Colonial, a bar that seven years earlier had hosted my watch party-turned-concession speech for a primary challenge I'd run against an incumbent Democrat (Rhode Island's current governor, then-lieutenant governor). I thought we'd done close to everything right in that race, and our campaign still came up two points short. I had learned--and I emphasized this to Morales--that it is very hard to knock off a sitting incumbent in a statewide or citywide primary challenge.
I'm so glad that Morales didn't listen to me. In the year and a half since I gave that pessimistic warning, he and his team built an extraordinary campaign, based around the belief that our city has the potential to be a Providence for all. It's a message Morales repeats in nearly all his communications, and it has succeeded in putting Providence's centrist mayor, Brett Smiley, firmly on the back foot. So how did this campaign go from a long shot to, I believe, the favorite to win? And does it offer any lessons for other upstart campaigns--especially those in smaller cities like Providence that can't count on the kind of outsized national attention that often helps drive momentum in places like New York City? Here are the core principles I've identified, from my own observations as a [supporter](https://substack.com/redirect/efe511c7-05a1-4bb1-acc1-f2398b43593b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and occasional adviser to the campaign and from conversations I've had with Morales and core members of his team.
### **A Defining Contrast**
The moment I first thought "OK, David really has a shot here" was last April, when Mayor Smiley [vetoed](https://substack.com/redirect/fb6e8aa2-5749-47e8-a55c-0eee8c492ac3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) legislation passed by Providence's City Council to cap annual rent hikes at 4 percent. This rent stabilization ordinance was the culmination of years of political organizing to elect a progressive council majority and months of policy work to develop an effective regulatory framework. It was, and is, desperately needed: A recent [study](https://substack.com/redirect/6bec8905-361a-46b6-a93b-3f063bbf79ae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that Providence is the least affordable city for renters in the country. Longtime residents are getting priced out, and essentially everyone who rents--and renters comprise 59 percent of the households in the city--understands that our trajectory is simply not sustainable. So when Smiley--who has fundraised extensively from wealthy developers and landlords--vetoed the most significant-ever attempt to bring this crisis under control, Morales immediately had an answer to the question, "Why should we fire our current mayor, who hasn't had any major scandals, and replace him with you?"
Establishing such an easy-to-understand contrast is often surprisingly challenging. On most issues, an incumbent can muddy the waters. As corporate strategist Richard Berman once [put it](https://substack.com/redirect/216c85cc-6181-4af1-9f1d-87aab46699be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a presentation to fossil-fuel companies, "You get into people's mind a tie. They don't know who is right. And you win all ties because the tie basically ensures the status quo." Berman was speaking about Big Oil's use of climate denial to stall decarbonization, but the principle applies equally well to how corporate Democrats often undermine progressive challenges.
It's one thing to say--to take another issue in this race that's proven far less decisive--"The mayor hasn't stood up strongly enough against ICE." It's true, but Smiley has belatedly taken (and heavily advertised) enough anti-ICE actions, however performative, to significantly undercut this distinction. But there's no real way to muddy the waters on killing critical legislation to stabilize our out-of-control rental market, and Morales's campaign has used Smiley's veto to effectively frame the race as a challenger fighting to make Providence affordable versus an incumbent who prioritizes the interests of his corporate donors.
### **A Unified Left**
A unified left is rarely enough to build a majority on its own. But it is almost always a prerequisite for a leftist victory, necessary both to activate the needed grassroots energy and to protect against that strain of progressive narcissist, the vote-splitting spoiler candidate.
The Morales campaign has unified the left in Providence and Rhode Island to a degree I've never seen before. It is, of course, critical that Morales spent years putting in the work as a movement elected official--walking picket lines, joining protests, pushing progressive legislation. But putting in the work as an individual candidate rarely guarantees a unified left. Much depends on the organizational ecosystem in a given community.
Case in point: Back in 2023, Rhode Island's DSA chapter made a [big show](https://substack.com/redirect/d42d94c9-6dec-4ae8-9da0-00f0011b286f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of publicly unendorsing Morales, then a state representative, for voting for Rhode Island's presumptive state House speaker, a more moderate Democrat. The chapter maintained its boycott of Morales during his mayoral run, and has even [criticized](https://substack.com/redirect/deba9af2-4a18-4231-a6ef-497815a3357e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) other DSA members and leaders outside of Rhode Island who are supporting him. (Because every DSA chapter has its own local leadership, there can be vast differences in strategic approaches and capacity across chapters, as exemplified in the contrast between RI DSA and NYC DSA, which was the driving force between Zohran Mamdani's campaign). And RI DSA was only one of multiple groups that for several years steered Rhode Island's political left toward anti-majoritarian purity tests, infighting, and petty grievances. In an environment dominated by these kinds of voices, a movement campaign like the one Morales has built would not have been possible.
Fortunately, in recent years, groups like the RI DSA have been eclipsed by organizations actually working to build real power. The most important example here is Reclaim RI, a group that emerged from local Bernie 2020 organizing but came into its own--with actual staff capacity and a significant base--in the last couple years. Morales launched his campaign with Reclaim's full support. As my friend Dan Denvir, co-chair of Reclaim RI and host of _The Dig_ podcast, described: "Reclaim has been laying the groundwork for this moment since our founding in 2020. We knew there was going to be another major upsurge in left politics--we just didn't know when. But we knew that we needed to be ready to provide leadership and infrastructure when it happened. Our volunteer leadership built out a massive canvassing infrastructure to back Morales alongside our endorsed council slate through a combined, cross-canvassing operation that allowed us to boost everyone simultaneously."
Once Morales demonstrated viability, he was able to score a number of other significant endorsements--SEIU 1199NE, Unite Here, the Providence Teachers Union, the Working Families Party. But it all started with Reclaim. Its support was key to ensuring that Morales's run did not feel like some fringe effort, but rather a movement challenge, rooted in a real social base.
### **A Different Kind of Field Operation**
Morales's campaign has knocked on over [80,000 doors](https://substack.com/redirect/423f26da-5f88-4cdb-8b9e-795ae259f79a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--a larger proportion of the households in Providence than Zohran Mamdani's primary campaign knocked in New York City.
I've known Morales's field director, Jenn Steinfeld, since we met in 2010 (during a much less exciting Providence mayoral campaign). When I asked them what their approach has been to building out such an expansive grassroots operation, they named two principles.
First, Steinfeld stressed how the campaign has prioritized volunteer autonomy and empowerment in every aspect of its team-building. "Part of what's made this campaign a success is that we are letting people practice democracy. We're letting volunteers take responsibility for things. We're letting them be in charge of a canvass. We're not asking people to memorize talking points. We're asking them to tell their story about why they are here, to have conversations with their neighbors."
Steinfeld has brought this attitude into every aspect of team training. "I like to give them support, but I don't like to answer their questions for them. I like to ask them more questions or encourage them to believe in their own intuition or turn it around and say, 'Well, what do you think we should do?'"
For Steinfeld, this is partially about increasing campaign capacity, but it's also about building movement capacity for the long term. "One of my big priorities is training a next generation of leftist organizers. Making sure that they have relationships with other organizations--like the Working Families Party, like Reclaim--that can be their organizing home after this election is over."
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=214914129&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE0OTE0MTI5LCJpYXQiOjE3ODg5NzM3NzcsImV4cCI6MTc5MTU2NTc3NywiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0._oiva07vWJbML1AMIRhehPztoK6xRBxVoYwE_yP3kRk)
Steinfeld's other guiding principle for the Morales field program--which progressive campaigns too often fail to prioritize--is joy. "Yeah I wanna reach the voters," they told me. "But I wanna take care of a team. We've built an environment where we get each other's backs, where you contribute and work really hard on this campaign, but where you can also take space for the other parts of your life." Steinfeld shared an example of how this worked for them personally. "My dad has Parkinson's, and he's never seen a total eclipse. He wanted to go to Europe to see one during GOTV. My team said, 'Absolutely you should do that, we've got this.' And they did."
The Morales campaign really has exuded an aura of joy, and that hasn't been an accident. As Steinfeld said, "We're not grinding people into dust. We're channeling our joy and our energy and our passion and our rage and our fear into something that is making Providence a better place for all of us."
### **A Dominant Social Media Presence**
This is a more basic, practical observation: A critical ingredient in the Morales campaign's success has been its absolute dominance of social media.
It took me longer than it should have to recognize the extent of this domination, simply because I'm a dinosaur who's not on most social-media platforms. I'm still active on X, where Morales's footprint has been relatively light. But X has never been the place for local political engagement. That's always been Meta, and especially Instagram. And Morales has absolutely owned Instagram.
I distinctly remember when I came to understand this dynamic. I'd been in a bit of a friendly debate with Morales's campaign manager, Ben Shanahan, over a campaign mailer--a [long-form introductory letter](https://substack.com/redirect/63e58338-d4b8-4072-a88b-ae5a1e7da12d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--that I'd helped Morales draft. I'd been advocating for the letter to be sent out to a broad universe. * * *
If Morales wins tonight, the most important takeaway for leftists considering mayoral campaigns in other small or mid-sized cities may be that the criteria for a run shouldn't focus on the opposition. If you'd have asked me last year if Brett Smiley was a particularly vulnerable incumbent, I'd have said absolutely not. Sure, he wasn't super well-liked, but he didn't have any major scandals, and he was sitting on well over a million dollars--a preposterous amount of campaign cash for the mayor of a city like Providence. We’re in the home stretch of the election.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=8812%2E582294%2EleOOXS)
Team,
We’ve officially entered the General Election, and we have our opponent: **Donald Trump’s hand-picked nominee, John Sununu.**
He’s got the name of a powerful political dynasty, the support of the entire GOP, and a super PAC with an $800 million war chest ready to go. I’m depending on this grassroots team to be able to compete.
**[Back-to-back polls show us down in this battleground Senate race for the first time this entire campaign. Will you chip in $50, $25, $5, or any amount so we can retake the lead before it’s too late?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260909_1.eNboKs&refcode=em20260909-1&t=2&akid=8812%2E582294%2EleOOXS)**
If you ask me, John Sununu’s decades-long record is nothing to be proud of. In case you need a refresher:
* **He holds Donald Trump’s personal endorsement:** National Republicans and Trump are backing Sununu because they know he’ll line up behind their extreme agenda in the Senate.
* **His name is in the Epstein files, and he was caught lying about it:** Reports recently exposed that Sununu flat-out lied about a trip to an elite event in Doha, Qatar – the exact same event where Jeffrey Epstein noted that “John Sununu, has good stories.” Granite Staters still haven’t gotten a straight answer on what else he’s hiding.
* **He sold out Granite Staters to Wall Street & Big Pharma:** In Congress Sununu voted against lowering prescription drug costs, then invested in Big Pharma after leaving office. He also voted for Wall Street’s $700 billion bailout, and then he got paid by a company propped up by the funds.
* **He was a lead architect of plans to privatize Social Security:** In Washington Sununu spearheaded efforts to gamble seniors’ hard-earned benefits on the stock market while Wall Street profited.
* **He’s backed by right-wing dark money:** Super PACs are already pouring tens of millions into New Hampshire to prop up his campaign.
* **He can’t be trusted to look out for New Hampshire:** While Granite Staters are paying for sky-high gas and grocery prices, John Sununu is profiting.

There’s a clear contrast – but with just 55 days until Election Day, we’re running out of time to make that case to the voters. I need your help to do it.
If we fail, there’s no path to a Democratic Senate majority. **But if we succeed, we can prove that New Hampshire is not for sale** – especially not to somebody like John Sununu and the MAGA billionaires bankrolling his campaign.
**[So please, now is the time: Rush a $5 contribution to our campaign so we can start this final phase of the election as strongly as possible and keep New Hampshire blue.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260909_1.eNboKs&refcode=em20260909-1&t=3&akid=8812%2E582294%2EleOOXS)**

Chris Pappas

body:
Republican candidate for Congress, Eric Conroy launches his second ad ahead of the general election in November.

| | | | | [|

| | | | | |

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
** September 9, 2026**Republican Eric Conroy Launches AI Bio Ad Highlighting Military, CIA Career****CINCINNATI, OH** — Republican candidate for Congress, Eric Conroy launches his second ad ahead of the general election in November. “[Spy Novel](https://us.list-manage.com/914zjYRjsnz?e=3f87e575ad&c2id=83ae238fa0f76420f201b2501cd8e566)” highlights Eric Conroy’s journey from Elder High School on Cincinnati’s West Side to the Air Force Academy, where he graduated with honors. He then served in the Air Force, where he led special operations forces, and in the CIA, where he recruited assets, hunted down terrorists, and kept America safe. Eric Conroy has always been on duty and wants to continue his life of service by representing Southwest Ohio in Congress. _“I have spent my life serving this country. I was “always on duty.” I am running for Congress to continue my life of service and be “on duty” for Southwest Ohio. In comparison, Greg Landsman has always been on duty to serve himself: tripling his net worth since elected to office by trading stocks, pretending to be a moderate while appeasing far-left progressives in California and New York, and continuing his career as a professional politician. It’s time for the people of Cincinnati to come first; I look forward to being “on duty” again when I am elected in November,” Conroy said_**Transcript:** Eric Conroy’s story reads like a spy novel.His steel was forged under the Friday night lights at Elder High and in the mud of the Air Force Academy, graduating with honors and rising to captain. Eric Conroy commanded special operations forces overseas. After joining the CIA, Conroy recruited assets in warzones and hunted down terrorists to protect our country. In the snows of Eastern Europe, Conroy ran high-stakes operations in Russia’s backyard, working clandestinely, gathering intelligence, keeping America safe. ‘I was always on duty’. Raised in a West Side family, a true son of Cincinnati, Eric Conroy learned the lessons of the greatest generation from his grandfather. ‘Service Before Self, always’. The crooks and career politicians in Congress better wake up. Change is coming in November. I’m Eric Conroy and I approve this message. **###**

This is not about “election integrity.” This is about control. States — not the White House — are responsible for administering elections. # ['I'm the house now': Bessent sizes the long-bond rescue](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Treasury is due Wednesday around 11 a.m. ET to size a long-dated bond buyback after Secretary Scott Bessent told currency traders, **["I am the house now,"](https://substack.com/redirect/e6471fa8-5b4a-4dad-bd64-ed9dc0eee119?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and **[dared them to bet against him.](https://substack.com/redirect/6e5bf43f-9f73-4128-83ae-007d59951c91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Street eyes larger start:** The Aug. 19 plan set a $4 billion floor, double the prior cap, for 10-to-20-year and 20-to-30-year notes. Wrightson ICAP sees $5 billion to $6 billion as the likely start.
* **Yen buys protect Treasurys:** Bessent said yen intervention **[gives Treasury asymmetric insight into the Bank of Japan.](https://substack.com/redirect/e6471fa8-5b4a-4dad-bd64-ed9dc0eee119?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** The U.S. bought yen for the first time in 3 decades so Japan would not sell Treasurys.

* **Debt pile still climbing:** Japan holds $1.1 trillion of Treasurys. U.S. debt has passed $40 trillion, the deficit is headed past $2 trillion, and the 10-year yield is up about 10 basis points.
* **Funds target cheaper yen:** Hedge funds bought options targeting dollar-yen below 150 by year-end, some to 140. Stanley Druckenmiller called the buyback expansion a price-management mistake.

# [Bessent's Operation Outcast sweep cuts Iran off from the sky](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Treasury Department on Tuesday **[sanctioned 36 aviation-linked targets,](https://substack.com/redirect/21a9e83e-7889-4a49-9e05-2c0e634f89ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/21a9e83e-7889-4a49-9e05-2c0e634f89ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)including 27 Iranian carriers, under Operation Economic Outcast, accusing Tehran of using commercial fleets to move weapons, personnel, and illicit cargo.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Bessent issues cutoff warning:** Scott Bessent said Treasury followed through on promised consequences for Iran's financial lifelines and warned counterparties of the newly sanctioned airlines they risk being cut from the global financial system.
* **IRGC uses commercial fleets:** Officials said the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps uses ostensibly private carriers **[such as Mahan Air](https://substack.com/redirect/a232b36b-f522-44c4-8e6e-a3d718ad018b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/a232b36b-f522-44c4-8e6e-a3d718ad018b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)to procure and transport weapons and to ferry personnel for the regime.
* **Front companies targeted too:** Treasury also targeted covert front companies, foreign intermediaries, and transshipment routes used to obtain U.S.-origin aircraft, including UAE-based ECT Aviation Support and Turkey-based Sky Phoenix.
* **Aging Mahan jets persist:** Turkey's S Sistem was cited for moving UAV components and industrial equipment for Mahan Air. Mahan, first sanctioned in 2011, still flies about 3 dozen aging Boeings and Airbuses.

* * *
* * *
# [AI giants just borrowed $500 billion as cash flow went red](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Hyperscaler capital spending **[is expected to near $1 trillion this year](https://substack.com/redirect/3ff54ae5-73a6-49e9-8137-5af120a8d594?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and top that in 2027, as most of those firms turn free-cash-flow negative and fund data centers with a wave of debt.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **On and off books:** ZeroHedge said the AI buildout has produced a deluge of debt issuance both on and off balance sheet to fund those obligations.
* **Off-sheet pile jumps:** A linked ZeroHedge analysis put off-balance-sheet AI debt at $3.1 trillion, up $1.3 trillion in 3 months.
* **Returns look capped now:** The site said an onslaught of Chinese open-weight models guarantees that returns on the AI trade will never meet investor bogeys.
* **Debt competes with Treasurys:** JPMorgan's Michael Cembalest, cited in the piece, echoed the warning that hyperscaler debt is now competing with demand for U.S. Treasurys.

# [AGI is here, Huang says. 400K GPUs incoming](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said **["AGI has arrived"](https://substack.com/redirect/8a9587e8-7a62-4267-8e4c-f8ea5c0284df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after OpenAI unveiled GPT-6 Astra, as **[Barron's argued](https://substack.com/redirect/1f024ab3-4636-4836-85da-2db9119e400e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Qualcomm's decade-long Amazon chip pact still leaves Nvidia firmly on top.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Huang cites Astra scale:** Huang wrote on X that Astra was trained on about 100K+ Nvidia Grace Blackwell NVLink72 systems, with 400K more GPUs coming online next.
* **Competing AGI tests differ:** OpenAI defines AGI as highly autonomous systems that outperform humans at most economically valuable work. Huang's bar is top-tier scores on professional certifications and tests.
* **Amazon deal size lags:** Qualcomm's Amazon deal is for up to $60 billion over a decade. Qualcomm kept a $15 billion fiscal 2029 data-center goal; Nvidia booked $89 billion in data-center revenue last quarter.
* **Inference not training fight:** Qualcomm issued a purchase-tied warrant and is targeting inference. Nvidia gave up no equity for Amazon's extra 2 million chips over 2 years.

# [Google drops $15B on Finland and locks the power](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Google said Wednesday it will invest at least **[13 billion euros](https://substack.com/redirect/549f5fc5-402a-410a-92e3-24544dff0e83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** ($15.1 billion) in[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/629bf1c4-a737-49c7-be77-98b91469209c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Finnish AI infrastructure through 2028,](https://substack.com/redirect/629bf1c4-a737-49c7-be77-98b91469209c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** its largest single European outlay, and signed a 22-year Fortum power deal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Four Finnish sites named:** The WSJ said the money funds data centers and other infrastructure in 2027 and 2028 across Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos, and Vaala, plus clean energy, nature, and community funds.
* **Fortum power deal lifts:** Google signed a 22-year life-extension power purchase agreement with Fortum. The utility's stock jumped 11%. Google will also study new business models for potential nuclear reactors at Loviisa.
* **Porat frames Finland roots:** Ruth Porat called it Google's largest single European investment, after more than 15 years in Finland, pairing infrastructure with new energy capacity, grid work, and affordability efforts.
* **Texas of Europe talk:** Lawyer Matti Lajunen said Finland is being called the Texas of Europe. CNBC noted Pure DC, Arcem, Nebius, and TikTok projects, and Google's $40 billion Texas plan through 2027.
