# [Meta just gave an AI the keys to your inbox](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meta on Tuesday rolled out Muse, **[a personal AI agent](https://substack.com/redirect/77c6c024-92dc-4aae-9dd4-ed16ce82fa0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that can autonomously send emails, book travel, sell a car, and lower a bill, running each agent on its own virtual machine.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **OpenClaw-style access model:** Muse is modeled on the open-source agent OpenClaw and can tap email, calendar, payments, health, shopping, and smart-home apps the user chooses and can revoke.
* **Works after app closes:** Each agent runs on a cloud virtual machine so it can keep working in the background, opening browsers, filling forms, and negotiating, then pause for approval before sending or buying.
* **Remembers one mention only:** Meta said Muse can recall preferences mentioned once, such as turning an Instagram recipe reel into a grocery list and a dinner-party menu that accounts for friends' diets.
* **Delayed for safety bar:** VP Vishal Shah said Meta held the April launch to clear safety, security, and privacy bars. A later Confidential VM will encrypt data so only the user holds the keys.

* * *
* * *
# [OpenAI adds Samsung as Nvidia's next problem](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
OpenAI said Wednesday it is **[deepening semiconductor and enterprise AI work with Samsung Electronics,](https://substack.com/redirect/9575fb38-f088-493f-ac92-d54611ebb4e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** citing joint next-generation chip research as ChatGPT Enterprise use in South Korea jumped about 28-fold.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0474f87e-ab8d-4c0c-8abd-34565a534fca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Seoul chip briefing lands:** Harrison Kim, general manager of OpenAI Korea, said joint production and research on next-generation chips is where the firms have made the most progress, without giving further detail.
* **Giant ChatGPT deployment cited:** Kim called Samsung one of the largest-scale ChatGPT deployments worldwide, with employees in South Korea and overseas using it across research, marketing, and sales.
* **Memory demand keeps rising:** Kim said more advanced AI hardware will keep lifting memory demand. Samsung and SK Hynix last year signed letters of intent to supply memory for OpenAI's Stargate project.
* **Jalapeno and HBM4E ship:** OpenAI unveiled Jalapeno in June with Broadcom for inference, to be made at TSMC. Samsung is shipping HBM4E samples first, used in Nvidia Rubin and Google Ironwood chips.

Friend, I just can’t stop thinking about the _long lines_ I saw recently at our local food banks; snaking down the road, and filled with hard working parents, seniors, and families who _never imagined_ they’d have to ask for help just to put dinner on the table. Lines like this shouldn’t be normal in Tennessee. But right now, this is the reality for thousands of good people. And let's be clear, this is the direct result of the cruelty being pushed by Republicans like Marsha Blackburn, who hasn't even committed to restoring the summer EBT program, leaving thousands of our neighbors scrambling. **SNAP is a vital lifeline.** When politicians chose to slash it, they knew it would hit our most vulnerable the hardest— _our kids, our seniors, and families already working around the clock just to barely scrape by._
### T**he numbers we are looking at across our state are staggering:**
* _1 in 7 children_ in Tennessee are facing hunger every single day.
* Nearly _1 in 10 seniors_ are struggling just to keep their pantries stocked.
* Grocery prices have _skyrocketed by nearly 25%_ over the last few years, pushing family budgets _past the breaking point._

No parent should ever have to make the _impossible choice_ between paying the electric bill and feeding their children. No grandparent should have to skip meals to afford their prescriptions. _**We deserve so much better than this.**_ **As your governor,_I promise to fight for the food security, economic fairness, and basic dignity every single Tennessean deserves._ **I will fully restore this program to make sure our kids aren't going hungry. We can build an economy that lifts people up _instead of leaving them waiting in line._ Everyday, we are gaining ground, but we still have a _massive fight ahead of us_ to flip this state and build a government that looks out for working families. _But we cannot do it alone_. clean_body: | Friend, I just can’t stop thinking about the long lines I saw recently at our local food banks; snaking down the road, and filled with hard working parents, seniors, and families who never imagined they’d have to ask for help just to put dinner on the table. Lines like this shouldn’t be normal in Tennessee. But right now, this is the reality for thousands of good people. And let's be clear, this is the direct result of the cruelty being pushed by Republicans like Marsha Blackburn, who hasn't even committed to restoring the summer EBT program, leaving thousands of our neighbors scrambling. SNAP is a vital lifeline. When politicians chose to slash it, they knew it would hit our most vulnerable the hardest— our kids, our seniors, and families already working around the clock just to barely scrape by. The numbers we are looking at across our state are staggering: 1 in 7 children in Tennessee are facing hunger every single day. Nearly 1 in 10 seniors are struggling just to keep their pantries stocked. Grocery prices have skyrocketed by nearly 25% over the last few years, pushing family budgets past the breaking point. No parent should ever have to make the impossible choice between paying the electric bill and feeding their children. No grandparent should have to skip meals to afford their prescriptions. We deserve so much better than this. As your governor,I promise to fight for the food security, economic fairness, and basic dignity every single Tennessean deserves. I will fully restore this program to make sure our kids aren't going hungry. We can build an economy that lifts people up instead of leaving them waiting in line. Everyday, we are gaining ground, but we still have a massive fight ahead of us to flip this state and build a government that looks out for working families. name: Caitlin Cattelino
subject: Join us for a special webinar on protecting our forests!
body:
Join Defenders public lands experts to learn more about how you can help protect our roadless areas!

Join Defenders public lands experts to learn more about how you can help protect our roadless areas!
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5992669/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5992670/38SyG9Xl)

Dear Defender,

Have you heard about the Roadless Area Conservation Rule, or “Roadless Rule?” It’s one of our country’s most important conservation policies. And it’s also in danger of being repealed!

The primary goal of the Roadless Rule is to protect some of our nation’s last remaining intact forests that provide disproportionate ecological value to wildlife. These forests are free from road construction and clearcuts and provide vital habitat for many animals, from salamanders and salmon to wolverines and grizzly bears. Even though roadless areas only make up 2% of land in the lower 48 states, they contain habitat for 57% of vulnerable terrestrial wildlife!

Unfortunately, the 45 million acres of national forest lands protected by the Roadless Rule are under attack. Last month, the Trump administration published its proposal to repeal these protections, which will open up America’s last remaining intact forests to road construction, destructive timber harvest and energy development, despite these conservation areas lacking commercial value.

Join Defenders for a webinar (https://support.defenders.org/s/5992671/38SyG9Xl) to learn more about the Roadless Rule and how you can submit a meaningful comment urging the Trump administration to not repeal this essential policy before the comment period ends!

Sign up to save your spot at our webinar!

WHAT: Protect the Roadless Rule

WHEN: Wednesday, September 16

TIME: 7:00pm ET / 6:00pm CT / 5:00pm MT / 4:00pm PT

WHERE: Live via Zoom

Register here – a zoom link will be sent to you (https://support.defenders.org/s/5992672/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5992673/38SyG9Xl)

Wildlife Defenders, like you, have the power to speak up and demand that our forests remain protected for wildlife! Repealing the Roadless Rule would put hundreds of species at greater risk of extinction, and it would deprive us of some of the last places we can go to experience the natural wonders of American forests that haven’t been carved up by roads.

With less than two weeks remaining in the comment period, now is the time to tell the Trump administration to not repeal the Roadless Rule! We look forward to seeing you on Zoom next week and working with you to protect our forests!

Hope to see you soon! (https://support.defenders.org/s/5992674/38SyG9Xl)

Caitlin Cattelino

Director of National Outreach

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

body:

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
** September 9, 2026**Republican Eric Conroy Launches AI Bio Ad Highlighting Military, CIA Career****CINCINNATI, OH** — Republican candidate for Congress, Eric Conroy launches his second ad ahead of the general election in November. “[Spy Novel](https://us.list-manage.com/3shZOiR4x3F?e=3f87e575ad&c2id=83ae238fa0f76420f201b2501cd8e566)” highlights Eric Conroy’s journey from Elder High School on Cincinnati’s West Side to the Air Force Academy, where he graduated with honors. He then served in the Air Force, where he led special operations forces, and in the CIA, where he recruited assets, hunted down terrorists, and kept America safe. Eric Conroy has always been on duty and wants to continue his life of service by representing Southwest Ohio in Congress. _“I have spent my life serving this country. I was “always on duty.” I am running for Congress to continue my life of service and be “on duty” for Southwest Ohio. In comparison, Greg Landsman has always been on duty to serve himself: tripling his net worth since elected to office by trading stocks, pretending to be a moderate while appeasing far-left progressives in California and New York, and continuing his career as a professional politician. It’s time for the people of Cincinnati to come first; I look forward to being “on duty” again when I am elected in November,” Conroy said_

---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1A998xzxqN5?e=3f87e575ad&c2id=83ae238fa0f76420f201b2501cd8e566)
| |
**Transcript:** Eric Conroy’s story reads like a spy novel.His steel was forged under the Friday night lights at Elder High and in the mud of the Air Force Academy, graduating with honors and rising to captain. Eric Conroy commanded special operations forces overseas. After joining the CIA, Conroy recruited assets in warzones and hunted down terrorists to protect our country. In the snows of Eastern Europe, Conroy ran high-stakes operations in Russia’s backyard, working clandestinely, gathering intelligence, keeping America safe. ‘I was always on duty’. Raised in a West Side family, a true son of Cincinnati, Eric Conroy learned the lessons of the greatest generation from his grandfather. ‘Service Before Self, always’. The crooks and career politicians in Congress better wake up. Change is coming in November. I’m Eric Conroy and I approve this message. **###**

body:
Five women. One moment to make history.

| [|
---](https://go.indigenouswomenleadpac.com/f/a/OlsHoCTj87zReaS6lUVIDw~~/AAUS1hA~/4yb-0G1ZSLN9QK_1AmEFTLUsCjke0RW0Yphe3e9PYdtngRydmf4mfotI2_MVpg4mzRl0QAMnNqx2BbbIiXobTtobSbuHFlHCjhqvbyR3t_tH8iJTu9548QM_d3bWzKcITugSkoW6Y4J2-cy1rxMc2g~~)
| | Peter, Something is happening this November that has never happened in American history: Three Indigenous women are running for top statewide offices in the same year. And a fourth is defending the seat where she made history in 2018. **Mary Peltola** , a Yup’ik leader and the first Alaska Native ever elected to Congress, is challenging Republican Senator Dan Sullivan and just outpolled him in Alaska’s primary. **Peggy Flanagan** , a citizen of the White Earth Nation, won her primary by roughly 20 points. If she wins in November, she’ll be the first Native American woman ever to serve in the U.S. Senate. **Deb Haaland** , a citizen of Laguna Pueblo and the first Native American Cabinet secretary, won her primary with more than 70% of the vote. She would be the first Native American woman ever elected governor. **Sharice Davids** , a citizen of the Ho-Chunk Nation and one of the first two Native American women ever elected to Congress, is defending her Kansas seat after winning her primary with 83%. **Claire Valdez,** a citizen of the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo Nation and a union organizer serving in the New York State Assembly, won her primary in New York’s 7th District this June — and is now poised to grow Indigenous representation in Congress. Here’s the thing: all five are tied or ahead in their races. But leading a poll isn’t even remotely the same as winning on Election Day. The final stretch is the expensive part, and that’s why Indigenous Women Lead PAC exists — to close the funding gaps and make sure these women cross the finish line. Peter, it's Dinesh D'Souza.

I want to share something deeply personal with you today. Something I've never said quite this way before.

**The night before I was set to be locked away, I made a decision that changed everything about how I fight and how I've fought ever since.**

I'm not going to bury the lead: _**what I learned in that moment is the same thing I believe every patriot in this movement needs to hear right now. **_

Because what we're facing today is a threat to everything we've built — it can feel like the walls are closing in.

I know that feeling.

**And what I learned on the other side of it is something I've passed on to only a handful of people I trust most, including my son-in-law Brandon Gill who took it to Dartmouth, then took it to Washington, and uses it every single day to expose and dismantle the radical left in ways they never saw coming!**

A local sheikh gives a final prayer over the body of one of six children killed in a September 7, 2026 Israeli airstrike on the Farhat family home in Kfar Remman, in Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon that killed a total of 12 members of the family. September 8, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller.
KFAR REMMAN, Lebanon--"They are killing children. That's what they're doing," Baker Malak said, pointing to the tiny coffins being carried through the streets of the town of Kfar Remman in southern Lebanon on Tuesday. He walked alongside hundreds of mourners in a funeral procession to bury 12 members of a single family, half of them children, killed in an Israeli airstrike on their home a day earlier.
Nearby, mourners carried the coffin of 18-year-old paramedic Ali Shahrour, killed in a separate strike on the town the same day. The procession wound through streets scarred by months of bombardment as an Israeli drone buzzed incessantly overhead.
"When Israel sees that the Lebanese government is doing nothing, they will keep targeting children," said Malak.
Israel bombed the three-story family home of the Farhat family on Monday morning without warning, reducing the entire building to rubble, and killing three men, three women, and six children between the ages of two months and 13 years. Two other children, both eight years old, were severely wounded in the strike.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9ceb7766-810d-47d6-8d27-c2832263b1e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Farhat family home in Kfar Remman, in Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon after a September 7, 2026 Israeli airstrike killed 12 members of the family. September 8, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller.
Malak, 45, a resident of Kfar Remman, was a close friend of two brothers killed in the attack, Hassan and Hussein Farhat. Both their coffins were draped in Hezbollah flags during the funeral. Malak told Drop Site he had seen the two men 10 days before the strike. He said they were preparing their children for school after months of closures due to Israel's bombardment. In the ruins of the family home, schoolbooks, timetables and notebooks lay scattered among the ruins. The Israeli military claimed without evidence that it struck Hezbollah operatives transporting weapons in the area. Malak told Drop Site the house was a civilian home and contained no weapons. Lebanon's Health Ministry called it a "grave violation of international law."
During the burial procession, a man's voice rang out over a loudspeaker: "Stand up and say goodbye to our angels"--referring to the six children among the dead. One of the few survivors, eight-year-old Mustafa Farhat, lost his entire immediate family in the attack--his parents, siblings and grandparents. Badly wounded, he remained at Al-Najda Hospital in Nabatieh.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9803eca2-7954-4516-bf8d-df5f7a6f4d68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The funeral procession for 12 members of the Farhat family killed in a September 7 2026 Israeli airstrike on their home in Kfar Remman, in Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon. September 8, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller.
The deadly attack on the Farhat home came as part of an escalated wave of Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon that killed at least 27 people, and wounded 69 over the previous three days, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/8fad3ada-9990-44e3-9155-b63f369bdfeb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the Health Ministry. The renewed Israeli assault forced some 20,000 people to flee Nabatieh district last week alone, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/8ddcc347-707f-4983-a487-50c6f8160df0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the United Nations.
The attacks come despite a ceasefire and U.S.-brokered framework agreement signed in Washington by the governments of Israel and Lebanon on June 26. The deal requires the Lebanese Armed Forces to disarm Hezbollah before Israel withdraws from parts of the swathe of Lebanese territory it occupies. Hezbollah has rejected the deal, which has been criticized for extracting few guarantees from Israel and placing nearly all obligations on the Lebanese government. An eighth round of talks between Lebanon and Israel overseen by Washington is expected later this month.
The talks have proceeded despite nearly daily attacks by Israel on Lebanon. Between Thursday and Monday, the UN peacekeeping force in Lebanon, UNIFIL, [recorded](https://substack.com/redirect/8ddcc347-707f-4983-a487-50c6f8160df0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) no less than 528 projectiles fired by the Israeli military. On Sunday alone, it recorded 62 Israeli violations of Lebanese airspace--among the highest daily totals since June. UNIFIL also detected Israeli airstrikes inside its area of operations and north of the Litani River. And for the first time since June 21, it also detected a Hezbollah projectile on Sunday, with the group beginning to reengage in retaliatory attacks.
Asked on Tuesday whether the escalation was being driven by one side, UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric pointed to UNIFIL's observations and said: "Everyone can draw their own conclusions pretty clearly."
Malak said the continuing strikes have only deepened the conviction among many in the south that the framework agreement has failed to protect civilians. "The resistance is the only solution," he said, referring to Hezbollah. He stressed that people in Nabatieh opposed the Israeli occupation of Lebanese territory in a variety of ways: with weapons, words, or by refusing to leave their land.
Malak remained in heavily bombarded Kfar Remman throughout the war, distributing aid and food, and helping to bury the dead. "I will never leave my village," he said. "If I ever have to leave, it will be to the grave."
Since the latest phase of the war began in Lebanon on March 2, nearly 4,400 people have been killed, including more than 250 children, and over 12,400 wounded, according to the Health Ministry. Israel has also targeted health care workers and medical facilities, killing at least 135 emergency workers and attacking 17 hospitals. On Sunday, an Israeli airstrike completely destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, according to the ministry, which condemned the attack as another violation of the special protections afforded to medical facilities.
At the funeral in Kfar Remman on Tuesday, Karim Saleh, a 32-year-old paramedic with Al-Rissala Scouts-- a Lebanese youth and civil defense organization--stood beside the grave of his friend and colleague, 18-year-old paramedic Ali Shahrour who was killed in an Israeli airstrike on his car in Kfar Remman at 1 a.m. on Monday.
Saleh, Shahrour, and two other paramedics, Hadi Farhat and Hassan Hamze, had just finished work at a small restaurant they had recently opened together and Shahrour was driving them all home. Saleh was dropped off first, but shortly after he entered his home, he heard the screech of a missile tearing through the air followed by an explosion. Saleh put on his scouts vest and raced to the scene. Shahrour, Farhat, and Hamze had been struck in the car. People managed to pull out Farhat and Hamze from the burning vehicle just before it exploded. Farhat and Hamze were wounded, but Shahrour was killed.
"Every time I close my eyes I see their faces from that moment. That's why I'm trying to stay awake, so I don't close my eyes," Saleh told Drop Site, his yellow emergency worker vest stained with blood and his eyes red from tears and exhaustion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/77bcfd66-89d3-490b-a145-a71765c66783?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Daniel Sharhour (left) the father of paramedic Ali Shahrour, who was killed in a September 7, 2026 Israeli airstrike on his car in Kfar Remman, stands beside Ali's friend and colleague, Karim Saleh (right). September 8, 2026. Photo by Katrine Houmøller.
When Saleh visited Farhat in the intensive care unit in Al-Najda Hospital, Farhat's first question was "Where is Ali?" He had only just been taken off the breathing tube so that he could speak. Saleh said his friend was in shock, struggling with traumatic memories of the attack. Farhat insisted on attending his friend Shahrour's funeral Tuesday, but doctors said his condition was too serious to leave the hospital.
"I'm not going to wash their blood off this vest," Saleh said. "It makes me feel like I'll always have them by my side."
Shahrour's father, Daniel Sharhour, stood beside him. "They killed him in his own hometown. In his own car. In his own country," Daniel Sharhour said. As he spoke, his voice grew louder, drawing people around him. "I will never forgive what happened to my son. Revenge is hanging around my neck like a necklace. I will take my revenge. I'm not afraid."

Please consider becoming a paid subscriber or making a . | | ---|---|--- A local sheikh gives a final prayer over the body of one of six children killed in a September 7, 2026 Israeli airstrike on the Farhat family home in Kfar Remman, in Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon that killed a total of 12 members of the family. September 8, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller. KFAR REMMAN, Lebanon--"They are killing children. That's what they're doing," Baker Malak said, pointing to the tiny coffins being carried through the streets of the town of Kfar Remman in southern Lebanon on Tuesday. He walked alongside hundreds of mourners in a funeral procession to bury 12 members of a single family, half of them children, killed in an Israeli airstrike on their home a day earlier. Nearby, mourners carried the coffin of 18-year-old paramedic Ali Shahrour, killed in a separate strike on the town the same day. The procession wound through streets scarred by months of bombardment as an Israeli drone buzzed incessantly overhead. "When Israel sees that the Lebanese government is doing nothing, they will keep targeting children," said Malak. Israel bombed the three-story family home of the Farhat family on Monday morning without warning, reducing the entire building to rubble, and killing three men, three women, and six children between the ages of two months and 13 years. Two other children, both eight years old, were severely wounded in the strike. | | ---|---|--- The Farhat family home in Kfar Remman, in Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon after a September 7, 2026 Israeli airstrike killed 12 members of the family. September 8, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller. Malak, 45, a resident of Kfar Remman, was a close friend of two brothers killed in the attack, Hassan and Hussein Farhat. Both their coffins were draped in Hezbollah flags during the funeral. Malak told Drop Site he had seen the two men 10 days before the strike. He said they were preparing their children for school after months of closures due to Israel's bombardment. In the ruins of the family home, schoolbooks, timetables and notebooks lay scattered among the ruins. The Israeli military claimed without evidence that it struck Hezbollah operatives transporting weapons in the area. Malak told Drop Site the house was a civilian home and contained no weapons. Lebanon's Health Ministry called it a "grave violation of international law." During the burial procession, a man's voice rang out over a loudspeaker: "Stand up and say goodbye to our angels"--referring to the six children among the dead. One of the few survivors, eight-year-old Mustafa Farhat, lost his entire immediate family in the attack--his parents, siblings and grandparents. Badly wounded, he remained at Al-Najda Hospital in Nabatieh. | | ---|---|--- The funeral procession for 12 members of the Farhat family killed in a September 7 2026 Israeli airstrike on their home in Kfar Remman, in Nabatieh district, southern Lebanon. September 8, 2026. Photo by Katrine Dige Houmøller. The deadly attack on the Farhat home came as part of an escalated wave of Israeli strikes across southern Lebanon that killed at least 27 people, and wounded 69 over the previous three days, to the Health Ministry. The renewed Israeli assault forced some 20,000 people to flee Nabatieh district last week alone, to the United Nations. The attacks come despite a ceasefire and U.S.-brokered framework agreement signed in Washington by the governments of Israel and Lebanon on June 26. The deal requires the Lebanese Armed Forces to disarm Hezbollah before Israel withdraws from parts of the swathe of Lebanese territory it occupies. Hezbollah has rejected the deal, which has been criticized for extracting few guarantees from Israel and placing nearly all obligations on the Lebanese government. An eighth round of talks between Lebanon and Israel overseen by Washington is expected later this month. The talks have proceeded despite nearly daily attacks by Israel on Lebanon. Between Thursday and Monday, the UN peacekeeping force in Lebanon, UNIFIL, no less than 528 projectiles fired by the Israeli military. On Sunday alone, it recorded 62 Israeli violations of Lebanese airspace--among the highest daily totals since June. UNIFIL also detected Israeli airstrikes inside its area of operations and north of the Litani River. And for the first time since June 21, it also detected a Hezbollah projectile on Sunday, with the group beginning to reengage in retaliatory attacks. Asked on Tuesday whether the escalation was being driven by one side, UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric pointed to UNIFIL's observations and said: "Everyone can draw their own conclusions pretty clearly." Malak said the continuing strikes have only deepened the conviction among many in the south that the framework agreement has failed to protect civilians. "The resistance is the only solution," he said, referring to Hezbollah. He stressed that people in Nabatieh opposed the Israeli occupation of Lebanese territory in a variety of ways: with weapons, words, or by refusing to leave their land. Malak remained in heavily bombarded Kfar Remman throughout the war, distributing aid and food, and helping to bury the dead. "I will never leave my village," he said. "If I ever have to leave, it will be to the grave." Since the latest phase of the war began in Lebanon on March 2, nearly 4,400 people have been killed, including more than 250 children, and over 12,400 wounded, according to the Health Ministry. Israel has also targeted health care workers and medical facilities, killing at least 135 emergency workers and attacking 17 hospitals. On Sunday, an Israeli airstrike completely destroyed Ghandour Hospital in Nabatieh al-Fawqa, according to the ministry, which condemned the attack as another violation of the special protections afforded to medical facilities. At the funeral in Kfar Remman on Tuesday, Karim Saleh, a 32-year-old paramedic with Al-Rissala Scouts-- a Lebanese youth and civil defense organization--stood beside the grave of his friend and colleague, 18-year-old paramedic Ali Shahrour who was killed in an Israeli airstrike on his car in Kfar Remman at 1 a.m. on Monday. Saleh, Shahrour, and two other paramedics, Hadi Farhat and Hassan Hamze, had just finished work at a small restaurant they had recently opened together and Shahrour was driving them all home. Saleh was dropped off first, but shortly after he entered his home, he heard the screech of a missile tearing through the air followed by an explosion. Saleh put on his scouts vest and raced to the scene. Shahrour, Farhat, and Hamze had been struck in the car. People managed to pull out Farhat and Hamze from the burning vehicle just before it exploded. Farhat and Hamze were wounded, but Shahrour was killed. "Every time I close my eyes I see their faces from that moment. That's why I'm trying to stay awake, so I don't close my eyes," Saleh told Drop Site, his yellow emergency worker vest stained with blood and his eyes red from tears and exhaustion. | | ---|---|--- Daniel Sharhour (left) the father of paramedic Ali Shahrour, who was killed in a September 7, 2026 Israeli airstrike on his car in Kfar Remman, stands beside Ali's friend and colleague, Karim Saleh (right). September 8, 2026. Photo by Katrine Houmøller. When Saleh visited Farhat in the intensive care unit in Al-Najda Hospital, Farhat's first question was "Where is Ali?" He had only just been taken off the breathing tube so that he could speak. Saleh said his friend was in shock, struggling with traumatic memories of the attack. Farhat insisted on attending his friend Shahrour's funeral Tuesday, but doctors said his condition was too serious to leave the hospital. "I'm not going to wash their blood off this vest," Saleh said. "It makes me feel like I'll always have them by my side." Shahrour's father, Daniel Sharhour, stood beside him. "They killed him in his own hometown. In his own car. In his own country," Daniel Sharhour said. As he spoke, his voice grew louder, drawing people around him. "I will never forgive what happened to my son. Revenge is hanging around my neck like a necklace. I will take my revenge. I'm not afraid." | A guest post by| journalist working in the Middle East, covering war and humanitarian crises through written journalism, photography and live broadcasting. [ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20260909-61798&t=1001&akid=61798%2E1407376%2EPwrbEW ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20260909-61798&t=1002&akid=61798%2E1407376%2EPwrbEW ]Demand Justice PAC

The Supreme
Court’s "shadow docket" was supposed to be for real emergencies. But now,
it’s been weaponized.

When Trump loses in a lower court, he runs straight to the Supreme Court
to use the "shadow docket" hoping the conservative justices will bail him
out.

No hearing, no arguments, hardly any real explanation. Just a one- or
two-line order that lets him keep doing exactly what a lower court just
said he couldn't.

More often than not, it works. This is a loophole — and Trump is running
through it faster than any president before him. He hit the same number of
emergency appeals in about five months of his second term that it took the
entire Biden presidency to reach.^1

The result? Immigrants lose protections overnight. Civil servants get
pushed out with no due process. The legal limits on presidential power
quietly disappear.

This is what a captured Court looks like. Untethered from the
Constitution, no transparency, and shifting their own legal standards in
ways that make it easier for Trump and entrenched power to win.

Demand Justice PAC is exposing this scheme and building the public and
political pressure to force real reform. Ethics rules, an expanded bench,
and structural changes that end government-by-shadow-docket for good.

But exposing a rigged system takes resources. Building the pressure to
actually fix it takes more.

Friends, I have some exciting news to share: **I'm running to be Vice Chair of the House Democratic Caucus.** If we win back the majority in November — and I believe we will, thanks to the incredible enthusiasm and hard work of millions of grassroots Democrats across the country — the job of actually governing starts _immediately_ , and we have some big tasks ahead. _And I want to be in a position to help shape how Democratic leadership shows up for that moment._ It will be crucial for Democrats to be bold, united, responsive, _and_ forward-looking, and to do that, we’ll need party leadership ready to roll up our sleeves, listen to feedback, and be proactive about solutions. It’s no secret that the Democratic Party has a major branding issue right now, and a serious trust issue. However you feel about the party, these are problems elected Democrats must meaningfully address, and quickly. **We need to use our power to earn back the trust of the American people and prove that we not only have real solutions to their problems — but also the political will, courage, and strategy to deliver them.** Of course, all of that starts with WINNING this November. clean_body: | | | | = Friends, I have some exciting news to share: I'm running to be Vice Chair of the House Democratic Caucus. If we win back the majority in November — and I believe we will, thanks to the incredible enthusiasm and hard work of millions of grassroots Democrats across the country — the job of actually governing starts immediately , and we have some big tasks ahead. And I want to be in a position to help shape how Democratic leadership shows up for that moment. It will be crucial for Democrats to be bold, united, responsive, and forward-looking, and to do that, we’ll need party leadership ready to roll up our sleeves, listen to feedback, and be proactive about solutions. It’s no secret that the Democratic Party has a major branding issue right now, and a serious trust issue. However you feel about the party, these are problems elected Democrats must meaningfully address, and quickly. We need to use our power to earn back the trust of the American people and prove that we not only have real solutions to their problems — but also the political will, courage, and strategy to deliver them. Of course, all of that starts with WINNING this November. I'm proud of the work I've been doing to get there: this cycle alone, I've raised nearly $5 million for Democratic candidates and causes to help us take back the House, I've been traveling the country campaigning for our frontliners and Red to Blue candidates every chance I get, and that’s what I’ll keep doing over the next 55 days. ---
Our country's history is rife with centuries of lawmakers taking _extreme action_ to stop minority communities, especially Black communities, from voting. **2026 is no exception.** By trying to change district lines to group more voters into GOP strongholds, far-right lawmakers are rigging the maps to keep their party in power while _diluting the power of votes like yours._ The DLCC sees these rigged maps for what they are, and we’re ready to work even harder to ensure the United States can be a truly representative democracy. That work starts with strengthening Democratic power in the states this fall. body:
Episode 18 now available!| | |

---
This week's Breakthrough Hour is about one of the most dangerous things happening in the American church —silence. The culture is arguing over the Lindsay Clancy case, over life and death and justice. It's clear that America isn't suffering from a shortage of opinions; it's suffering from a shortage of truth. In this episode, I walk through what happens when the church gets comfortable proclaiming Jesus only in the spaces we control — from the famine of the word in our land, to the toll abortion takes on the women sitting in our congregations, to watching other movements and religions boldly claim the public square while Christians retreat. I share why Let Us Worship was born in 2020 and why the streets are our lane. And we just saw it again at Mt. Rushmore. A packed amphitheater under the silhouettes of four presidents, worshipers who'd driven hours to be there, and a holy rumble rising out of the Black Hills. That's what happens when the church goes outside. Darkness didn't suddenly become powerful. The light retreated. America doesn't need a quieter church — it needs a bolder one. The church has left the building, and we're not going back inside.

clean_body: Episode 18 now available!| | | | | This week's Breakthrough Hour is about one of the most dangerous things happening in the American church —silence. The culture is arguing over the Lindsay Clancy case, over life and death and justice. It's clear that America isn't suffering from a shortage of opinions; it's suffering from a shortage of truth. In this episode, I walk through what happens when the church gets comfortable proclaiming Jesus only in the spaces we control — from the famine of the word in our land, to the toll abortion takes on the women sitting in our congregations, to watching other movements and religions boldly claim the public square while Christians retreat. I share why Let Us Worship was born in 2020 and why the streets are our lane. And we just saw it again at Mt. Rushmore. A packed amphitheater under the silhouettes of four presidents, worshipers who'd driven hours to be there, and a holy rumble rising out of the Black Hills. That's what happens when the church goes outside. Darkness didn't suddenly become powerful. The light retreated. America doesn't need a quieter church — it needs a bolder one. The church has left the building, and we're not going back inside. "What happened to the Church in America?" Each week on Breakthrough Hour, we will shine a spotlight on what God is doing right now across nations, cultures, and communities! You'll hear real stories from the front lines of faith. Stories of freedom, healing, salvation, courage, and perseverance. Stories that remind us that light is still overcoming darkness, often faster than we realize and in places we don’t expect! | | | | About Sean Feucht Sean Feucht is a husband, father, worshipper, revivalist, author, recording artist, and podcaster. clean_body: Pat Ryan voted to denounce socialism in 2025. Then he reversed course. Here is exactly why. | Fellow Patriot, I have to tell you what Pat Ryan just did because it tells you everything about who he is. Congress recently voted on a resolution denouncing socialism and supporting voter ID. Pat Ryan voted no. He joined 191 House Democrats to oppose it. The resolution passed 220 to 192. Here is what makes this so outrageous. In November 2025, Pat Ryan voted yes on an almost identical resolution denouncing socialism. He was one of 85 Democrats who crossed the aisle to condemn it. The mask is off, and what changed? This time the resolution also included the SAVE America Act, requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote and photo ID to cast a ballot. The moment election integrity was attached to it Pat Ryan flipped his vote and sided with the radical left. And here is where it gets even more hypocritical. Pat Ryan owns a private financial stake in Socure, an AI company that specializes in identity verification technology - the exact same technology the resolution called for to secure our elections. Pat Ryan is betting his own money on the value of identity verification while voting against using it to protect your vote. Let me put it simply. Pat Ryan is a capitalist when he buys Tesla stock. A venture capitalist when he invests in private AI companies. A socialist when he spends your money. And a hypocrite when it comes to securing our elections. Hudson Valley families deserve a representative who protects their votes and their paychecks as aggressively as Pat Ryan protects his own portfolio. I am running to be that representative. Campaigns are tough.
There's so much work to be done in so little time, and it's all very expensive.
We set big fundraising goals for our campaign each week so that we can ramp up - not pull back on - the things that will help us win this election, but that means **the pressure is on.**
I'm hoping there's something I can say to convince you to make a donation today to help us hit this week's goal.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c2ec6b13-6fc5-4a1d-a905-30d16c4746c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
What if I told you that everyone from President Trump to Vice President Vance to Stephen Miller is personally attacking me and lying to voters about me and my values?
What if I told you that my Republican opponent dropped a new seven-figure ad buy in North Carolina and a recent poll came out showing this race statistically tied?
What if I told you that GOP dark-money super PACs are pouring close to $100 million into this race so far to halt our momentum - and Republicans say spending could reach up to $600 million?
**The GOP is coming after me so hard for one simple reason: If we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will lose our chance at taking back the Senate.**
You have the power to ensure that doesn't happen. Please: [Will you chip in $10 or even just a few bucks today](https://substack.com/redirect/c2ec6b13-6fc5-4a1d-a905-30d16c4746c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to help us keep pace with our crucial fundraising goals, fight back against the GOP's attacks and win this race?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c2ec6b13-6fc5-4a1d-a905-30d16c4746c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you,
Roy Cooper

body:
We need to start this general election on the right foot.
[](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260909-pappas.NQqcsE&refcode=em20260909-5654&%3Bamount=5&t=1&akid=5654%2E35263%2Ed4L-qN)
Hi Peter, it’s Chris Pappas.
**It’s official: I am the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate here in New Hampshire.**
I’m so grateful to every Granite Stater who put their trust in me and helped build this campaign together.
Growing up in Manchester and working alongside my family at our restaurant, I learned that you don’t get ahead just by making promises. You have to be accountable. You listen to people, work hard, and deliver.
That’s the same approach I’ve brought to Congress, and it’s why I’m running for the Senate.
I’m running to make New Hampshire more affordable for working families; protect Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid; safeguard reproductive freedom; and stand up for the small businesses that are the backbone of our communities.
**And now our general election fight against John Sununu officially begins.**
Political experts just changed this race to a Toss-up, Peter. The fact is: New Hampshire is a fiercely independent state, and this election could go either way. The country is watching, and the outcome here in New Hampshire will determine control of the U.S. Senate and what the next two years look like for millions of families across the country.
**[Peter, we are running a grassroots-powered campaign fueled by people like you. We need all hands on deck in order to keep New Hampshire blue and flip the Senate. Will you step up with $5 or whatever you can spare – split between me and Tammy Baldwin – to boost our campaign as we enter the general election?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260909-pappas.NQqcsE&amount=5&refcode=em20260909-5654&t=2&akid=5654%2E35263%2Ed4L-qN)**
**[CHIP IN TO KEEP NH BLUE](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260909-pappas.NQqcsE&amount=5&refcode=20260909-5654&t=3&akid=5654%2E35263%2Ed4L-qN)**
John Sununu has spent his career putting Washington and corporate special interests ahead of Granite Staters. While he was in Congress, he voted to give tax breaks to Big Pharma and Big Oil, and now he’s profiting off of investments in those same industries.
As we speak, national Republicans and dark-money groups are spending millions to put him back in the Senate because they know he’ll do the bidding of Trump and corporate interests, not look out for the people of New Hampshire.
**This race is a toss-up, so we need to join together right now and stay focused over the next eight weeks.**
**[Will you chip in a $5 contribution split between my campaign and Tammy Baldwin right now to help us hit the ground running to keep this seat blue?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20260909-pappas.NQqcsE&amount=5&refcode=em20260909-5654&t=4&akid=5654%2E35263%2Ed4L-qN)**

When you love New Hampshire, you don’t just talk about what makes this state special. You stand up and fight for the people who call it home.
Thank you for everything,
Chris Pappas

clean_body: | We know you’re getting lots and lots of messages from candidates running for Congress and Senate. But here’s the thing: there are thousands of under-the-radar races happening all across the country where we have a real chance to build a firewall between our communities and this Administration. Pennsylvania is one of those states. We’re just three seats away from flipping the State Senate — ending a 30+ year GOP majority in the chamber and opening the door to real climate action in a state that is all too familiar with the consequences of oil and gas pollution. = | = = Mark Pinsley - Senate District 16: Mark understands that the climate crisis is also a cost-of-living crisis. He’s fighting to bring clean, affordable energy to Pennsylvania, create good-paying jobs, and make sure corporations don’t leave working families holding the bill. And one of the biggest fights for that kind of accountability right now is the explosion of massive data centers across Pennsylvania. Mark supports a moratorium to give the state legislature time to put strong protections in place — requiring data centers to pay for necessary grid upgrades and making regulators answer to Pennsylvania families instead of utility shareholders. = Eileen Hartnett Albillar - Senate District 6: She’ll oppose fossil fuel expansion, prioritize the transition to renewable energy, and invest in public transportation. And she already has a record of protecting the places Pennsylvanians call home — helping preserve thousands of acres of open space as Clerk of Courts. = Brian Wrightson - Senate District 40: With more than 200 data centers proposed in his district, Brian is fighting for strong guardrails that protect Pennsylvanians and keep utility costs in check. He’s never taken money from corporate PACs or data center developers. His opponent, meanwhile, has accepted contributions from people connected to the very developments residents are fighting against. These three races are must-wins if we want a chance to flip the State Senate. But the stakes, and the impact, go far beyond control of one chamber. State legislatures have enormous power over whether states move toward clean energy or remain tied to fossil fuels, whether polluters are held accountable, and much more. Big Oil and dark-money groups will spend whatever it takes to protect the GOP majority. Peter,
Late last week, the Missouri Supreme Court struck down MAGA's gerrymandered map and ordered that the illegal map must NOT be used for the November midterm election.
MO Republicans appealed to the ultra-conservative US Supreme Court, hoping for favorable treatment for one of Trump's signature election rigging moves.

It’s time for Congress to put working families first.

That’s why, in Congress, I’ve supported legislation to strengthen unions, raise the minimum wage, secure paid family and medical leave, and more.
Workers deserve fair pay, good benefits, and protected rights — full stop. And you can always count on me to ensure workers and unions across our state have a strong voice down in Washington.
But to keep up this fight, I’m counting on your support. The Delaware primary is happening next Tuesday, September 15th, and once it’s over, we’ll officially know who our Republican opponent is next November.
Whoever it is, you can bet they won’t have the same commitment to unions and working people, and **I’m going to need your help to keep this seat blue.**

Sarah McBride

Peter,

subject: Should Tea Party Patriots Action Support The Dalilah Law (S.3917 / H.R. 7758)?
body:
Do you support legislation to bar states from issuing commercial driver licenses to noncitizens.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/010001a0879bb3ab-c7ab7597-b172-4d79-b71e-2f04351ac64c-000000/DwZgIgueN9BHSN9lHGjtZZ04HwjtPcGBr_80pC0Z3eI=452)Patriot–We need your input on legislation moving through Congress, and we want to know what you think before taking a position.The bill, known as "The Dalilah Law," is legislation that would bar states from issuing commercial driver's licenses to anyone who isn't a U.S. citizen, a lawful permanent resident, or the holder of certain specific work visas (E, H-2A, or H-2B).There are two versions of the bill. The Senate version, S.3917, is sponsored by Indiana Senator Jim Banks. The House version, H.R. 7758, was introduced by Kentucky Congressman Andy Barr. Both bills are currently in Committee.[_**You can read the full Senate text of the bill.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.congress.gov%2Fbill%2F119th-congress%2Fsenate-bill%2F3917%2Ftext/1/010001a0879bb3ab-c7ab7597-b172-4d79-b71e-2f04351ac64c-000000/vYZC79WdGPP9FSiIEbl647g9Nnomi63vfro6mHtkYhU=452) Commercial driver's license eligibility touches immigration enforcement, highway safety, and state authority. We know you care about all of these issues and [_**we want to hear your opinion**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fdocs.google.com%2Fforms%2Fd%2Fe%2F1FAIpQLSfGwXs1QEqPfS4lPAnswAfIYrtU2CYcRdw82OZh5JaWkjCebA%2Fviewform/1/010001a0879bb3ab-c7ab7597-b172-4d79-b71e-2f04351ac64c-000000/OE09GT-hrLLrwK7t81a1cFubFAXJsgq4GKRkiUQXuto=452).[COMPLETE MY SURVEY](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fdocs.google.com%2Fforms%2Fd%2Fe%2F1FAIpQLSfGwXs1QEqPfS4lPAnswAfIYrtU2CYcRdw82OZh5JaWkjCebA%2Fviewform/2/010001a0879bb3ab-c7ab7597-b172-4d79-b71e-2f04351ac64c-000000/ApqDwXA-1ianzeAC28AR3yyaW-WDcqOHE0FLXOc481E=452)Any concerns about the bill, or how it might play with your local organization? Should we publicly support the Dalilah Law?Your feedback directly shapes whether and how we engage on this.Thank you, as always, for being the boots on the ground for this movement.In Liberty,Jenny Beth Martin[CONTRIBUTE](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org%2Fdonate%2F/1/010001a0879bb3ab-c7ab7597-b172-4d79-b71e-2f04351ac64c-000000/wADcV1bmjTJDmMJ34XG7OzKtAPeahP9q5s740In6ddA=452) _This email list is a joint venture of the following separate organizations: Tea Party Patriots Action, Inc., Tea Party Patriots Foundation, and Tea Party Patriots Citizens Fund. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Friends,Mike Kelly has been telling Johnson County taxpayers that he **lowered spending** , passed a **“flat” budget** , and added **no new property-tax-funded employees.** Sounds great.There’s just one problem: **you have to read the fine print and understand the context.****CLAIM: “We lowered spending.”** Yes, the 2027 expenditure number is lower than the amount _budgeted_ for 2026.But why?The County’s own budget says the decrease is driven largely by **lower Wastewater SRCFP (Nelson Treatment Plant Construction Fund) going down by $35.6 million** , even while personnel and other ongoing costs continue to rise.That is very different from finding meaningful savings in the day-to-day operation of county government.**CLAIM: “No new property-tax-funded FTEs.”** Notice the wording. The County is not saying it added no employees.Budgeted staffing actually increases from **4,407.85 FTEs in 2026 to 4,426.88 in 2027** , an additional **19 positions.** They simply funded the new positions through fees, other revenue sources or reallocations instead of labeling them “property-tax funded.”**Moving the money to a different pocket does not make the spending disappear.****CLAIM: “We passed a flat budget.”** Even the County’s own September 3 press release says the total budget is **UP 0.37%.** I recognize this is being a bit of a stickler, but flat is flat - even one penny more is not a flat budget.What is actually flat is the **mill levy.** And as we have discussed before, a flat mill levy does **not** mean a flat property-tax bill.When property values rise, the County collects more money even without changing the rate. The County projected assessed valuation to increase roughly **5.1%** for 2027.In fact, at the Revenue Neutral Rate hearing, the County's own handout showed that remaining revenue neutral would mean collecting approximately **$19.8 million less in property taxes.** So let's stop playing word games.**Spending wasn't broadly cut. Staffing isn't flat. The budget isn't flat. And property-tax collections aren't flat.** Johnson County taxpayers deserve straight answers, not carefully constructed talking points.You can call it a “flat mill levy.”
You can call employees “non-property-tax funded.”
You can compare this year's budget to whichever prior number makes the chart look best.But at the end of the day, **the government is still spending more of your money.** You deserve to know the difference and hopefully will support someone who passionately believes that tax payers don’t deserve the “spin machine”.If you believe that too, I’d be grateful for your help getting that message in front of more voters.[**DONATE HERE**](https://us.list-manage.com/v9juVs7R1u3?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494) Fighting for you,
Karen Crnkovich
Candidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

| Friend,

This week, the entire Republican Party has its eyes on Texas. Our first-ever GOP Midterm Convention is happening right in Dallas, in the North Texas region I am honored to represent.

I could not be more thrilled to serve as a host! President Trump and Vice President Vance are here in North Texas, rallying the country around everything we have delivered: real tax relief, a secure border, American energy dominance, and safer streets.

Through the matching program, a $10 gift becomes $70. A $25 gift becomes $175. A $50 gift becomes $350. The money you give does not just help, it multiplies. That is how a grassroots campaign goes toe to toe with a machine that has held this office for nearly two decades. Democrat Tom DiNapoli has the incumbency, the name recognition, and the special interests. We have you. Every donation matters. That is why closing this $7k gap is the whole story right now. | New Yorkers deserve a Comptroller who protects their retirement, their tax dollars, and their future. The show's executive director and producer, Jeremy Boreing, is helping to shape one of the first great conservative cultural movements. Boreing helped found the Daily Wire in 2015, and has relentlessly advocated for conservatives to build culture instead of merely critiquing it.
"We don't make films to win the next election," Boreing told The Capitalist. "We make them because we're called to create, and in creating something that is true, good and beautiful, we can shape the affections. That's what conservatives, from Burke to Breitbart, had in mind when they've argued that culture sits upstream from politics."

* * *
* * *
Since 1960s liberalism swept America, the left has often claimed "the arts" as their own. Actors, artists, and musicians have primarily aligned themselves with the left. Conservatives have historically been driven out of the arts, but the phenomenon reached a breaking point during the 2010s and early 2020s. Cancel culture threatened the careers of stars like James Woods, Mel Gibson, and Gina Carano, who spoke out against transgender ideology or publicly defended their faith.
"If you make something rooted in truth and in the particular, then you cannot help but make a film that speaks to conservatives," Boreing told The Capitalist.
In the Trump era, audiences are eager for truth. There is a hunger for conservative media, as the success of "The Pendragon Cycle" has shown. Movies and television shows have become far more explicit. Streaming services have allowed for restricted content to become **[normalized](https://substack.com/redirect/2bbdba31-0192-4d5e-88ad-626bff152eab?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ,** and dozens of shows like "Euphoria" or "Game of Thrones" have resorted to hypersexualization, gore, and vulgarity. In response, audiences are looking for more virtuous art.
"The market for conservative consumers was never in doubt," Boreing told The Capitalist. "People have always been hungry for stories about great ideas. Inheritance, memory, fidelity. Those are some of the oldest subjects in drama, and they also happen to be among the deepest conservative concerns."
"Part of the solution also starts with conservatives being a little more generous with our own tradition," Boreing said. "We became so politically successful in the 1980s that we mistook the bumper sticker slogan for the whole of conservatism. We need to be able to recognize our ideas when they appear on screen."

* * *
* * *
"Pendragon" isn't afraid to be edgy or controversial. Its mission is to tell a story that paints a clear contrast between good and evil, between morality and wickedness, between heroes and villains. This juxtaposition is valuable because it creates tension, which isn't always comfortable. The show is far from political, but it holds fast to truth, beauty, and goodness, which are the heart of conservatism.
Boreing's brilliance lies in his decision to pursue the Fantasy genre. His choice to adapt "The Pendragon Cycle" came from a decades long love for its source material.
"I was captivated by Stephen R. Lawhead's stories when I was a teenager and then spent much of the next 25 years thinking about how to bring them on screen," Boreing told The Capitalist. "It's a more gritty form of Christianity that's taking root in a hostile world. I'm thrilled to see audiences react to it the way they have."
The success of "The Pendragon Cycle" is a call to action for young creatives. After decades of being excluded from artistic movements, "Pendragon" proves that there is an enormous audience for traditional, well-crafted art.

subject: They can’t even bother hiding it anymore

body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260909-6698-footer&t=1001&akid=6698%2E420207%2EdLEIn4 ]Pramila Jayapal

Peter,

Trump’s Homeland Security Secretary just doubled down. He is going after
immigrants whether they have a criminal record or not:

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/em20260909-dismantle-ice-petition?source=em20260909-6698&t=1002&akid=6698%2E420207%2EdLEIn4 ]A tweet from Homeland Security that quotes Markwayne Mullin on Fox
News. He says "these individuals that we're going after, I don't care if
you have a criminal background or don't have a criminal background, you
chose to break the law when you came across our border ILLEGALLY. It's our
position to hunt you down and send you back to where you came from."

They can’t even bother hiding it anymore.

While ICE insists that they’re deporting hardened criminals, Secretary of
Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin just made it clear that their goal is
to go after as many immigrants as possible– regardless of whether they
have a criminal background.

ICE is terrorizing our communities.

ICE is kidnapping and detaining people.

ICE is breaking down doors without warrants.

ICE is tearing families apart in the middle of the night.

They kill U.S. citizens in broad daylight. They snatch elderly people from
their homes. And they send our community members to countries entirely
unfamiliar to them, with no due process.

There are still families afraid to go to the grocery store for fear of
being targeted by ICE. There are still children living in constant fear
that their parents might not be there when they get home from school.

No one should have to live like this.

I want to be clear: ICE has never made our communities safer. They turn
our neighborhoods into hunting grounds and weaponize fear against the most
vulnerable communities — all to serve this administration’s cruel
authoritarian agenda.

It’s beyond past time to completely dismantle ICE. Our communities cannot
afford to wait any longer. This fight belongs to all of us,
Peter — that’s why I need you
with me on this.

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/em20260909-dismantle-ice-petition?source=em20260909-6698&t=1003&akid=6698%2E420207%2EdLEIn4 ]Can you add your name to this petition right now to demand Congress
dismantle ICE and protect our communities?

[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/sign/em20260909-dismantle-ice-petition?source=em20260909-6698&t=1004&akid=6698%2E420207%2EdLEIn4 ]Add Your Name

In solidarity,

Pramila Jayapal

Lead Story · The 2026 MapREPUBLICANS OPEN FIRST MIDTERM CONVENTION AS TRUMP HEADLINES BOTH NIGHTSWhat's Happening
* The Republican National Committee's **first-ever midterm convention** opens Wednesday at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, a two-day event the party bills as the first of its kind in American political history.
* President Trump delivers Wednesday's keynote, tentatively set for **9 p.m. ET** , and speaks again Thursday to close the convention after Vice President JD Vance's keynote — an unusual arrangement putting the president in primetime on both nights.
* RNC Chairman Joe Gruters told Fox News Digital: "We are putting the president on the ballot. That's exactly what we're doing with this midterm convention."
* Speaker Mike Johnson speaks Thursday evening. Senate Majority Leader John Thune is **absent from the released speaker list** ; a source told Fox News Digital he will be in Dallas anyway on a schedule that includes helping Senate candidates fundraise. That detail rests on an unnamed source.
* Senate candidates on the Wednesday program include Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and former RNC Chairman Michael Whatley of North Carolina. Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio and Rep. Mike Collins of Georgia are also slated to speak.

The Situation
* Republicans are defending **slim House and Senate majorities**. Fox News reported the party goes into the fall facing persistent inflation, high gas prices tied to what it described as an unpopular war with Iran, and negative approval ratings for Trump — the article did not name a pollster, sample or date for those characterizations.
* Gruters, asked about Republicans skipping the event: "There's some people in tight races, they want to stay home."
* Secretary of State Marco Rubio has largely avoided campaigning for GOP candidates this cycle and is not expected in Dallas, according to the Washington Examiner.
* In New Hampshire on Tuesday, former Sen. **John E. Sununu** won the Republican Senate primary with **69.6%** to former Massachusetts Sen. Scott Brown's **25.2%** when the Associated Press called the race at 8 p.m. with about 15% of the vote counted. He faces Rep. Chris Pappas for the seat Sen. Jeanne Shaheen is vacating.
* DNC Chairman Ken Martin called the convention a "multi-million dollar party to celebrate Trump's failing presidency." The DNC attached no dollar figure to the claim, and Fox's report did not verify one.

The PerspectiveGruters deserves credit for saying out loud what most party chairmen would bury in a memo: this is a referendum strategy, and Trump is the ballot question. It is a defensible bet, because the coalition that shows up for him does not reliably show up for a generic congressman in an off year. But a bet is not a plan, and the same nationalization that lifts turnout also hands every Democrat in a swing district a single target. Notice who is not coming to Dallas — the majority leader, the secretary of state, and, by Gruters' own admission, candidates in the tightest races. When the people closest to the fight quietly choose distance, that is data too.[Read the full story at Fox News](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_NRx3TmKyUjNZ_2a-If6mrdtr-aUKkVRYbHc-4VfA6xOlh9900CH202WY80QUBs0o6YDun69-u32K6lkMMs9jICn4Q1tF7AXtsFREiiPj79jEMtB1il-rqp4GzVdBZrWr37TFzpaWHjBhMfCYzI8VEns-wuS19K8ceQcZMujBjkC42Umf8kYEBMzyZp3J-_sOktZYM4gVoL2na_eJk0AfFmSuApCdbsp8eVvRxeDAyyZFWBfasqgxckq5laucxoxOcLlGWjY8Npl0RlGNQnJwnZoHfF1BIRCYBM4AUrWtD3ijhv2I22yqG4q9sqjP3QlYv2l2NW-97KILrc03Bcy_BtPWTiAIgdQ-Th9unSCfTql/4tw/wXe2fSVLSDOMWXg7WnqhKg/h5/h001.OZRtOT_Dn0zQYy41g1Ra3tP90bY0b3O5J7AzoGM0deY)

The Iran ConflictCENTCOM SAYS IT DESTROYED FIVE IRANIAN TANKERS AFTER MISSILES TARGETED A U.S. WARSHIPWhat's Happening
* U.S. Central Command said it destroyed **five Iranian crude oil carriers** on Tuesday, after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles on two occasions over two days.
* CENTCOM named the vessels in its statement: the "IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Kaviz, M/T Charminar, M/T Horizon 1, and M/T Riesco in the Gulf of Oman as well as M/T Derya near Kharg Island."
* CENTCOM said American forces "directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable."
* CENTCOM said the warship **evaded the attacks** and continued to patrol regional waters. Every operational detail here comes from CENTCOM's own release and has not been independently verified.

The Situation
* Tuesday's operation follows a **Sept. 5 strike** in which CENTCOM said it destroyed three Iranian tankers after an earlier failed attack on U.S. naval ships. The two operations are separate events and are easily conflated.
* CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said after the earlier strike: "Let the message to the IRGC be clear... If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours."
* The IRGC said, through Iran's semi-official Fars news agency, that **two American warships were attacked and damaged**. That directly contradicts CENTCOM's account that the warship evaded the attacks and that no American personnel were harmed. Neither version has been independently confirmed.
* No casualties from Tuesday's strikes were reported in CENTCOM's statement or in the Washington Examiner's account, which said crews were ordered off the vessels first. Whether the crews reached safety is not addressed in either.

The PerspectiveWarning a crew off a ship before you sink it is the mark of a disciplined military, and it is worth saying plainly that American sailors were shot at twice this week and came home. The strategy behind it is coherent: hit the export revenue that funds the missiles rather than the cities that house the people. But a campaign measured in hulls destroyed needs an endpoint stated in public, and it does not have one yet. Tehran's claim that it damaged two U.S. warships is almost certainly propaganda; it is also a reminder that both sides are now narrating this war to their own citizens, and that the tanker count is climbing while the diplomatic track is nowhere in sight.[Read the full story at the Washington Examiner](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_F0KAElx4yVoiF03sTMUTyUT70T3bUtUddhBUBTd1H3EZm9ldZLAr9BvSYWWoxi9NgNnACxKy1IFhWHPZ9s0fYytxhea4UZJQWm-wcp95rzEDgGSBCe2ouAB52YY-sXfiZQjLXkAkLOdkdYRqHt6z7ksQnZB8M_YDSqbRlTnxFcie7TmU6Fttir0vEOO_V8dSYlIpUgpFxylkC1lOYVoYaIeGUSVDS3-gUsqsgBKdH5hw2COTOymDs3fChnBk1D8hOiJn-Ws-cqlSm8OQruxzBqS6yikccIIklaXPp1vvam-jmh26JO49TxBbMmLMIJxoBYK4whtPus4_jMMhYKlqZ3QG48H0SsRyLV2d1ILPgah/4tw/wXe2fSVLSDOMWXg7WnqhKg/h6/h001.bBvUwlaMmWTsxyi39ooOSw_61WTmLle7UI73SSNTaKE)

TradeTRUMP MOVES TO BLOCK CANADIAN GOODS FROM A $50 BILLION FEDERAL CONTRACTING PROGRAMWhat's Happening
* Trump directed his administration Tuesday to begin blocking Canadian products from a federal contracting program the Washington Examiner described as worth **more than $50 billion annually**.
* He announced it in a **Truth Social post** , directing the General Services Administration, working with the U.S. trade representative, to "take all necessary steps" to remove Canadian products from the agency's multiple awards schedules.
* Trump said the block stands unless Canada provides "full and fair reciprocity" for American companies.
* The premise — that Canada has restricted U.S. firms from competing for Canadian contracts while Canadian companies keep access to American markets — is **Trump's claim** , and the Examiner's report describes it as such rather than confirming it.

The Situation
* The GSA's multiple award schedules are the government's standing catalogs of pre-negotiated contracts that federal agencies buy through, so this works through **procurement rather than tariffs**.
* The Examiner reported a companion measure in the same window: a U.S. ban on importing **Canadian alcohol, dairy products and some motorcycles** as a retaliatory move.
* The Examiner also reported that **Kansas Republicans have bucked Trump** over a threat to blacklist Canadian jets — a sign the friction runs inside his own party as well as across the border.
* The report did not specify an effective date, how existing contracts would be treated, or which product categories are affected first.

The PerspectiveReciprocity is the right principle. If Ottawa fences off its own procurement while Canadian firms bid freely on ours, then American taxpayers have been subsidizing a one-way street, and no one should have to apologize for closing it. The honest caveat is that procurement retaliation is paid for at home: agencies buying from a shorter list of vendors pay more, and it is the Kansas aircraft supplier and the American contractor with a cross-border supply chain who feel it before Ottawa does. That is why Kansas Republicans are objecting, and their objection is worth hearing rather than dismissing. Announce the reciprocity evidence, name the deadline, and this is a strong hand. RedistrictingKAVANAUGH DENIES MISSOURI'S BID TO REVIVE ITS NEW CONGRESSIONAL MAP FOR NOVEMBERWhat's Happening
* The Supreme Court on Tuesday **denied Missouri officials' bid** to reinstate a new congressional map for the November election.
* **Justice Brett Kavanaugh** , the justice assigned to handle emergency petitions from Missouri, denied the emergency application and declined to elaborate on his reasoning.
* The order leaves the Missouri Supreme Court's ruling in place, reinstating the congressional map **used in the 2022 and 2024 elections**.
* The new map's fate now shifts to a **statewide ballot measure** put before Missouri voters.

The Situation
* Because Kavanaugh gave **no reasoning** , the order settles nothing about whether the new map is lawful. It means only that Missouri did not win emergency relief on this timeline.
* Missouri had filed an **earlier emergency application** in the same dispute, following the Missouri Supreme Court ruling it was trying to escape.
* Fox News reported on Sept. 5 that Missouri's attorney general had petitioned the Court to revive the map, which Fox described as **Trump-backed**.
* The practical effect: Missouri votes this November under lines drawn for the last two cycles, with the new map deferred to the voters rather than struck down on the merits.

The PerspectiveDrawing congressional lines is the legislature's job, and conservatives are right that unelected judges have too often treated map-drawing as their own prerogative. But there is a real principle at stake in this denial that cuts the other way: you cannot redraw the districts once the election machinery is already turning, and a one-line order from a Republican appointee that offers no reasoning is a fairly clear signal about timing rather than ideology. Missouri's map may well be perfectly lawful. It will now be decided by Missouri voters, which is not a defeat for self-government — it is self-government. The lesson for both parties is the same one the mail-ballot fight is teaching this month: do the structural work in an off year, or the calendar decides it for you.[Read the full story at the Washington Examiner](https://elink20c.newsletter.joinjustthetruth.com/ss/c/u001.SfPhhFqVdCCzAqIAosiI_F0KAElx4yVoiF03sTMUTyWFa1tWox1t_YE5rpY7L5b5wgDRXXPRAa8Tb9y-iJwX79nAKylJdUGe-n-GWW1x_LcJT7OC4_qOtSMkgJ6vhmr5LMOVlBLCNscrmZqAXz-lqDmFW3g_Fk3uFfcjTMXxBBKjU_6mG-KBVA1m5vaABOC-MgA7WBGI-BwRIo3UwlH6tLuy_gFvy-HuXfIAl08MMBoFQ_Mwxp3eOfBgQNkWh6bHmKgnIpI13-l5CnyRSyPhPDDqGrxgjT5BFe2TmdA_9I43p7VFFWYzw7NA0sWeIYbuuPJr3diiBV9gEe9xiejA2UTAiXKR5YfgAT1HOYDLhnVX1ssD7H6yvePcJWIi4SMF/4tw/wXe2fSVLSDOMWXg7WnqhKg/h8/h001.t61L-uXEUWPGPe5sBM0T7kDJZh7P9utdUTtw82xYPtU)
| ⚡ The Bottom LineFour stories, one question: does anyone in Washington still work on a deadline that isn't November? The party is nationalizing a midterm around one man because that is the fastest route to turnout, not because it is the safest. The Navy is sinking tankers on a schedule set by Tehran's missiles rather than by any stated objective. A $50 billion procurement block arrives by social media post without an effective date. And a congressional map dies not on its merits but on the calendar. Governing is the unglamorous work of building things that hold up after the votes are counted — and the side that remembers that in October is the side still standing in January. That's just the truth.
