It's just the truth. | Wednesday, September 9, 2026| Dallas: Trump On The Ballot ---|--- 6-minute read · 4 stories Lead Story · The 2026 MapREPUBLICANS OPEN FIRST MIDTERM CONVENTION AS TRUMP HEADLINES BOTH NIGHTSWhat's Happening The Republican National Committee's first-ever midterm convention opens Wednesday at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, a two-day event the party bills as the first of its kind in American political history. President Trump delivers Wednesday's keynote, tentatively set for 9 p.m. ET , and speaks again Thursday to close the convention after Vice President JD Vance's keynote — an unusual arrangement putting the president in primetime on both nights. RNC Chairman Joe Gruters told Fox News Digital: "We are putting the president on the ballot. That's exactly what we're doing with this midterm convention." Speaker Mike Johnson speaks Thursday evening. Senate Majority Leader John Thune is absent from the released speaker list ; a source told Fox News Digital he will be in Dallas anyway on a schedule that includes helping Senate candidates fundraise. That detail rests on an unnamed source. Senate candidates on the Wednesday program include Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and former RNC Chairman Michael Whatley of North Carolina. Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio and Rep. Mike Collins of Georgia are also slated to speak. The Situation Republicans are defending slim House and Senate majorities. Fox News reported the party goes into the fall facing persistent inflation, high gas prices tied to what it described as an unpopular war with Iran, and negative approval ratings for Trump — the article did not name a pollster, sample or date for those characterizations. Gruters, asked about Republicans skipping the event: "There's some people in tight races, they want to stay home." Secretary of State Marco Rubio has largely avoided campaigning for GOP candidates this cycle and is not expected in Dallas, according to the Washington Examiner. In New Hampshire on Tuesday, former Sen. John E. Sununu won the Republican Senate primary with 69.6% to former Massachusetts Sen. Scott Brown's 25.2% when the Associated Press called the race at 8 p.m. with about 15% of the vote counted. He faces Rep. Chris Pappas for the seat Sen. Jeanne Shaheen is vacating. DNC Chairman Ken Martin called the convention a "multi-million dollar party to celebrate Trump's failing presidency." The DNC attached no dollar figure to the claim, and Fox's report did not verify one. The PerspectiveGruters deserves credit for saying out loud what most party chairmen would bury in a memo: this is a referendum strategy, and Trump is the ballot question. It is a defensible bet, because the coalition that shows up for him does not reliably show up for a generic congressman in an off year. But a bet is not a plan, and the same nationalization that lifts turnout also hands every Democrat in a swing district a single target. Notice who is not coming to Dallas — the majority leader, the secretary of state, and, by Gruters' own admission, candidates in the tightest races. When the people closest to the fight quietly choose distance, that is data too. The Iran ConflictCENTCOM SAYS IT DESTROYED FIVE IRANIAN TANKERS AFTER MISSILES TARGETED A U.S. WARSHIPWhat's Happening U.S. Central Command said it destroyed five Iranian crude oil carriers on Tuesday, after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted a U.S. Navy warship with ballistic missiles on two occasions over two days. CENTCOM named the vessels in its statement: the "IRGC crude oil carriers M/T Kaviz, M/T Charminar, M/T Horizon 1, and M/T Riesco in the Gulf of Oman as well as M/T Derya near Kharg Island." CENTCOM said American forces "directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable." CENTCOM said the warship evaded the attacks and continued to patrol regional waters. Every operational detail here comes from CENTCOM's own release and has not been independently verified. The Situation Tuesday's operation follows a Sept. 5 strike in which CENTCOM said it destroyed three Iranian tankers after an earlier failed attack on U.S. naval ships. The two operations are separate events and are easily conflated. CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper said after the earlier strike: "Let the message to the IRGC be clear... If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours." The IRGC said, through Iran's semi-official Fars news agency, that two American warships were attacked and damaged. That directly contradicts CENTCOM's account that the warship evaded the attacks and that no American personnel were harmed. Neither version has been independently confirmed. No casualties from Tuesday's strikes were reported in CENTCOM's statement or in the Washington Examiner's account, which said crews were ordered off the vessels first. Whether the crews reached safety is not addressed in either. The PerspectiveWarning a crew off a ship before you sink it is the mark of a disciplined military, and it is worth saying plainly that American sailors were shot at twice this week and came home. The strategy behind it is coherent: hit the export revenue that funds the missiles rather than the cities that house the people. But a campaign measured in hulls destroyed needs an endpoint stated in public, and it does not have one yet. Tehran's claim that it damaged two U.S. warships is almost certainly propaganda; it is also a reminder that both sides are now narrating this war to their own citizens, and that the tanker count is climbing while the diplomatic track is nowhere in sight. TradeTRUMP MOVES TO BLOCK CANADIAN GOODS FROM A $50 BILLION FEDERAL CONTRACTING PROGRAMWhat's Happening Trump directed his administration Tuesday to begin blocking Canadian products from a federal contracting program the Washington Examiner described as worth more than $50 billion annually. He announced it in a Truth Social post , directing the General Services Administration, working with the U.S. trade representative, to "take all necessary steps" to remove Canadian products from the agency's multiple awards schedules. Trump said the block stands unless Canada provides "full and fair reciprocity" for American companies. The premise — that Canada has restricted U.S. firms from competing for Canadian contracts while Canadian companies keep access to American markets — is Trump's claim , and the Examiner's report describes it as such rather than confirming it. The Situation The GSA's multiple award schedules are the government's standing catalogs of pre-negotiated contracts that federal agencies buy through, so this works through procurement rather than tariffs. The Examiner reported a companion measure in the same window: a U.S. ban on importing Canadian alcohol, dairy products and some motorcycles as a retaliatory move. The Examiner also reported that Kansas Republicans have bucked Trump over a threat to blacklist Canadian jets — a sign the friction runs inside his own party as well as across the border. The report did not specify an effective date, how existing contracts would be treated, or which product categories are affected first. The PerspectiveReciprocity is the right principle. If Ottawa fences off its own procurement while Canadian firms bid freely on ours, then American taxpayers have been subsidizing a one-way street, and no one should have to apologize for closing it. The honest caveat is that procurement retaliation is paid for at home: agencies buying from a shorter list of vendors pay more, and it is the Kansas aircraft supplier and the American contractor with a cross-border supply chain who feel it before Ottawa does. That is why Kansas Republicans are objecting, and their objection is worth hearing rather than dismissing. Announce the reciprocity evidence, name the deadline, and this is a strong hand. Announce it on social media without either, and it reads as leverage in search of a strategy. RedistrictingKAVANAUGH DENIES MISSOURI'S BID TO REVIVE ITS NEW CONGRESSIONAL MAP FOR NOVEMBERWhat's Happening The Supreme Court on Tuesday denied Missouri officials' bid to reinstate a new congressional map for the November election. Justice Brett Kavanaugh , the justice assigned to handle emergency petitions from Missouri, denied the emergency application and declined to elaborate on his reasoning. The order leaves the Missouri Supreme Court's ruling in place, reinstating the congressional map used in the 2022 and 2024 elections. The new map's fate now shifts to a statewide ballot measure put before Missouri voters. The Situation Because Kavanaugh gave no reasoning , the order settles nothing about whether the new map is lawful. It means only that Missouri did not win emergency relief on this timeline. Missouri had filed an earlier emergency application in the same dispute, following the Missouri Supreme Court ruling it was trying to escape. Fox News reported on Sept. 5 that Missouri's attorney general had petitioned the Court to revive the map, which Fox described as Trump-backed. The practical effect: Missouri votes this November under lines drawn for the last two cycles, with the new map deferred to the voters rather than struck down on the merits. The PerspectiveDrawing congressional lines is the legislature's job, and conservatives are right that unelected judges have too often treated map-drawing as their own prerogative. But there is a real principle at stake in this denial that cuts the other way: you cannot redraw the districts once the election machinery is already turning, and a one-line order from a Republican appointee that offers no reasoning is a fairly clear signal about timing rather than ideology. Missouri's map may well be perfectly lawful. It will now be decided by Missouri voters, which is not a defeat for self-government — it is self-government. The lesson for both parties is the same one the mail-ballot fight is teaching this month: do the structural work in an off year, or the calendar decides it for you. | ⚡ The Bottom LineFour stories, one question: does anyone in Washington still work on a deadline that isn't November? The party is nationalizing a midterm around one man because that is the fastest route to turnout, not because it is the safest. The Navy is sinking tankers on a schedule set by Tehran's missiles rather than by any stated objective. A $50 billion procurement block arrives by social media post without an effective date. And a congressional map dies not on its merits but on the calendar. Governing is the unglamorous work of building things that hold up after the votes are counted — and the side that remembers that in October is the side still standing in January. That's just the truth. "The truth isn't conservative or liberal. name: OnePA Team
subject: RE: Private equity should not own our hospitals
body:
Delaware County learned what happens when private equity gets control of health care. Now we can stop it from happening somewhere else. | |
---
Peter, **A hospital is the difference between life and death.** It is where babies are born, where workers care for their neighbors, and where families turn during the worst moments of their lives. **Private equity firms should not get to buy these institutions, pull money out of them, and leave communities to deal with what remains.** Delaware County, Pennsylvania has already lived through the consequences. **Prospect Medical Holdings bought Crozer Health in 2016 while controlled by private equity firm Leonard Green & Partners. Crozer’s hospital properties were eventually sold, the system was burdened with more than $200 million in mortgage debt, and all 4 hospitals that once made up Crozer Health ultimately closed.** More than 3,000 health care workers lost their jobs. Delaware County lost its primary trauma center and only burn unit. A community of hundreds of thousands of people was left with far fewer places to turn to for care. **This is what corporate extraction looks like when the asset being stripped is a hospital.** And communities should not have to wait until another emergency room closes to demand something different. [**Send a message to your state legislators today demanding they pass a moratorium on private equity purchases of hospitals and protect community health care from corporate extraction.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm39TyzbXIpOoq2iqzYMm8391MGwtxxepouc_6AYtC3AHXNCmTeS9sx6zodarSteAyKVv2UthW1sdHG9_QsaMld60T5aNmxLxhzRPY8OAEWY0b5wZ8Db_eilpZ_XKrCoLVOY5qq3BrrOynlcBhBzjhVpIG21ex0WuowTEVBFETXv1u3MBaiy0-CJJPvLkzzQY4Yk4IzQY0GI06P3K5n9iG3QSYw9LxpfwnJV-nXXSJP471WG3jj0Fmxt3qWaza8acCdpQ5Wu-fBqS-LxK0qT91ZHO38Iz28xphV1PLYlYMebpOL-ctbkWSoGhga3TC_khyOZksYKcPx9fvNW7RYFd9wy4AlCUwWIFe-ISqPDO83VsJjPHgQmBRQhFirVEsYtCcHKqUoz-iWCai8mIIO6DKWZBLnm2dUJBRHp81gtMnWphvQkGw1uRVGiwY-FIAWCOnzw/4tw/UAm4qStFTjOHoO_82JztIg/h0/h001.DPmQMslweVN3NUfSNfAt9x3f1_xHue3iOBRY3L1S6Ag) body:

[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1320-fr-nd&t=2&akid=12326%2E400544%2EGFJk6M)
Hi friend, it's Deb Haaland. I am the daughter of Pueblo women, a single mother, a former small business owner, a former Congresswoman, and the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in U.S. history. **And thanks to your support, I am the official Democratic nominee for Governor of New Mexico.**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1320-fr-nd&t=3&akid=12326%2E400544%2EGFJk6M)
---
But no matter where I go and no matter what role I serve in, **I'm a proud Pueblo woman.** That's why I often wear my mocs or my ribbon skirt. These symbols remind me of how powerful traditional clothing is in sharing our heritage, and they remind me to honor the shoulders I stand on.

In a minute, I'm going to share some of the places I've rocked my ribbon skirt and mocs. [ _**But before I do, I have to ask:**_**_Will you please help fuel our fight to the general election by giving $5 to my campaign right now?_**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16526?refcode=jtk1320-fr-nd&t=4&akid=12326%2E400544%2EGFJk6M)
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1320-fr-nd&t=5&akid=12326%2E400544%2EGFJk6M)
---
| | On the day I was sworn in as Secretary of the Interior, I decided to wear my white moccasins and a handmade ribbon skirt adorned with butterflies, stars, and corn. No matter where I go, I am a proud Pueblo woman first — including at the Department of the Interior.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/8175?refcode=jtk1320-fr-nd&t=6&akid=12326%2E400544%2EGFJk6M)
---
| | On the first day of the White House Tribal Nations Summit in 2021, I wore my beaded moccasins in solidarity with our Indigenous people across the country. I am incredibly grateful that together, our administration made extraordinary accomplishments for Indian Country — enduring progress that would make our ancestors proud.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1320-fr-nd&t=7&akid=12326%2E400544%2EGFJk6M)
---
| | From my ancestral homelands here in New Mexico to the halls of Congress — and as I filed my candidate petition to add my name to New Mexico's ballot for Governor — I rock my ribbon skirt to honor my ancestors.
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1320-fr-nd&t=8&akid=12326%2E400544%2EGFJk6M)
---
Friend, history has shown us there’s nothing we can’t accomplish when we work together, which is why I’m counting on the support of people like you as we fight for a New Mexico that works for everyone.
This race is heating up, friend, and I need your help. **I am ready to fight for an education that gives every child the chance to dream big and reach their full potential here in New Mexico. Give families a raise by increasing the minimum wage and the child tax credit. Protect affordable healthcare for all New Mexicans who depend on it. And with less than two months to go until Election Day, we are one step closer to making this vision a reality.**

**_[Please, friend: Will you chip in $5 right now so we can build a strong campaign capable of winning this race and making history again?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16526?refcode=jtk1320-fr-nd&t=9&akid=12326%2E400544%2EGFJk6M)_**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16462?refcode=jtk1320-fr-nd&t=10&akid=12326%2E400544%2EGFJk6M)

I am so grateful for your support. Thank you for being by my side.

Be fierce,
Deb

The latest polling has us dead even. After all his money, after all his attacks, this race is a _toss-up._ That’s exactly where we need it with Election Day closing in.
So what’s Lombardo’s reaction to this? Dial up as many data center CEOs and MAGA billionaires as he can and hope they can save his flailing campaign.
Yes, we’re being outspent right now. Even knowing that, I still believe we have a real shot to flip this governor's seat blue in 2026. **But that’s only if we can keep pace with the special interest money pouring into Lombardo’s campaign right now.**
Every dollar we receive from folks like you helps us keep ads on the air and get our message in front of voters, proving that a people-powered campaign can beat a billionaire-backed one.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Abbott’s lead is gone
body:
This is the moment we’ve been working toward, Texas.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, look at this:
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260909_2_tiepoll.RN-MkK&refcode=em20260909-2065&amount=5&t=1&akid=2065%2E299639%2EfAzrFC)_Source: Univision/YouGov poll, 9/9/26_
In June, we were down 6 points. In August, down 1. Today, a brand-new Univision poll has this race TIED. 47-47.
_This is the moment we’ve been working toward._ It's the first poll of this campaign to show us dead even with Greg Abbott. But it's not the first to show us within striking distance. Seven other polls in the last month have had this race statistically tied. **Four of those had us within a single point.**
That's not a fluke. It's not simply a good week. It's a clear trend that’s been moving in one direction. [**Chip in right now to help us take the lead and take back Texas.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260909_2_tiepoll.RN-MkK&refcode=em20260909-2065&amount=5&t=2&akid=2065%2E299639%2EfAzrFC)
Here's what’s changed since the June poll showing us down 6: Texans are getting to know me. Every time voters learn more about who I am and what I’m fighting for, our numbers go up. And every time they take another look at the man who's run this state for twelve years, Abbott's poll numbers go down. His approval is underwater. His favorability is underwater.
I don’t need to tell you why. You’re living it. Rising grocery bills, rising premiums, rising property taxes. Data centers flooding our state. And a governor who’s spent over a decade protecting the people at the top instead of the Texans footing the bill.
**All the wind is at our backs. Ours is the campaign with all of the momentum. But we don’t have the resources to match it — not yet, not without your help.**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260909_2_tiepoll.RN-MkK&amount=5&refcode=em20260909-2065&t=21&akid=2065%2E299639%2EfAzrFC)
We are TIED with Greg Abbott, but he has nearly $70 million in the bank. He is going to spend every dollar of it to make sure Texans who are ready for change don't show up in November. A tie is not a lead. We have to go and take it for ourselves.
**[Can you chip in $5 right now to help us break this tie and finally defeat Greg Abbott in November?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260909_2_tiepoll.RN-MkK&refcode=em20260909-2065&amount=5&t=22&akid=2065%2E299639%2EfAzrFC)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260909_2_tiepoll.RN-MkK&amount=5&refcode=em20260909-2065&t=41&akid=2065%2E299639%2EfAzrFC)
It’s because of your support that we’ve erased Greg Abbott’s lead. This is a tied race: 47-47. We can finally win back Texas and make it work for regular Texans, but we need your support again today. Let’s make it happen.
Gina

[ Donate » ](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_gh_footer?refcode=em20260909-2&t=42&refcode2=2065_299639_fAzrFC&akid=2065%2E299639%2EfAzrFC)

| TO: PeterFROM: Speaker Mike JohnsonRE: Fate of the House Majority
FROM THE DESK OF SPEAKER MIKE JOHNSON:
I am writing to you directly because the fate of our House Majority rests on winning Virginia’s 2nd Congressional District.
Right now, Congresswoman Jen Kiggans is locked in one of the absolute toughest, most competitive re-election battles in the entire nation.
Far-Left Democrat Super PACs have officially placed VA-02 at the top of their target hit list. They are preparing to flood the district with MILLIONS of dollars in negative attack ads, dark-money smear campaigns, and paid activists to flip this seat BLUE.
Why are they targeting Jen? Because she is one of the most effective, commonsense conservative fighters we have in Washington. As a former Navy Helicopter Pilot, a Nurse Practitioner, and a dedicated Mother, Jen doesn't back down from a fight. She stands as a brick wall against the Left's radical agenda.
The Democrats know the math: If they take down Jen Kiggans, they can shatter our House Majority.
---
| [VIEW OUR STRATEGY TO DEFEND VA-02 >>](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)
---
We cannot sit on the sidelines and watch a veteran and proven leader get outspent by far-left Super PACs. Losing this seat is simply not an option if we want to protect our agenda and stop the Left in their tracks.
I have put together an aggressive tactical plan to counter the Democrats' money, defend Jen Kiggans, and keep Virginia-02 RED.
[Read the full campaign playbook here and see how we win this fight >>](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.-4EtDGI0QYg)
Peter, holding this seat will require immediate, aggressive action from top grassroots patriots like you. We need to ensure that Jen has all of the resources necessary to run a successful campaign. That means chipping in a few dollars now so that yard signs can be bought, TV ads can be paid for, and critical voters can be reached before November.
[Will you consider chipping in a few dollars to help fund one of the most crucial GOP battleground races of the year? ](https://trk.join.jenforcongress.)

I'm angry, Peter.

Families in Washington are already stretching their paychecks to cover groceries, housing, gas, and everything else that seems to cost more these days.

And now, _Donald Trump is choosing to make things even more expensive._ His administration just slapped a 50% tariff on billions of dollars' worth of goods coming from Canada—**one of our closest allies and one of Washington state's biggest trading partners.**

_And Canada is fighting back with tariffs of its own._

Let's be clear about who gets caught in the middle of this completely unnecessary trade war with our closest ally: American families, farmers, workers, and small businesses.

That's what makes me so **frustrated.**

This isn't some political game happening thousands of miles away. Here in Washington, our economy depends on trade and travel with Canada. When Trump recklessly picks a fight with one of our biggest trading partners, there are real consequences for the people I represent.

_It means higher costs._

_More uncertainty for small businesses._

_Farmers and exporters wondering what happens to their markets._

_And families paying the price at the checkout counter._

Peter, we **deserve** leaders who are actually trying to make life more affordable—not those who are hellbent on creating chaos and then asking working people to pick up the tab.

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: I was not popular when I got to Washington
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
When I got to Washington, I was not popular.
I had just unseated a very powerful guy in Washington — and at my first big meeting during orientation, he was presiding over the room.
Everyone knew him. I was new. I did not know anyone.
Then a congressman leaned over to me and said: "Man, it's such a shame that girl beat him." I looked back at him. I said: "You mean me?"
The blood drained from his face as he realized I was "_that girl._ " Not just because I won my race — but because I represented a threat to the typical D.C. power structure that existed back then and still exists now.
You see, I am proud of that moment. I did not get involved in politics because I wanted to be part of that system. I ran on the issues that matter to the working class and are too often ignored in Washington: Medicare for All, a living wage, stable housing, affordable childcare, and getting corporate money out of politics.
That is why I have never taken a dime from lobbyists or corporate PACs, and I never will.
And that is the power behind what this win meant in that room all those years ago: I did not do it alone.
Thousands of people like you knocked on doors, talked to their neighbors, and chipped in what they could. We out-organized them once. We will do it again, in my district and across the country.
[ If you can chip in $5 today, that is what it funds.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260909.wPrb2K&refcode=em20260909-12256-P_FND_EGR_GRM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12256%2E2526796%2EyFM1a9)

**[If you cannot donate, sign up to volunteer in the future and give your time instead.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/38163?t=23&akid=12256%2E2526796%2EyFM1a9)** Either way, it is good to have you here.
Pa’lante,
Alexandria

Friend, Earlier this year, Trump signed an executive order aimed at restricting who can receive a mail-in ballot and giving his administration unprecedented control over how the USPS handles them. Courts have blocked parts of it and the Supreme Court has let other parts move forward, but the legal fight is still playing out. This is a blatant attempt to make it harder for seniors, veterans, working parents, active-duty servicemembers, students, and rural voters to cast a ballot the way they always have. Millions of Americans vote by mail because it's convenient, secure, and it works. Every voter in NJ-09 deserves the same shot at making their voice heard, whether they vote at a polling place, drop off a ballot at a drop box, or mail it in from their home. name: David Hogg
subject: We’re not writing Florida off
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
If we’re serious about fighting for our future, we have to expand the battlefield.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260909-1&t=1&akid=3990%2E587540%2EWrpWVL)
Peter,
For years, Democrats have looked at Florida and just shrugged, writing it off completely. They say it’s a lost cause, that there’s no way we can gain ground in that kind of political landscape. Too red, too expensive, too far gone.
But listen: I have good reason to believe otherwise. Earlier this year, I spent several days in Florida meeting with prospective candidates and connecting with organizers, and what I saw was potential. Real, tangible potential.
Florida is red because the infrastructure to consistently compete isn’t there. Republicans invested for decades in school boards, county councils, state legislative seats, judicial races. They built that power from the ground up.
**That’s not luck or destiny, that’s strategy. And strategy can be beaten.**
Is it complicated, messy, even? Yes. But that’s why it matters so much, and why the kind of organizing we’re building there isn’t just important. It’s urgent.
Florida has become a testing ground for some of the most extreme and heinous policies in the country. Book bans pushed through school districts, attacks on LGBTQ+ kids, six week abortion bans, and more recently, cooperation agreements that have expanded ICE’s footprint within local law enforcement, and sweeping immigration raids that have torn families apart and led to thousands of arrests across immigrant communities. These policies are altering people’s everyday lives.
**Even in the face of all that, Florida is not lost, Peter. Not for us, not for the people we’re fighting for, and definitely not for the movement we’re building. It’s a challenge, yes, but the best opportunities always are.**
If we’re serious about building durable power, we can’t just defend the bluest states and hope for the best, we have to compete _everywhere all the time._
Florida is still a massive state with millions of persuadable voters. Rapidly changing suburbs, some of the largest youth populations in the country, and working class people who are tired of being used as political props instead of being heard. None of that disappears after a few tough election cycles.
This is the reality: If we abandon states, or ignore them altogether when it gets hard, we shrink the map of opportunity and limit what’s possible in our future.
Like I said, the right didn’t win Florida overnight. They invested, and they organized.
So will we.
Because giving up is not an option. We don’t win by chasing the easiest ground. We win by expanding the battlefield, and Florida has the potential to be one of the biggest pickup opportunities in the country if we’re willing to think long term.
**[I’m not giving up on the Sunshine State, and you shouldn’t either. Will you chip in $5 today to help us build lasting power in Florida and support the next generation of young, bold leaders in the state?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260909_1_florida.jpWBnj&refcode=em20260909-3990&amount=5&t=2&akid=3990%2E587540%2EWrpWVL)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

Senate Republicans recently announced that they have no plans to spend party money to help conservative Ken Paxton win the U.S. Senate race in Texas. "We in the Senate don't have the money budgeted for Texas. We need help from the president," said Senator John Kennedy (R-LA). Republican Leader John Thune (R-SD) later confirmed the plan to abandon Paxton financially and deflected responsibility to the president. "I'm hoping the White House will become engaged; Texas is an incredibly expensive state," Thune said. What makes this so infuriating is that the Senate GOP spent over $100 million attacking Ken Paxton in the Republican primary. **They had plenty of money to spend on Texas when they were trying to defeat a conservative, but when it comes to defeating a Marxist like James Talarico, they’ve got nothing.** You would think that since they spent so much against the party's eventual nominee, they would feel some obligation to help him now. **This race is competitive because they hurt Paxton in the primary. It should be on them, not President Trump, to clean up their mess. You break it, you own it.** Sadly, that's not going to happen. body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
Hi there,

We know we usually send you updates about fundraising deadlines, the $4
million Republicans spent in August to attack Jocelyn, and a whole bunch
of other things, but today we wanted to send you a different kind of
email.

It’s been a busy summer for our campaign. Jocelyn, Winnie, and the rest of
our team have been traveling across Michigan, meeting voters, listening to
families, and talking to Michiganders about what’s at stake in this
election.

So we thought we’d give you a peek into our camera roll and give you a
look at what we’ve been up to:

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/15815?t=1001&akid=1854%2E181023%2EfL0gg9 ][IMG]

We welcomed Winnie Brinks to the campaign as Jocelyn’s running mate & took
a couple selfies to commemorate the history-making moment!

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/15815?t=1002&akid=1854%2E181023%2EfL0gg9 ][IMG]

Celebrated the results of Primary Night. We have momentum on our side —
now it’s time to knock doors, make calls, and elect Democrats up and down
the ballot.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/15815?t=1003&akid=1854%2E181023%2EfL0gg9 ][IMG]

Spent an afternoon at UAW Local 600’s annual picnic, talking to
Michiganders and their families about an economy where everyone has the
opportunity to get ahead.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/15815?t=1004&akid=1854%2E181023%2EfL0gg9 ][IMG]

On Monday, The Blaze and The Washington Times picked up a [Daily Caller News Foundation investigation](https://dailycaller.com/2026/09/08/exclusive-mitch-mcconnell-wife-elaine-chao-ccp-appointments) built on translations of Chinese government and state-media records: Elaine Chao -- Labor Secretary under George W. Bush, Transportation Secretary under Donald Trump, wife of Mitch McConnell -- was named to at least four Chinese government positions since 2008, including three tied to arms of the United Front Work Department, the CCP's influence-and-access apparatus, plus an international advisory post with the municipal government of Wuhan.
According to [the reporting](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/sep/8/chinese-groups-named-elaine-chao-advisory-posts-overlapping-cabinet), she disclosed none of these positions at her January 2017 confirmation hearing, which by rule required her to list every outside post she had held _in the prior decade_. Her spokesman [strongly disputes](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/report-chao-held-china-posts-221645694.html) the story: she never held a position with a foreign government, never acted on its behalf, and the suggestion slights five decades of service to the United States.
Note the dates. The appointments date to 2008 and after. Her Transportation Cabinet tenure ran from 2017 to 2021. Those two facts lived on the same resume at the same time.

Harry Mason Reid Jr. was a United States senator from Nevada from 1987 to 2017. He led the Senate Democratic Caucus from 2005 to 2017 and was the Senate majority leader from 2007 to 2015. He died December 28, 2021
The official record, first
On New Year's Day 2015, at his Henderson, Nevada home, the outgoing Senate Majority Leader was mid-routine -- 250 sit-ups, yoga, and a heavy resistance band -- when the band snapped and threw him backward into a row of cabinets. The blow shattered bones around his right eye and broke four ribs; [his security detail rushed him to the hospital](https://www.idahostatesman.com/news/politics-government/article40660908.html). When the injuries surfaced on January 22, the photos were unforgettable: a man who'd run the Senate floor for eight years, his eye taped shut. The vision in his right eye [never came back](https://abcnews.com/Politics/harry-reid-lose-eyesight-exercise-injury/story?id=28120573).
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ce788e5d-f067-4179-87cd-505c1ba897bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Reid told the story and stuck to it. He [sued the band's manufacturer](https://www.npr.org/sections/thetwo-way/2015/10/08/446867225/sen-harry-reid-sues-makers-of-exercise-band-over-his-injuries), and in 2019 a jury ruled against him -- finding he'd [misused the device](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2019/apr/06/harry-reid-loses-case-exercise-band-blinded-him) -- which is as close to a courtroom verdict of "accident" as American litigation produces. That didn't stop the theories. Rush Limbaugh aired the "beaten by the mob" version in March 2015, and Reid was [asked about it on camera](https://joemiller.us/2015/04/senator-harry-reid-beat-up-by-the-mafia); right-wing media floated a fight with his brother -- a story a Las Vegas man later [admitted he fabricated](https://www.mediaite.com/online/man-claims-he-concoted-story-of-harry-reid-getting-beaten-up-to-test-media-gullibility) just to test how gullible partisan media had become. And Donald Trump, years later, [suggested publicly](https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/nation-politics/reid-lashes-out-at-trump-for-mocking-dems-injury) that the man resume exercising with the equipment that blinded him.
There is no evidence anyone hurt Harry Reid, and the speculation that did exist had nothing to do with China, but because the China ledger Reid carried in that exact window is genuinely remarkable -- and it ran in both directions.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b08be9cf-b8fe-4a52-8834-aaa01682869e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to take back control of Congress this November. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Eli Lily, Nvidia, Lockheed Martin, oh my!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY WARREN FOR SENATE**
body:
I’m so sick of Donald Trump’s corruption
#
I’m so sick of Donald Trump’s corruption.
I want to be focused entirely on the things that I know matter most to you: Lower prescription drug prices, better wages, and an economy that works for working people.
But it seems like every single day Trump is coming up with a new way to use the presidency to enrich himself rather than lower costs for you — and we need to call it out and fight back.
Between the frenzy of his $10 billion lawsuit against his own IRS, and the sham settlement that created a $1.8 billion slush fund to compensate January 6th insurrectionists, it was also reported that Trump has been astonishing Wall Street insiders with his trading activity.
In just the first three months of this year, Trump’s accounts made over 3,000 stock trades — roughly 60 trades every day the market was open.
He traded up to $680,000 in Eli Lilly while his administration shaped policies that could boost the company’s profits from its weight-loss drug.
He traded Nvidia — then approved the sale of advanced chips to China.
He bought stock in defense contractors like Lockheed Martin, General Dynamics, and Northrop Grumman — while the U.S. is in yet another war in the Middle East.
Trump is trading stocks in companies his administration impacts through policy. He's holding the stocks and pulling the levers that determine their value.
Looks like corruption. Plain and simple.
[**Bottom line: The president should not be able to own and trade stocks. Or the vice president. Or members of Congress. And we have a plan to ban this. If you believe presidents and politicians shouldn’t be allowed to own or trade stocks, add your name now.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22968?t=1&akid=1709%2E2118727%2E5HfYK8)
Every modern president before Trump has understood that holding individual stocks while running the country was a fundamental conflict of interest.
But truthfully, this isn't just a Trump problem.
Members of Congress have been doing a version of this for years.
Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are trading stocks in the very industries they regulate and the defense contractors they fund. Making suspicious trades right before major announcements. And facing little to no consequences.
I couldn’t think of a simpler way to restore the people’s trust in their government than banning stock trading by top government officials.
Let’s show that this plan has strong, public support: If you agree that presidents, vice presidents, and members of Congress should be banned from owning and trading stocks, add your name here.
Working families deserve a government focused on lowering costs and improving lives — not politicians treating public office like a personal investment strategy.
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth
**PAID FOR BY WARREN FOR SENATE**

When I'm writing thank-you notes to donors, I very intentionally place my American flag stamps upside down.

[](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=5ed27cb13eb2435d9a8b0bdc4bdcf59b&_e=b1Kr8YVYxPsNs6I-VdaCIJouL2B5JmFV1kG4RMJBXPvgJTg4xKAV4nN3FEZadUDtpj7B_7dqXlNaBOdeAgq21g0ntVvLvQmtxS2WsDegGvwf3GRy7QD2o1UVoOICVq2Tl-rvhHb-nm7JEffuwi2kJtrj7PMY70_7Os3Pdn3ra-qGRpKKgJUIXKaPdHHUc0pdy0fgau7TmWV1MZZ4RuIk_9q6xURPBR6aEz-zJipmHtYVCaauczD8PgEJsQXfXsjwbITDkKRHqDPi5LKIUcJIRUIujpu4BQVLND_M4m6wERtUXAiBC8R3BTGzGBbmoteONT4dkK4Q3fllfkbkbrK_K_akQ7XJcwIYktWKS6lDu5-RsuQyy4df85OJhsBsUGeq_kzAmbLvryCoS8CLae7A9TfB4DR_K8BOiU-D8isbPEXOv5ZgrY8IUC_lJynMI3MiDi7vqmvfLPWUssfq3y5MlBgm8GG7c8WP_lIcKCjR46U2t2lcUtK67F5M0QxcKZvx_fACt6oEhqXxfE3yxaLIKOIzbgTks27xjV4t2ksx-bEZOqaL5t-4FUV6CtXNqNTbbP53vZu6Mk6oSsMQ7_MIjoCMN_UhOnzCQ5NuL5AfpvKDSTg2p8JwedZDbNtC80T8)

I'm not sure if you're aware of this, but it symbolizes a "citizen in distress".

When the J6ers were in prison and wrote letters to supporters and anyone on the outside, we would place our stamps upside down to let them know how we were being treated, in case our messages were being censored.

**I continue to use it because it symbolizes how J6ers are still in distress. **

Even though we've been pardoned, many of us are still trying to rebuild from the ground up. There are some who are in need of jobs, reliable transportation, housing, help paying utilities, food, and support for their families.

That's why Stand in the Gap Foundation exists.

Through emergency financial assistance, practical resources, donated vehicles, and compassionate support, we give these men and women a second chance to rebuild their lives.

**Every dollar you give helps restore hope to a patriot working to regain stability and provide for his or her family.**

I have the privilege of standing beside American patriots who have paid a tremendous price for what they believed was their constitutional duty.

Many of them - fathers, mothers, veterans, Christians, and everyday working-class Americans - are still dealing with the legal and financial repercussions from that one day.

**At Stand in the Gap Foundation, our mission is deeply rooted in the conviction that legal forgiveness is only the beginning.**

To navigate the challenges of incarceration and reentry, we provide essential resources to J6ers and their families, such as -
* Legal support
* Emergency funding
* And our latest initiative, fighting judicial overreach

All of these services are committed to standing beside those facing persecution -- long after the verdict, the plea, or the pardon.

**So if you receive a thank-you note from me, and you see that American flag stamp turned upside down, I hope you 'll understand what it means.**

clean_body: Fellow Patriot, When I'm writing thank-you notes to donors, I very intentionally place my American flag stamps upside down. I'm not sure if you're aware of this, but it symbolizes a "citizen in distress". When the J6ers were in prison and wrote letters to supporters and anyone on the outside, we would place our stamps upside down to let them know how we were being treated, in case our messages were being censored. I continue to use it because it symbolizes how J6ers are still in distress. Even though we've been pardoned, many of us are still trying to rebuild from the ground up. There are some who are in need of jobs, reliable transportation, housing, help paying utilities, food, and support for their families. That's why Stand in the Gap Foundation exists. Through emergency financial assistance, practical resources, donated vehicles, and compassionate support, we give these men and women a second chance to rebuild their lives. Every dollar you give helps restore hope to a patriot working to regain stability and provide for his or her family. Will you ? I have the privilege of standing beside American patriots who have paid a tremendous price for what they believed was their constitutional duty. Many of them - fathers, mothers, veterans, Christians, and everyday working-class Americans - are still dealing with the legal and financial repercussions from that one day. At Stand in the Gap Foundation, our mission is deeply rooted in the conviction that legal forgiveness is only the beginning. To navigate the challenges of incarceration and reentry, we provide essential resources to J6ers and their families, such as - Legal support Emergency funding And our latest initiative, fighting judicial overreach All of these services are committed to standing beside those facing persecution -- long after the verdict, the plea, or the pardon. So if you receive a thank-you note from me, and you see that American flag stamp turned upside down, I hope you 'll understand what it means.** It is more than a symbol. It is a message. We are grateful for everything you have done. But we are still in distress, and we still need your help. Thank you, Shane Jenkins Founder and Executive Director of Stand in the Gap Stand In The Gap is registered as a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. All contributions are tax-deductible to the extent permitted by law. [](https://substack.com/redirect/d80c451d-61b3-462a-8e69-d9a21fcebd5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
They charged him with a felony for standing in front of a gate.
I want you to sit with that for a second. David Huerta, president of SEIU California, the largest labor union in the state, stood at the entrance of a downtown LA clothing wholesaler while federal agents conducted an immigration raid on the workers inside. He yelled at them. He told masked agents to take their masks off. He flipped them off. He sat down in front of a van. He was angry, and he made sure they knew it.
He was not violent. He did not touch anyone.
They arrested him anyway. And the arrest was not gentle. He ended up in the hospital with a head injury.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..fNwLanjl4_MPwPoOpIcljztvdjv_xSupSxtW6jZG6O8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214957193)
The next day, Donald Trump sent the National Guard to Los Angeles.
I'll be honest with you. I spent years inside the United States Capitol. I know something about how institutions use force to send a message. Sometimes the arrest is the point. It does not matter if it holds up in court. What matters is the footage of the handcuffs. What matters is that everyone watching understands what happens when you get in the way.
The charge they used was conspiracy to impede a federal officer. Civil War era. It had barely been touched before this administration started reaching for it. They were not interested in conviction. They were interested in the message.
Here is what they may not have fully understood about David Huerta. This was not a first offense. This was a life's work.
Under his leadership at SEIU, the union built immigrant integration programs. English classes for members. Hundreds of people became US citizens. He was advocating for comprehensive immigration reform, helping workers understand their rights and become their own advocates, long before Trump's Justice Department knew his name. The Obama White House recognized him for it. That record is archived, frozen in time, on a government website Trump cannot reach back and change.
His family were immigrants. He is a US citizen who spent his career standing up for people under pressure. That is the person they arrested. That is the person they charged with a felony.
He spent thirteen months under that charge. Thirteen months of court dates, bond conditions, the whole weight of a federal case hanging over him.
Last month, the charges were dismissed.
Huerta put out a statement. He said: "This means the government is finally admitting what we knew from day one and what was obvious to anyone who saw the videos. The charge against me was baseless and meant to intimidate anyone who dares to speak out or organize or demand justice. There was never a real case. Only an attempt to punish and silence me for exercising my constitutional rights."
He is right. And you can tell he is right by the way the Justice Department responded to the dismissal. Their statement said, and I am quoting directly, that "The Department of Justice does not arrest people for peacefully protesting." Then, in the same statement, they mentioned that Huerta had been compliant with his bond for thirteen months and had not engaged in the same behavior again.

That is their argument. He behaved himself, so everything worked out.
Look. I know that move. When you cannot defend the action, you pivot to the outcome. You act like the system corrected itself. But the system did not correct itself. The system dropped a case it knew it could not win in front of a jury.
That is the real reason. It was all on tape. Every one of these interactions is filmed. People are watching. And if you are going to put masked federal agents and a labor organizer in front of twelve ordinary Americans and ask them to say that man committed a felony, you are going to lose. This Justice Department knows it has been losing. The credibility is gone. They walked away from this one before the jury could take it from them.
What I cannot stop thinking about is the timing of all of this. Because what happened to David Huerta was not an isolated incident. This is a campaign. Mark Wayne Mullen has talked openly about deploying ICE to polling places on election day. Stop and think about what that means. This is not about prosecuting crimes. It is about making people afraid to show up. Afraid to be visible. Afraid to stand at a gate and say, these are my members, and I am not moving.
Courage is contagious. I believe that. I have seen it. And I have seen the other side of it too, the way fear moves through a crowd, the way one arrest can make a hundred people step back. That is what they are counting on.
David Huerta did not step back. They put him in the hospital, charged him with a Civil War felony, and watched him for thirteen months. He came out on the other side saying he has nothing to apologize for.
He doesn't.
-Harry

Hey Peter,
---
---
Yep, that’s incumbent Brad Knott from North Carolina's 13th Congressional District in the picture above, working at the delivery window at McDonald’s. And that’s also DJT in the other picture, working at a McDonald’s delivery window two years ago. Look, I used to work at McDonald’s in the summer of 1984, so I know a little bit about working at Mickey D's. It was hard work. I never made the delivery window. Instead, I took out the trash and cleaned the bathroom. There were perks, though: unlimited fries for lunch.Seriously though, I’m not sure I understand the message from our incumbent representative. Is he saying that he’s with the president? We knew that already. Data shows [he votes with the president about 99% of the time.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138894867/645534479/-385625403?id=547&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTgyNDQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjcyMmYwZDYtOTlhYy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZcKco__qzPX5xn4TTEC6vEPkasxOORaWBvRN-4B3WT4=&emci=7f71bb3f-8dac-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=6722f0d6-99ac-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=29273515) When the president’s policies, like the war on Iran, tariffs, etc., are driving our cost of living higher every day, it’s not a good thing. [1 in 5 Medicaid‐enrolled workers are restaurant workers.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138894868/645534480/-1368479320?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTgyNDQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjcyMmYwZDYtOTlhYy1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZcKco__qzPX5xn4TTEC6vEPkasxOORaWBvRN-4B3WT4=&emci=7f71bb3f-8dac-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=6722f0d6-99ac-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=29273515) Restaurants and other dining establishments are the top employer of SNAP recipients in many states. Among other large employers in NC, McDonald's ranks among the largest employers of individuals receiving SNAP benefits. For me, it would be hard to look folks in the eye if I had voted to cut access to Medicaid and SNAP benefits for millions, as Brad did. When I get elected, I’ll work to hold the administration accountable for the actions that are driving costs higher for each of us every day. I'll keep myself available, hold regular town halls, and show up... because listening to constituents will always inform the work I do as your representative.

National Republicans might be rethinking having their national convention in Dallas and supporting Greg Abbott because it is under his leadership that Texas currently has the most uninsured people and children, leads the nation in power shutoffs as prices skyrocket, and has seen schools close all across the state. That's not something most people want to throw their support behind.
Unlike Abbott, I remain committed to helping Texans achieve their version of the American Dream. That means quality schools for our kids, jobs that pay enough for families to buy a house and maybe take some vacation time too, access to healthcare, and a government you can trust. None of that has happened under twelve years of Abbott -- so why should we believe it will with another four years?
Greg Abbott has made it clear who he's willing to fight for -- his billionaire donors. I've made it just as clear who I'm fighting for: Texans.
And with Election Day around the corner, I need you fighting with me. So while Republicans gather for their convention to spew their lies, I want to remind you of a few things:
#### **1\. Greg Abbott okayed the largest data center in the world right here in Texas.**
This summer, I visited the site of Project Matador, which will be the largest data center in the world, right outside of Amarillo, Texas. I walked the five miles of the future site and met with members of the community who are rightfully worried about the future of their town.
Greg Abbott invited data centers to use Texas as their playground when he signed House Bill 2712 into law back in 2015 and gave hyperscale data centers _20-year tax breaks._
He promised to make Texas the "epicenter" of AI data centers, and then took millions from the companies and executives cashing in.
As a result of growing outrage about the excessive water use of data centers, Abbott finally signed a temporary moratorium, but that's only because he is afraid to lose. The only way Texans are actually protected is if real laws are passed by the state legislature.
Greg Abbott could call a special session of the Legislature to put real protections in place and give Texans a seat at the table to decide if and how data centers come into their communities. But he hasn't.
#### **2\. It took public outcry and an investigation of a state agency to force Greg Abbott to stop state funding for Flock cameras.**
Flock cameras started off as a means to provide extra security in local neighborhoods but are now used all across the country. Flock cameras are connected to a network of other cameras across the country. They store data on all of us, and there's hardly any oversight on how that data is used. Flock cameras bypass our legal system and put people at risk of being misidentified on a daily basis.
Faced with growing opposition to Flock cameras, Abbott finally paused state funding for them, but only after The Texas Tribune was set to publish a [report](https://substack.com/redirect/6dcd3ae3-8904-4521-88f0-b5312eede191?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) detailing how a state agency devoted a full $30 million to acquiring these cameras to give out to local police departments.
And to make matters worse, the Texas Department of Safety will keep operating its existing cameras despite growing concerns about privacy, oversight, the legality of Flock cameras, and whether or not they are making us safer. DPS' network of cameras was accessed 600,000 times in one month -- roughly once every four seconds.
That should concern all of us.
We deserve to know how these cameras are being used and what safeguards are in place.
#### **3\. Greg Abbott has yet to speak out about the 92 polling locations that were eliminated in Tarrant County just weeks before early voting starts.**
Tarrant County commissioners eliminated 92 Election Day voting sites -- nearly 30% of the voting locations available for the county's 1.3 million registered voters during the midterms -- significantly limiting access for voters across the region. **That 's voter suppression.**
Tarrant County's 1.3 million registered voters now have 92 fewer Election Day polling locations available to them, just weeks before early voting begins.
They have tried to justify their actions by citing budget cuts, but we know their goal was to make it harder for people to vote. It's not a coincidence that this decision has come months after voters in Tarrant County delivered one of the biggest upsets in recent Texas history, flipping the 9th State Senate District.
The reduction forces many voters to travel farther, wait in longer lines, and face additional barriers to casting a ballot in one of Texas' largest counties.
Every eligible Texan deserves equal, unobstructed access to the ballot box. As Governor, I will veto rigged maps and voter suppression measures so that every Texan's voice is heard.
#### **4\. Greg Abbott 's $1 billion school voucher scam is taking money out of Texas neighborhood schools.**
There can be no American Dream without strong public schools.
I first ran for office as a mom because state budget cuts were threatening to shut down my son's neighborhood school. Instead of letting politicians rob my child of an education, I immediately chose to fight. I organized parents, worked with my neighbors, built a community coalition and, thankfully, won that fight and became president of our local school board.
Under Abbott's tenure, over 150 schools have closed, and he passed his $1 billion voucher scam that's diverting funds out of our neighborhood schools. Thousands of great, experienced teachers have left the classroom, often as a result of high-stakes testing and burdensome workloads, and are being replaced by uncertified, first-time teachers.
I'm running for governor to change all of that. We need to get back to the basics and put good teachers at the front of the class and trust them to do what they've been trained to do.
As governor, I will end the era of high-stakes STAAR testing. I would roll back Abbott's voucher scheme that funnels your hard-earned taxpayer dollars into private academies, and I'd work to ensure that Texas educators are properly paid.
Our neighborhood schools are essential to the American Dream, but they cannot survive another four years of being starved of resources by Greg Abbott.
#### **5\. Greg Abbott refuses to collect the $11 billion in federal reimbursements we are owed as a state.**
Abbott spent more than $11 billion in state taxpayer dollars on border security. Congress passed a law that promised states would be reimbursed. Abbott praised the legislation but has yet to bring that money back to Texas. That's our money.
As governor, I'd do everything in my power to put money back into the pockets of everyday Texans because they need it. Our government shouldn't be hoarding our money, especially when electricity bills are up and people are struggling to pay for everyday necessities.
That money could be spent to fund the things we all care about, such as property-tax relief, schools, water infrastructure, health programs, and more.
In true Abbott fashion, he's failing to do what's best for Texans to stay in the good graces of Washington.
Enough is enough.
#### **6\. We have to constantly ask ourselves:**_**Is this the Texas that is by and for the people, or is this great state the billionaires ' world and the rest of us just live here?**_
I told you, there is a lot at stake this election. Abbott has failed Texans time and again, but it's up to us to fight for that change.
I know what version of Texas I'm fighting for -- the one where we all have a chance to achieve the American Dream. While the GOP is in Dallas likely lying about the damage Abbott and others like him have done to our state, I'm connecting with voters, making sure we all get a seat at the table.
I believe in Texas and am working to secure a future where all Texans can not just live, but thrive.
We're not done fighting yet.
-- Gina

[We’re calling on every Democrat to sign our letter DEMANDING the Postal Service obey the court order and protect vote-by-mail. Add your name before your spot expires at MIDNIGHT »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/129638?t=7&akid=28622%2E878179%2EqP4K_X) | [TELL THE USPS TO PROTECT MAIL-IN VOTING BY SIGNING THE LETTER HERE »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/129638?t=8&akid=28622%2E878179%2EqP4K_X)
---
TO: U.S. Postal Service
FROM: Willis
Subject: Please don’t cave to Trump.

Dear USPS,

**I am writing today to DEMAND that you stand up to Donald Trump and PROTECT vote-by-mail.**

Vote-by-mail has expanded voting access to millions of Americans in rural areas, serving overseas, and in marginalized communities.

Limiting access to states who do Trump’s bidding is UNDEMOCRATIC and straight up AUTHORITARIAN!

The Postal Service is a vital institution that has done so much good for our country — **so please don’t sacrifice everything you stand for now.**

[I’m signing this letter today to DEMAND you stand up to Trump and this disgusting attack on voting rights. Along with my signature, I’m chipping in $3 to the Voter Protection Project to ensure we flip the House this November and SAVE vote-by-mail »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/129638?t=9&akid=28622%2E878179%2EqP4K_X) | [SIGN THE LETTER ASAP: DEMAND USPS PROTECT MAIL-IN VOTING »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/129638?t=10&akid=28622%2E878179%2EqP4K_X)

We can’t let Trump get away with this,

Donald Trump just announced that he plans to put more money in the pockets of stay-at-home moms and destroy fraud all at the same time.

BREAKING: Trump admin drafting plan (pushed by JD Vance) to let married couples with one stay-at-home parent claim federal child care subsidies -- up to ~$9K/year -- via existing CCDF funds. No new law needed.
| 4:53 AM * Sep 6, 2026 * 554 Views3 Replies * 1 Repost * 7 Likes

There are just a few problems. In many states, those "low-income families" aren't actually that low-income, and this welfare is being used by illegal immigrants across the nation.
In California, for example, a family of four just has to make under $115,600 to qualify. It doesn't matter if you're a U.S. citizen; under current law, taxpayers will pay $9,000 for someone else to watch your kid.
Not only does this create a massive fraud problem, but it also incentivizes mothers to work outside the home, away from their children. It's clear which party designed that system, and it wasn't the one that believes in the nuclear family.
We've all heard what Nick Shirley discovered in Minnesota. The Trump administration admits this is part of why they want to change the policy.

# Who should be Trump's next White House Press Secretary?
White House Principal Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly has taken the lead as the most likely replacement for Karoline Leavitt, **[according to Kalshi trading markets](https://substack.com/redirect/b1a09fa6-4237-4356-94c6-201a3e20d717?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , with CNN conservative powerhouse Scott Jennings as a close second.

* * *
_**(Piece continues)**_
"Paying providers upfront based on paper enrollment instead of actual attendance invites abuse. In Minnesota, we've seen credible and widespread allegations of fraudulent daycare providers who were not caring for children at all," HHS Deputy Secretary Jim O'Neill said. "The reforms we are enacting will make fraud harder to perpetrate."
Trump's proposal is very simple: take that money from the Child Care and Development Fund, created by the Clinton administration, and give stay-at-home moms $9,000 a year.
To qualify, families would need to meet the following requirements:
* **Be married**
* **Have one spouse working at least 35 hours per week**
* **Have the other spouse stay home to care for the children**
* **Meet similar income requirements to the CCDF**

The spending doesn't go up, but it doesn't go down either... and that's where the proposal has drawn some criticism.
Republicans in favor of the bill argue this is clearly a net positive. The money was already being spent in a less favorable way, and now we can invest in families that prioritize being together.
Republicans against this bill argue that we shouldn't have this spending at all; that it's just another example of our bloated welfare system, and that fraud is entirely possible in this new program as well.

I'm a young parent. I had my first daughter at 23 and am expecting my second right now. My wife works from home, and truth be told... an extra $9,000 a year would make a huge difference. As a parent, I'll take the money. Why wouldn't I?
I'm also a fiscal conservative. I see that this is inflationary and ultimately may cost us more in the long run than it gives us. I think this is better than what we had before, but an even better policy would be eliminating large welfare programs altogether.
This proposal forces a real question: if the government is going to spend our money anyway, shouldn't it support the parents actually raising their own kids instead of subsidizing a broken system? I'm torn between the relief it brings young families like mine and the principle of cutting spending, but one thing is certain: the conversation around who we incentivize has finally shifted.

clean_body: Our movement to save lives and end genocide has built real cultural and political change, but we still have so much to do. | | | Friend, Thanks to our growing movement and ongoing public pressure, more anti-genocide candidates are running for office, and more Democrats (plus some Republicans!) are refusing AIPAC support. This summer, the majority of Democrats in Congress voted to end all yearly funding for Israel’s military. This would have been inconceivable just a few years ago. Multiple U.S. Representatives lost their AIPAC endorsements because of that vote, and replied that they didn’t want to be associated with AIPAC anyway. We’ve come so far culturally and politically, but we still have so much work to do. For example, while Israel’s government continues to violently ethnically cleanse Gaza, the West Bank, and Lebanon, the U.S. House of Representatives just passed a bill to cancel federal aid for universities that boycott for Palestinian rights. | When U.S. Senators come back to Washington, D.C. next week, they’ll consider recent House-passed bills, including the version of the annual military budget that includes a section to further integrate the U.S. and Israeli militaries. Most U.S. voters oppose this kind of military integration, including 80% of Democrats and over 70% of Independents. We urgently need to secure a Congress that reflects the majority of the American people, who know that Israel’s government is committing genocide and want to end U.S. aid to Israel’s military. Over a month ago, AIPAC had already spent at least $105 million in primary elections. Funded by Trump-supporting billionaires, AIPAC has spent a lot more in the past month of primary elections — and its super PAC is the top outside spender in this year’s midterm elections. In spite of this interference in Democratic primaries, many pro-Palestine congressional candidates won their primaries and will win in solidly blue districts this November. Now, together, we’re supporting anti-genocide candidates in swing states and districts, such as Angie Nixon in Florida and Abdul El-Sayed and Will Lawrence in Michigan. The next few months are vital. Together, we will keep fighting for freedom and liberation for all people. And we will keep pushing our government to invest in our communities’ needs, rather than spending trillions of taxpayer dollars on war crimes and genocide. Over the last few weeks, he and his MAGA allies have been relentlessly outspending us on TV ads. **Slowly but surely, we’ve been closing that gap. Peter, **Across the country, Democrats are heeding the people’s call for reform and proposing solutions to return the Supreme Court to one that actually serves the American people, not dark money and wealthy interests.** “There’s constant and building dismay about the increasingly appalling record of the court,” said Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, the co-sponsor of a Supreme Court term limits bill. “And I think the continuing interest in reform springs from continued dismay and concern about the court’s misbehavior.” 1 [**Make your voice heard and take our brief survey: tell us what reforms would restore**** _your_****confidence in our Supreme Court!**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38hPO8ZlJ6RdA0OLiB53pbc7tEFUZfg3XTQcCfN3lnfoX0tl1LSRMPCugvRXzgb7bocbETGx4GNguC50hfI-51Z5LLspdswPNAR564-gSmIuXOQvuvEUqJAAUrXAib6OhqR6XOJgvZqgn5uknTaWdZXJJIr-7es5XTFyvewyVM2L7NoOvRnPfAwIbiQFIVarDEfIZPtTOzec6_KeWjeS8wSxmSr6FW_aT8NJ98RpBDD4cS3ZK2SVrlBYnf8QKS9pjFAU9v84s1sUZ2Jlw2_RzNy1K3YiU28yhmHN8CZ2-OBCobF92dhMLv0le8g7_DaNJA/4tw/HFpwmFeoQBeM1ZPN_EP8dQ/h0/h001.Jex1twEwApP9KNUsD6wsPREilmghxoJKtlWmF9QJX3c) A group of Democratic senators is pushing for **18-year term limits for Supreme Court justices** , a system which would allow presidents to choose a new justice every two years, thereby maintaining a balanced bench. Other Democratic leaders have proposed **expanding the court, from 9 to 13 justices.** In July, Representative Hank Johnson from Georgia introduced a bill that would require federal judges and Supreme Court justices **to place certain financial assets in blind trusts** , in order to avoid conflicts of interest and restore American’s faith in the courts.2 In Johnson’s words, _“Americans deserve to know that officials in every branch of government—including the judiciary—are acting honorably and in the interest of the people, not their bank accounts.”_ Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg has proposed a major court overhaul that would **ideologically balance the court by expanding it to 15 seats** : five aligned with Democrats, five with Republicans, and a remaining five to be selected by the first ten justices. Another area of proposed reform calls for **transparency around the Supreme Court’s emergency or “shadow” docket**. The current Court has been criticized for using the shadow docket to make important rulings while offering little to no explanation for those decisions. [**The Supreme Court is meant to serve the American people, not special interests, so we want to know: what reforms do**** _you_****want to see in the Supreme Court? **Team:** Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections. Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office. **That's no longer the case.** Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a _regional processing facility_ , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts. **How does this impact vote-by-mail?** If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- _something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those_ \-- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, _a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day,_ making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control. **Of course, this was followed by the recent news that USPS won't deliver your ballot unless your state put your name on Trump's list** \-- usurping the Constitution and trying to take control of elections away from the states in order to suppress the vote. **[Team, Every voter needs to know about these massive changes. It's the only way you can be sure it's not being trucked to a regional facility and postmarked days after you mailed it. | | | | = Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections. Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office. That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts. How does this impact vote-by-mail? name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: $1 billion in dark money
disclaimer_text: paid for by the wealthy and powerful
body:
| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3015%2E4032634%2EiUBlK6)
---
Something is happening in our elections that deserves every voter's attention: **Dark money groups are spending record amounts of money to influence our elections.** A New York Times analysis found roughly $1 billion in anonymous political spending moving through the political system this year — and that number is almost certainly an underestimate. |
---

AIPAC, crypto billionaires, the AI industry — they're all dumping millions into race after race to handpick candidates who'll bend over backward for their bottom line.
The money moves through layers of nonprofits, super PACs, and committees. This lets wealthy special interests shape our elections from behind a curtain, leaving voters to make decisions without knowing who is pulling the strings.
In exchange for all that money comes time, access, and the corruption of our "representative" democracy.
It’s unsettling (to say the least) to think about what powerful interests might expect from candidates in return for the millions they’re pouring into their elections.
That's why it matters that we pay attention to how candidates choose to fund their campaigns. I say choose — because it is a deliberate, intentional decision. When we back candidates who reject corporate PAC money — who refuse to be bought — we send a message that power comes from ordinary people, not billionaires. And more importantly, it works:
**The 2026 primaries have given us countless examples that the many can beat the money.**
In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed won his Senate primary despite being dramatically outspent, with outside groups spending tens of millions of dollars to try to stop him. A week later, Peggy Flanagan won Minnesota's Senate primary after nearly $20 million was spent against her. In New York, Zohran Mamdani launched his candidacy virtually unknown and built a grassroots campaign that defeated former Gov. Andrew Cuomo in a record-spending election. And just this month, State Rep. Angie Nixon won Florida's Democratic primary for U.S. Senate, after being outspent 16 to 1.
These primaries and others like them proved that when people organize, show up, and build a campaign rooted in their communities, money isn't the only force that matters.
But we can't slow down now. Because September, October, and November are when the most spending and voter contact takes place. This is when corporate money floods the airwaves. This is when our opponents are making their final push.
Our democracy shouldn't be bought and paid for by the wealthy and powerful. It belongs to all of us. Getting big money out of politics is how we make that real.
That’s why right now, it's more important than ever that we keep building strength within this grassroots movement.
[**If you believe this is possible, and if you're able to, please pitch in to support our campaign today. With your support, we're proving that grassroots power can beat dark money — and building the political force needed to finally get it out of our elections for good.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3791?t=8&akid=3015%2E4032634%2EiUBlK6)

clean_body: | | | Our opponent, Michael Alfonso, really hates spending time in Wisconsin. Right now, Alfonso is in Dallas at the RNC “midterm convention” where, rumor has it, reps had to pay anywhere from $25K-$100K to attend. Almost no elected Republicans are there, it’s only those looking to kiss the ring of GOP party leaders. = = Think about that: Alfonso has been ducking the media and hard questions here at home while he’s being wined and dined by the national Republicans -- as people in our district can barely make ends meet. Gas prices and groceries are through the roof because of an unnecessary war and tariffs, and Michael Alfonso thinks it’s a great idea to rub elbows with the party leaders who got us here. Where you spend your time tells us what you care about. For Northern Wisconsin, we need an independent leader who will stand up to their party. Alfonso is scared of voters. Fred Clark is not. And we can gain real ground in the state House with enough outreach and elbow grease. Yes, Peter: we can flip Texas this November.
And it would make a huge difference in the fight for fair maps.
In Texas, the governor can veto new gerrymanders. We've endorsed Democracy Defender Gina Hinojosa in her tight race against Republican incumbent and notorious map manipulator Greg Abbott. He showed no hesitation in capitulating to Trump’s demands that Texas redraw its maps in 2025 to give the GOP another five seats. He’s got to go.
We’ve also endorsed 75 other Democracy Defenders running for the Texas State House, which helps draw congressional and state legislative maps.
Although Republicans currently hold an 88-62 majority in that chamber, we can narrow that margin, invest in the long-term fight to take back control, and make it that much harder for the GOP to pass extreme new gerrymanders.
**A small number of races in states like Texas will decide whether Republicans continue to hold — or expand — unchecked power over redistricting ahead of the 2031 post-census redraw. They’re desperate to win so they can continue to cheat. **

Patriot,

**September 10th marks one year since we lost Charlie Kirk.**

For an entire year, we’ve felt the absence of a man who dedicated his life to standing up for what he believed in and inspiring a generation of young Americans to get involved, speak up, and never be afraid to make their voices heard.

Charlie built a movement that reached college campuses and communities across the country. He traveled from campus to campus, had difficult conversations, challenged ideas, and encouraged young people to take an active role in our country's future.

But beyond his work and his public life, Charlie was a husband, a father, a friend, and someone who made a lasting impression on countless people.

**During the one-year anniversary of his passing, we want to remember Charlie not just for what he accomplished, but for the moments that made him who he was.**
